title: Josh Allen makes the case for grass fields everywhere
summary: Allen says he's had "numerous" turf burns that make it difficult to sleep.
full_text: ' When it comes to the issue of grass vs. turf (as well as any other player-related questions), it's important for the NFL's best players to add their voice to the cause. Bills quarterback Josh Allen, the NFL's MVP in 2024, has done so. "I think grass is healthier for our bodies," Allen said. "I'm to a point in my career now that when we practice inside on the artificial [surface], I can feel it the next day, and when we go out there [on grass], I feel great. I think any guy that was honest would tell you that's how they feel. So, one, I think it's healthier [as to] injury prevention. "I've gotten numerous, numerous burns on my legs from artificial turf, like, to the point where I can't sleep at night because it's bubbling over and, like, it's very painful. So I'm excited to not have to deal with that at home at least. I know we still probably will play games on the road that are turf, but if I can snap my fingers and make every field grass, that's what I would do, for sure." This year, Allen and the Bills will play on artificial turf in Week 1 (at Texans), Week 5 (at Rams), Week 9 (at Vikings), Week 10 (at Jets), and Week 13 (at Patriots). The issue of getting rug burns on fake grass is a problem. Injuries like that won't end up in the NFL's calculation of injury rates between grass and turf. But it's painful. And unsanitary, especially with the billions of toxic rubber pellets and all of the other stuff (spit, sweat, blood, vomit) that end up interspersed with the plastic. From a 2022 article published by the National Institutes of Health: "Numerous studies have shown that chemicals identified in artificial turf, including polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), phthalates, and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), are known carcinogens, neurotoxicants, mutagens, and endocrine disruptors. . . . [F]ew laboratory and epidemiology studies have been performed on the potential health impacts of artificial turf in athletes and communities, despite the abundance of evidence of carcinogens, neurotoxicants, mutagens, and endocrine disruptors in its components." In other words, it's obviously not healthy for humans to be exposed to the various components of a turf field. The compounds get in player abrasions, in their mouths, in their noses, in their eyes. It seems inevitable that, with further research, a study will emerge linking playing on artificial turf fields with one or more specific and serious long-term health risks. Until then, many NFL teams will opt for the fake stuff, because it's cheaper to install and maintain — and because it's easier to have non-football events in stadiums that use it. And all of them will hide behind the inherently misleading notion that the injury rate is identical on grass and turf.
author: Mike Florio

title: Josh Jacobs charged with two misdemeanors related to May arrest
summary: Jacobs could be suspended under the Personal Conduct Policy.
full_text: Packers running back Josh Jacobs has been formally charged with two misdemeanors related to his May arrest in Wisconsin. According to multiple reports, the Brown County District Attorney's Office has charged Jacobs with misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor criminal damage to property. Those were two of the five charges that Jacobs initially faced in the arrest , which came after a domestic disturbance call, but prosecutors are not moving forward with a felony charge of strangulation and suffocation or two other misdemeanors. Jacobs has been available to practice and play for the Packers since the arrest, but he could face discipline under the league's Personal Conduct Policy as a result of the arrest. General Manager Brian Gutekunst said at a press conference this week that the Packers have prepared for a possible suspension during the 2026 season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bill Belichick continues to say he's focused on UNC, not the NFL
summary: As should-be Hall of Fame head coach Bill Belichick prepares for his second season in college with an opening game in Ireland, he was asked if he ever sees himself returning to the NFL.
full_text: As should-be Hall of Fame head coach Bill Belichick prepares for his second season in college with an opening game in Ireland, he was asked if he ever sees himself returning to the NFL. "I'm focused on UNC right now absolutely ," Belichick said, via Brian Murphy of WRAL. "I've recruited these kids, two years with them, been with these guys. I want to help them. I had a great experience in the NFL, but I'm very happy at North Carolina. I'm excited to be there. Excited about the future of our program." The reality is that Belichick won't have a chance to return to the NFL unless someone wants him. Through three hiring cycles since the Patriots fired Belichick, he has had one interview. This year, with 10 openings, his name never came up. Last year, the Raiders and Tom Brady hired Pete Carroll without taking a serious look at Belichick. It's difficult if not impossible to imagine Belichick back in the NFL. No fan base is clamoring for him. No front office will want to work with him. No owner will become smitten with the notion that he'll turn an also-ran into a champion. The bigger question is whether he'll unlock a third season at North Carolina. If this season goes like last season for UNC, he may be SOL in 2027.
author: Mike Florio

title: 49ers sign DL Jah Joyner, put DL Victor Dimukeje on IR
summary: The 49ers made a change on their defensive line on Thursday.
full_text: The 49ers made a change on their defensive line on Thursday. They announced that they have signed Jah Joyner to their 90-man roster. Victor Dimukeje was placed on injured reserve in a corresponding move. Joyner signed with the Raiders after going undrafted out of Minnesota in 2025 and played in the UFL this year. He had 66 tackles, 14.5 sacks, nine passes defensed, four forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries in 42 college games. Dimukeje was a Cardinals fifth-round pick in 2021. He had 67 tackles, four sacks and two forced fumbles in 55 games with Arizona and he appeared in five games for the Giants last season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Dolphins trade Tutu Atwell back to Rams
summary: Wide receiver Tutu Atwell is heading back to Los Angeles.
full_text: Wide receiver Tutu Atwell is heading back to Los Angeles. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that the Dolphins have agreed to trade Atwell to the Rams. Atwell was a 2021 second-round pick of the NFC West club and he spent the last five seasons playing for head coach Sean McVay. The Rams will send running back Jarquez Hunter to Miami in exchange for Atwell. Atwell caught 105 passes for 1,535 yards and five touchdowns during his first stint with the Rams. He will join Davante Adams, Puka Nakua, Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield, and sixth-round pick CJ Daniels as options in the passing game for quarterback Matthew Stafford. Hunter was a 2025 fourth-round pick and played five games on special teams during his rookie season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jalen Milroe to start, play entire game on Friday vs. Chiefs
summary: Jalen Milroe will get plenty of playing time in Seattle's preseason finale.
full_text: ' Jalen Milroe will get plenty of playing time in Seattle's preseason finale. Head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters in his Thursday press conference that Milroe will start and play the entire game on Friday night against the Chiefs. Macdonald does not plan to play the starters. “I think it’s really great that he has an opportunity — just like the Green Bay [preseason] game last year — where you’re not subbing in, you’re not coming in at halftime,” Macdonald said. “You’re going through the whole process of starting a game and getting in rhythm, managing the situations — all those things we want from our quarterback. “So, excited to see him play. It’s a great opportunity.” So far this preseason, Milroe has completed 11-of-19 passes for 88 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions. He’s also rushed for 52 yards on six attempts. Macdonald mentioned Drew Lock will be ready to play if necessary. Additionally, recent free-agent signee Trevon Diggs is set to get some playing time at cornerback in the preseason finale. Kickoff between the Seahawks and Chiefs is slated for 8 p.m. ET on Friday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Robert Saleh: Wan'Dale Robinson being evaluated for concussion after "cheap" hit in Bears joint practice
summary: Titans head coach Robert Saleh gave an update on wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson after Robinson made an early exit from Thursday's joint practice with the Bears.
full_text: Titans head coach Robert Saleh gave an update on wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson after Robinson made an early exit from Thursday's joint practice with the Bears. Saleh said that Robinson is being evaluated for a concussion after taking a hit from Bears safety Xavier Woods during the session. The hit drew a response from Robinson's teammates on the field and from Saleh while he was at the podium for his press conference. Saleh called the hit by Woods "cheap." Woods played for the Titans last season and was released shortly after Saleh was hired this year. Robinson signed with the Titans as a free agent in March. Robinson will go into the concussion protocol if doctors find he suffered a concussion Thursday. That would keep him out for several days, but would leave ample time for him to be cleared before Week 1.
author: Josh Alper

title: Tommy Castellanos will play for Texas Tech after participating in NFL minicamp
summary: Although the Big 12 has now joined the Big Ten and SEC in banning anyone who has been an NFL player from returning to play college football, Texas Tech will be adding Tommy Castellanos to its roster.
full_text: ' Although the Big 12 has now joined the Big Ten and SEC in banning anyone who has been an NFL player from returning to play college football, Texas Tech will be adding Tommy Castellanos to its roster. Castellanos, at the time Florida State's quarterback, announced in December that he was entering the NFL draft, and after he went undrafted he was in rookie minicamp with the Dolphins. But Castellanos will apparently be allowed to play in the Big 12 because at the time he said he was entering the draft, he believed he was out of NCAA eligibility, and when he was in rookie minicamp he was there only on a tryout basis, and not on an NFL roster. Texas Tech will be Castellanos's fourth college team, having previously played at Florida State, Boston College and UCF. He is a college quarterback but was trying to make the NFL as a wide receiver. Castellanos got his NCAA eligibility back on Friday when a Kentucky judge granted him a temporary restraining order allowing him to play a fifth season of college football. Castellanos will join Will Hammond and Kirk Francis in the Texas Tech quarterback room. The quarterback situation at Texas Tech has been a major offseason storyline since Brendan Sorsby initially won a court ruling to get back his eligibility and play for Texas Tech, which sparked outrage in the college football world. Sorsby ultimately left college football, tried and failed to enter the NFL via the supplemental draft, and is now sitting out 2026 and hoping to get drafted in 2027.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Breaking down the new formula for safety-rule suspensions
summary: The NFL and NFL Players Association have adopted a new formula that calls for a one-game suspension when a player commits three violations of the same specific safety rule.
full_text: The NFL and NFL Players Association have adopted a new formula that calls for a one-game suspension when a player commits three violations of the same specific safety rule. The system potentially carries violations over from one year to the next, for the purposes of identifying the third offense as to five specific (hip-drop tackles, horse-collar tackles, launching, hits on defenseless players, and blindside blocks). All players enter the year with a clean slate, as to all on-field violations. (Previously, violations remained relevant to determining enhanced discipline for 34 regular-season games.) If a player has only one violation in a given season, he enters the next year with a clean slate. If a player has two violations in the same year, one violation carries over to the next season. If there is no violation in the next season, he resets to zero for the following year. (If he has one violation in the second season, he'll carry one violation into the third year.) If a player has three violations, he receives a one-game suspension. He'll be suspended for each additional violation that same year. He'll then carry two violations into the next year. This means that he remains on the brink of another suspension for the next full season after the season in which he was suspended. If he has no violations in the next season, he resets to zero for the following year. It's a little confusing, but the teams will surely be keeping close track of each player's status as to the five categories of infractions that can lead to a suspension. The media also will be keeping tabs on the various violations, so that it will be generally known if/when a player is facing a third strike — and a suspension. As noted last night, the new formula would have resulted in only one suspension in 2024 and one in 2025. And that was without the threat of a suspension. Ideally, those players who get to two violations of any of the five rules will know the consequences of a third one — and avoid committing it at all costs.
author: Mike Florio

title: Lions RB Isiah Pacheco dealing with a back injury
summary: Lions running back Isiah Pacheco has picked up another injury.
full_text: Lions running back Isiah Pacheco has picked up another injury. Pacheco sprained his MCL earlier this month and head coach Dan Campbell said at the time that the team thought Pacheco would be able to return for Week 1. On Thursday, Campbell said that Pacheco is now dealing with a back injury and that his status for the opener is unclear. "I can’t give you anything definitive," Campbell said at a press conference. Campbell did say that the knee is not "a concern" when it comes to Pacheco's availability. The Lions met with free agent Kareem Hunt earlier this week and any move to add options in the backfield could be a sign that they don't think Pacheco will be ready to go against the Saints.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jonnu Smith agrees to one-year deal with Packers
summary: The Packers are adding some depth to an offensive position.
full_text: The Packers are adding some depth to an offensive position. Tight end Jonnu Smith is signing with Green Bay on a one-year deal, according to Jordan Schultz of the Schultz Report. Smith, 31, spent last season with Pittsburgh, appearing in all 17 games. He caught 38 passes for 222 yards with two touchdowns. A third-round pick in 2017, Smith has appeared in 141 games with 91 starts for the Titans, Patriots, Falcons, Dolphins, and Steelers. He’s caught 345 passes for 3,52 yards with 30 touchdowns in his career. Smith has not missed a game since 2022, playing all 17 games in each of the last three seasons.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Seahawks, Leonard Williams agree to three-year, $90 million extension
summary: Williams was previously entering the last year of his contract.
full_text: ' The Seahawks are working to keep one of their defensive stars on the club into the future. Per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Seattle and defensive lineman Leonard Williams have agreed to a three-year extension. Rapoport notes the deal is worth $90 million. Williams, 32, was entering the last year of his contract with the Seahawks. He’s been with the club since midway through the 2023 season, playing 43 games. He’s recorded 22.0 sacks with 34 tackles for loss and 61 quarterback hits for Seattle. Last season, Williams tallied 7.0 sacks, nine TFLs, and 22 QB hits in the regular season. He then had a sack, a tackle for loss, and three QB hits in three postseason games as Seattle won Super Bowl LX. The No. 6 overall pick of the 2015 draft out of USC, Williams has recorded 61.5 career sacks with 93 TFLs and 223 QB hits for the Jets, Giants, and Seahawks.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Report: Browns to release WR Cedric Tillman
summary: Wide receiver Cedric Tillman's time with the Browns is coming to an end.
full_text: Wide receiver Cedric Tillman's time with the Browns is coming to an end. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that the Browns will release Tillman as they work to bring their roster down to the 53-man limit by Sunday afternoon's deadline. Tillman was a 2023 third-round pick in Cleveland. He has played in 38 games and made 19 starts during his time with the Browns. Tillman has 71 catches for 833 yards and five touchdowns over the course of his career. First-round pick KC Concepcion and second-rounder Denzel Boston join Jerry Jeudy, Isaiah Bond, and Tylan Wallace on the top rungs of the depth chart in Cleveland.
author: Josh Alper

title: Al Riveron returns to replay-review role with NFL
summary: Al Riveron is back.
full_text: ' Al Riveron is back. The NFL's former senior V.P. of officiating will return to the league office in 2026, as one of the three persons responsible for conducting replay reviews during games. Via Adam Schefter of ESPN, teams were informed on Wednesday that these individuals will handle the replay decisions : Riveron, Mark Butterworth, and Mike Annibale. More than a decade ago, the NFL centralized the replay function with the goal of ensuring that one standard will be applied at all times. Previously, the referees made the calls, and the 17 different white hats applied the clear-and-obvious standard inconsistently. The current system was specifically designed for former senior V.P. of officiating Dean Blandino. When Blandino left for Fox (as Blandino later said, the NFL doesn’t properly value the position), Riveron stepped into the role. It didn't go well. The tipping point came in 2019, when the league experimented for one season with replay review for calls and non-calls of offensive and defensive pass interference — and when the decisions were all over the place. Eventually, the league moved on from Riveron, who has spent the last four years with the ACC. Now, he and two others will be making replay rulings. The rulebook gives ultimate authority over replay review to the senior V.P. of officiating. In recent years, that position has been vacant. This has created confusion as to who is ultimately making the replay decisions. It's still not clear whether one specific person will be ultimately responsible for all replay-review decisions. The latest news suggests that it will be Riveron, Butterworth, or Annibale. Will they have final say over the games to which they are assigned? Will they even be assigned to specific games? Will someone in the league office have the ability to overrule their decisions? Thus, while the latest development answers one specific question, it invites other questions that the teams will surely be asking. There should be one person in the league office who is present for all games, and who has final say over all replay decisions. It should be the senior V.P. of officiating. Before that can happen, the NFL would have to, you know, give someone that title.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL ditches the Pro Bowl
summary: The league will instead name and honor an 88-player Pro Bowl team.
full_text: Say goodbye to the Pro Bowl. Jonathan Jones of The Athletic reports that the NFL has pulled the plug on the event, which has morphed in recent years from a game of two-hand-touch in full pads to a variety of non-football events capped by a game of flag football. Instead, the league will name a Pro Bowl team — consisting of 88 players — and have no Pro Bowl game or other competitive events. “All-star games, I think, for all leagues have been fraught for a long time, and they haven’t necessarily represented the very best premium of that sport for those players,” NFL executive V.P. Peter O’Reilly told Jones. “I think all leagues have struggled with that. We made the switch four years ago from the ‘tackle’ Pro Bowl to the flag game, and that was more strategic for us. In many ways, we saw a decrease in the replacement players. “But ultimately, the Pro Bowl, at its core, is about honoring the best of the best in that season, on the field, in real games. And the shift here is about shifting the focus from the game — which is ultimately where people’s attention goes, especially the replacement players tied to it — to the honor.” The players will be invited to L.A. for an in-person celebration in February, presumably during Super Bowl week. The NFL had a Pro Bowl, in some form, every year since 1951. The common habit of players ditching the game created often absurd outcomes via the process of replacing players. Last year, Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders made the AFC Pro Bowl roster as the sixth alternate. It's the right outcome, something we argued for once it became clear that there was no legitimate business reason for a player healthy enough to play another game in February to risk injury. Name the team, have a dinner, and move on. Finally, that's what the NFL will be doing.
author: Mike Florio

title: Colts activate Alec Pierce off PUP list
summary: The Colts are getting a key player back on the field.
full_text: The Colts are getting a key player back on the field. Per Mike Chappell of Fox 59 Indianapolis, Alec Pierce is being activated off of the physically unable to perform list on Thursday. Head coach Shane Steichen said earlier this week that Pierce was nearing his return . Pierce has been sidelined after undergoing offseason ankle surgery. The Colts signed Pierce to a four-year, $114 million deal in March to keep the young wideout with the club. He’s coming off his best season, having caught 47 passes for 1,003 yards with six touchdowns in 15 games in 2025. In his 64 career games, Pierce has recorded 157 receptions for 2,934 yards with 17 touchdowns.
author: Myles Simmons

title: New fine reimbursement system would have saved players $1.7 million annually in recent years
summary: For some violations, a 100-percent refund is available.
full_text: '' At a time when the NFL would love to do a comprehensive deal with the NFL Players Association on a new Collective Bargaining Agreement that would expand the regular season to 18 games (and that would allow up to 16 international games per season), the NFL and the NFLPA found a way to get another important piece of business done. The new system regarding the enforcement of player-safety rules allows for players to recover half, or all, of the fine money paid for a violation of on-field rules. On Wednesday, the NFLPA informed players that the new system would have resulted in an average total refund of roughly $1.7 million per year "in recent years." Here's how it works. For the five specific rules that trigger a suspension for three violations (hip-drop tackles, horse-collar tackles, launching, hits on defenseless players and blindside blocks), a player with only one violation in a given season gets 50 percent of the fine money back at the end of the year. While certain violations result in no refund (offenses against game officials, fighting, throwing a punch, forearm, or kick, and violent gestures), a single violation as to all other on-field rules ( e.g ., facemask) results in a 100-percent refund. In 2024 and 2025, roughly 50 players per year would have gotten a 50-percent refund, and roughly 200 players per year would have gotten a 100-percent refund. There's a very important caveat as to eligibility for a refund. The player must have appealed the fine in order to get the money. Therefore, all fines should be appealed — even if the player has no real basis for the appeal. Moving forward, that's the thing for all players and agents to remember. Every fine must be appealed. Then, potentially, all or half of the money will be refunded, even if the appeal fails.
author: Mike Florio

title: Steelers free up $18 million in cap space by restructuring DK Metcalf's contract
summary: The Steelers were dead last in the NFL in available salary cap space for the 2026 season.
full_text: The Steelers were dead last in the NFL in available salary cap space for the 2026 season. Now, they're not. Field Yates of ESPN reports that the Steelers have restructured the contract of wide receiver DK Metcalf, converting most of his $25 million base salary into a signing bonus, which creates almost $18 million in cap space that the team can use this year, and moves that money into future years' salary caps. For Metcalf, it's a simple restructuring that doesn't affect how much he gets paid this season. Prior to restructuring Metcalf's deal, the Steelers had very little money available under the salary cap with the offseason rules that count only the 51 highest-paid players on the 90-player roster toward the salary cap. Once the regular season starts, all players under contract count toward the salary cap — not just the 53 players on the active roster, but also players on injured reserve and the practice squad. That means the Steelers needed to make a move. Now, they have. With $18 million in additional cap space, the Steelers have some breathing room under the cap.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Eagles sign WR Tahj Washington
summary: The Eagles made a change to their wide receiver group ahead of Sunday's deadline to cut rosters to 90 players.
full_text: '' The Eagles made a change to their wide receiver group ahead of Sunday's deadline to cut rosters to 90 players. They announced that they have signed Tahj Washington to the active roster. Brandon Hayes was waived in a corresponding move. Washington was a 2024 seventh-round pick by the Dolphins and was with the team until being waived earlier this week. He appeared in six games last season and had three catches for 37 yards. Hayes signed with the Eagles three weeks ago. He was undrafted out of Southeastern Louisiana. DeVonta Smith, Makai Lemon, Dontayvion Wicks, Hollywood Brown, Elijah Moore, Darius Cooper, Britain Covey, Quez Watkins, Danny Gray, Samori Toure, and Erik Ezukanma are also on the roster at receiver.
author: Josh Alper

title: NFL bars first-year players who sign with college teams from returning in 2026
summary: Former NFL players who return to college will be free agents in 2027.
full_text: ' The college-to-NFL-to-college ping-pong game will not include a return to the NFL. Via multiple reports, NFL teams will be informed on Wednesday that players who return to college will not be permitted to return to the NFL during the 2026 season. Also, any player who goes from the NFL to college will not re-enter the draft. Instead, they will be free agents in 2027. Any rules in this regard presumably require a modification, or at least a clarification, of the Collective Bargaining Agreement. The CBA already addresses one specific wrinkle that could become relevant in 2027, when the NCAA's new five-year rule goes into effect. If a team drafts a player who returns to college, the team holds that player's rights in the same slot as of the year that his college eligibility expires. We floated that possibility last year, as Shedeur Sanders fell through the first four rounds of the draft. By next year, the theoretical move could become commonplace, if a player with a fifth year in his back pocket is drafted lower than expected and decides to make another year of NIL money before starting his NFL career.
author: Mike Florio

title: Free agent RB Miles Sanders was arrested for DUI in June
summary: Veteran running back Miles Sanders was arrested in Pennsylvania in June for driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs.
full_text: Veteran running back Miles Sanders was arrested in Pennsylvania in June for driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs. KDKA reports that court records show Sanders was arrested in Churchill Borough outside of Pittsburgh on June 8. Per the criminal complaint, an officer found Sanders "in and out of consciousness" while in the driver's seat of a car in the middle of the road. Sanders failed a field sobriety test and tested positive for alcohol on a breath test. Marijuana was also found in the car. "This is a private matter that has not even reached the preliminary hearing stage and there will be no further comment," Sanders's attorney Phil DiLucente said. Sanders is a free agent after playing for the Cowboys last season. He worked out for the Raiders in July.
author: Josh Alper

title: Roger Goodell says Illinois still has an opportunity to keep the Bears
summary: “We want to make sure that Arlington Heights and Illinois have an opportunity, as well as Indiana, to put their best foot forward," Goodell said.
full_text: Despite the Bears saying last month that they are moving forward with plans to build a new stadium in Indiana , NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell says Illinois is not out of the running. Goodell told reporters at Wednesday's owners' meeting that the former racetrack in Arlington Heights, Illinois, that the Bears purchased in 2023 could still be the team's next home. “There’s no specific timetable from my standpoint, other than we know that they are looking at the alternate groups, Indiana or Arlington Heights,” Goodell said, via Jarrett Bell of USA Today . “We want to make sure that Arlington Heights and Illinois have an opportunity , as well as Indiana, to put their best foot forward.” Goodell said he recently met with Illinois officials. Proposals for Illinois taxpayers to pay for infrastructure around the Bears' new stadium haven't gone anywhere, while Indiana is willing to spend tax money to attract the Bears. “I’m involved in a lot of stadium efforts,” Goodell said. “It’s not unusual for me to be involved in conversations with either public officials or others. Or our staff. There are important decisions, not just for the communities but for teams and the NFL. So these are important things for us.” Remaining in the city of Chicago, where the Bears have played for more than a century, does not appear to be an option. The question is whether the Bears will move to a Chicago suburb in Illinois or in Indiana. The Bears' stadium saga has been going on for years, and the team's recent comments seemed to suggest that Indiana would be the Bears' next home. Goodell sounds more willing to give Illinois time to come up with a deal to keep the Bears in the state.
author: Michael David Smith

title: NFL will have three sportsbook partners, no prediction market deals for 2026
summary: Look at them yo-yos, that's the way you do it.
full_text: Look at them yo-yos, that's the way you do it. The NFL has renewed its money-for-nothing relationship with the top two U.S. sportsbooks, to go along with a deal recently done with a relative newcomer to the industry. For 2026, DraftKings, FanDuel, and Fanatics will be the league's official sportsbook sponsors , via David Purdum of ESPN. The companies will have access to official, real-time data (allowing for live betting) and the right to use league and team marks and logos. The NFL, in return, just sits back and cashes the checks. For DraftKings and FanDuel, the sticking point had been the fee charged by Genius Sports for the data. That gap obviously has been bridged, either because the parties found a middle ground or the sportsbooks simply caved. The league also will have a say as to the types of bets that are offered, intelligence sharing, advocacy efforts ( i.e. , getting more states to legalize sports betting), and responsible gambling initiatives. Frankly, the most effective responsible gambling initiative would be to constantly remind gamblers that they can't win. (And that, if they somehow figure out a way to consistently win, they'll be cut off.) None of those companies became so rich and powerful because the business loses money. The house wins. It always wins. And the advertising needs to better reflect that. Instead, it contains just enough of a whiff of the notion that you can, and will, be the exception to the rule. (Until you get cut off.) That's where the NFL could do some real good for its fans who could develop a real addiction to gambling, if it ever chooses to do so. But the league has done a 180 from hating sports betting to loving it, because it's free money. While the league has tried to justify the cash grab by claiming that the relationships are necessary to the effort to enforce gambling rules as to players, that could be accomplished without turning it into a major revenue stream. Fortunately, the NFL has yet to try to turn prediction markets into a revenue stream. Purdum notes that the league will have no deals with Kalshi or Polymarket. Also, the sportsbook deals don't extend to the companies' burgeoning prediction-market operations. It nevertheless feels inevitable that the league will flip the switch on the financial firehose that will come from allowing prediction markets to align with the NFL. For now, the NFL will focus on funneling cash from sportsbooks. Despite the lingering risks to the game flowing from the legalization, and normalization, of sports betting. Before the Supreme Court opened the floodgates in 2018, the NFL banged the drum loudly about the potential impact of widespread sports betting on the perceived integrity of the game. Once the NFL realized how much money could be made from cozying up to the sportsbooks, the league has conveniently forgotten about the things that it said about the potential pitfalls of sports betting — even though the risk still looms that fans will wonder whether otherwise normal incidents of the game suggest that the fix is in.
author: Mike Florio

title: Lamar Jackson: Ja'Kobi Lane is like Odell Beckham Jr., DeAndre Hopkins with his hands
summary: Throughout training camp, reports out of Baltimore have indicated rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane could be a significant part of the Ravens' offense in the coming season.
full_text: Throughout training camp, reports out of Baltimore have indicated rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane could be a significant part of the Ravens' offense in the coming season. Reporters have noted how Lane seems to catch everything that comes in his direction, making impressive grab after impressive grab in practice. Quarterback Lamar Jackson was asked about the USC product in his Wednesday press conference and called Lane an "easy target." "Big guy — like 6-4, 6-5 — [he can] catch the ball with the best of them," Jackson said, via transcript from the team. "I told you, my comparison [is] like Odell Beckham Jr. and DeAndre Hopkins with the hands.” Those are some lofty comparisons, particularly for a rookie. We'll see if he can live up to them. A third-round pick in this year’s draft, Lane caught 43 passes for 525 yards with 12 touchdowns at USC in 2024 before catching 49 passes for 745 yards with four TDs in 2025.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Jayden Daniels admits Commanders had "not the best day" in joint practice with Ravens
summary: The Commanders and the Ravens had a joint practice today that reporters on the scene described as an ugly performance from the Commanders' offense.
full_text: The Commanders and the Ravens had a joint practice today that reporters on the scene described as an ugly performance from the Commanders' offense. Jayden Daniels was a little more charitable in his description of it, but admitted it wasn't good enough. Daniels said after practice that the offense could have been better, but also described it as a learning experience. "Not the best day that I thought we could have had, all-around, from myself to everybody else, but these are the opportunities we get to learn from," Daniels said. Multiple reporters at the practice described the Commanders' offensive line as getting dominated by the Ravens' defensive line, with the absence of Commanders center Nick Allegretti, who is out with a calf injury, causing particular problems for Washington. Daniels said he just has to do his best with the teammates available. "I'm out here with who's out here, at the end of the day," Daniels said. "At the end of the day, I'm just doing my job." Commanders fans will hope Daniels and his teammates can do their jobs better when the season starts.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Falcons OC Tommy Rees: We'll have open dialogue about our QB choice
summary: The Falcons' quarterback competition fully launched this week with Michael Penix's clearance for all phases of football work and the team will be under a time crunch to make their choice for Week 1.
full_text: ' The Falcons' quarterback competition fully launched this week with Michael Penix's clearance for all phases of football work and the team will be under a time crunch to make their choice for Week 1. Penix became the quarterback of the future in Atlanta when he was drafted in the first round in 2024, but his brief run as a starter as a rookie was followed by nine starts and a torn ACL last season. That led the team to bring in Tua Tagovailoa as a free agent and he handled the 11-on-11 work with the first team while Penix was waiting for the go-ahead from trainers. Tagovailoa's play didn't convince anyone he's clearly the best choice to open the season and offensive coordinator Tommy Rees said this week that he looks forward to hearing all opinions as the team figures out the best path. "We have a very good dialogue between all of us, so I am not real concerned with voices not being heard or not," Rees said, via the team's website. "There's been an open dialogue and a lot of mutual respect in terms of who we work with. Those conversations will take place and we will all say our part and we will move forward together with one decision." Rees also shared how he'll evaluate the two players given their imbalanced workload in the offseason and summer. "I think you look at the whole body of work, you certainly know where guys have been in their career," Rees said. "You know what they have done in real games, on a big stage. So, certainly, there are things you can draw back to, talk through and know that guys have handled things in the past. We're really trying to evaluate how they've handled [a new offensive install], what we have asked them to do and I have been pleased with the progression." Friday's preseason game will give the Falcons one more data point to consider before moving forward with their conversations about starting Penix or Tagovailoa.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jayden Daniels: I've said everything I needed to say about my LSU jersey number
summary: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels does not want to talk about his battle with LSU about the school not retiring his jersey number.
full_text: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels does not want to talk about his battle with LSU about the school not retiring his jersey number. Daniels' lawyer told LSU to cease using Daniels’ name, image and likeness because Daniels is upset that the No. 5 he wore on his jersey at LSU is now being worn by cornerback DJ Pickett. At the Commanders' practice on Wednesday, where many reporters who cover the Commanders were questioning him for the first time, Daniels was asked if he wants to say why he filed the cease-and-desist. "No, I posted a statement on Instagram and said everything I needed to say. So, appreciate y'all. Thank you," Daniels said, ending the press conference. In the statement he posted to Instagram two weeks ago, Daniels said, “I have been locked in on training camp and that’s been my number one focus. I have a lot of gratitude for my time at LSU and I’m proud of what my teammates and I accomplished there. Obviously there are issues to be worked out between my team and LSU and my hope is that it will get done privately. My sole personal focus is on Commanders’ football. I realize the business of football is unique and I trust this can all be resolved.” That statement may be all we hear from Daniels about his relationship with LSU, but it's clear that Daniels is not happy that the No. 5 jersey will be on the field this season, when he believes it should be on display to commemorate his career as a Heisman Trophy winner.

title: Renner's 2027 NFL Draft scouting series: Who's the No. 1 EDGE between Dylan Stewart and Colin Simmons?
summary: Stewart and Simmons could both sit out the 2026 season and still be first-round picks in April
full_text:
The top of this edge class has a chance to be special. Dylan Stewart vs. Colin Simmons could end up being Jadeveon Clowney vs. Khalil Mack for a new generation of draft fans.
Outside of those two, the 2027 class is loaded with prospects who look the part but relatively short on prospects who play the part. The good news is that this far out from the draft, the former is often more important than the latter. It will be a very fun class to track this fall for just that reason.
Positional rankings: IOL • S • LB • DT • TE • OT • RB • CB • EDGE • WR • QB
Note: ⭐️ represents each player's 247Sports star rating as a high school recruit
Dylan Stewart's absurd physical talent has been on display since the first time he stepped on a college field.
how in the world is this is a true freshman pic.twitter.com/6Jq9qghsbQ
His combination of bend and burst looks closer to that of a cornerback than a 6-foot-5, 250-pound defensive end. He's the closest physical specimen to Myles Garrett since Garrett came out of Texas A&M in 2017.
While Stewart's strength hasn't progressed the same way Garrett's did after his freshman year -- Garrett gained 30 pounds at Texas A&M to reach 270 by his junior year, while Stewart is listed at 250 -- even 90% of Garrett is still an elite edge rusher in the NFL . He doesn't need to show any more to be a top-10 pick.
Colin Simmons is the modern prototype speed rusher, the kind who can get by in the 240s because he's so athletic and overtly physical. With how much defenses use stunts and slanting blitzes, those kinds of athletes are incredibly valuable. If you're slow out of your stance against him, you're toast. He's yet another prospect who doesn't have to play another down to go top 10.
Texas EDGE Collin Simmons has insane traits for a true junior pic.twitter.com/CnxMAgsc0F
There were a couple of defensive linemen on Clemson last year who entered the season with a lot more hype, but by the end of the year, no one was more effective than Will Heldt .
At 6-foot-7 and 260 pounds, it's hard not to see some pre-breakout Aidan Hutchinson when watching Heldt's tape. That's because at that size, he doesn't so much win with pure power but rather bend and agility. He's got a whirlwind spin move that he deploys in obvious passing situations that will be even more of a weapon in a defense without so many schemed rushes.
I'd like him to get better as a pure bull rusher, but as someone who's relatively young for a senior (he turned 21 in February), there's still time for improvement in that regard.
I got to Sahir West 's tape late in the summer and most certainly did not expect a James Madison transfer to UCLA to be one of the most physically impressive defensive ends in the class. At 6-foot-3 and 279 pounds,
Sahir West can move. Obviously, you'd expect an end that big to win with power, and he does, but there are a handful of times a game when he leaves offensive linemen grasping at air.
New UCLA DE Sahir West is my pick for biggest breakout prospect this year. Jumbo DE (279 pounds) w/exceptional bend and agility combined w/ violent hands. Didn't get many pure pass-rush opportunities in JMU's defense last year, but all the tools and still only in 3rd year pic.twitter.com/7UIXCvw6iz
He didn't even get many true pass-rushing opportunities last season, as James Madison heavily featured three-man rushes, and he still notched seven sacks. If he can pin his ears back more this fall, his production should soar.
Don't let Tennessee's heavy edge rotation, which kept Jordan Ross largely under wraps last season with just 249 snaps, make you think Ross is a normal backup. He's a former five-star with an ideal edge-rusher frame, bend and explosiveness. It's all there physically for him to end up a first-rounder.
You see flashes of everything, but nothing is particularly consistent. That's not too concerning, though, for an inexperienced redshirt freshman. It's really just a matter of reps and block awareness at this point. If he gets those at LSU, he'll fly up boards.
Jordan Ross (6’5 245) LSU ✅ Reportedly has an 80+” wingspan ✅ 9.9% stop rate during 2025 ✅ 8.3% career missed tackle rate ✅ Pursuit speed and athleticism pic.twitter.com/iuRyyuiOiz
Yhonzae Pierre 's scouting report is eerily similar to the man above him on this list except he's just a year older. Pierre barely saw the field his first two seasons at Alabama before a breakout eight-sack campaign last fall.
Yhonzae Pierre has Day 1 talent. Multiple prominent programs offered him a huge bag to leave, but he elected to finish his career in Tuscaloosa. Probably going to be my top player in the roster rankings. pic.twitter.com/U7bNv2wPj9
The only thing standing between him and a first-round selection is consistency in his power. He has the physical tools to be a bull rusher and hard edge-setter, but he ran hot and cold in both regards on tape.
Matayo Uiagalelei is a former five-star who started as a true freshman for Oregon in 2023 and has gotten steadily better ever since. He's never quite made the leap to dominance, though, which may be due to the fact that he's young for his grade and only turned 21 in July. He's a power player who wins through opponents' chests.
Matayo Uiagalelei with a beautiful bull rush for the strip sack pic.twitter.com/oaTW921Z91
While every other prospect in this top 10 has a relatively ideal frame for the edge position in some way, Clev Lubin decidedly does not. He's got a squatty build for an edge with shorter arms and a bit of an awkward gait.
When he fires off the line to rush the passer, though, it's like someone strapped NOS to his back. Add a relentless motor, and it's easy to see him still working out in the league despite not being the prototype.
Clev Lubin got the better of both Miami tackles who went in the top 100 of the NFL Draft Lubin should be well gone inside the top 50 next year pic.twitter.com/ENzx8mw6rF
It's rare to describe an Ohio State defensive lineman as a project with legendary line coach Larry Johnson, yet that's where I see Kenyatta Jackson Jr . in his development. That's not terribly encouraging for a player heading into his fifth year, but Jackson has traits that are going to be hard to give up on -- especially his play strength.
He'd line up as a 3-technique in bear fronts last year and stack-and-shed guards with ease. That kind of ability will at least give him a high floor against the run at the next level.
Kenyatta Jackson will return to Ohio State for his final season of eligibility Key piece for the 2026 defensive line pic.twitter.com/LSp6clvMMR
This is a tall top 10, and Boubacar Traore fits right into that mix at 6-foot-5. He looks the part coming off the bus, and his high-end flashes do as well. He came back from a torn ACL in 2024 to be Notre Dame's best pass rusher last year.
I just wish he played with more active hands, as he has a lot of rushes where I'm not sure what he's even trying to do.
This is advanced quarterback hunting from Boubacar Traore. The set-up, the spin move on projected first-round OT Francis Mauigoa and the speed to chase down Beck are all elite. Next step for Traore is to do it consistently. pic.twitter.com/g2IYfdwP0t
Note: These aren't necessarily the next three players in my rankings, but rather three prospects who caught my eye for one reason or another.
When watching tape of Chris Cole and Quintavius Johnson , former Georgia first-rounder Jalon Walker came to mind for both. With Cole, it's the role he played last year as an off-ball/on-ball hybrid that was similar to Walker's in 2024, and I could easily see Cole making a similar transition to the edge. Truthfully, his body type is even more suited for it than Walker's.
Chris Cole will be a 10.0 sack player at some point. Not a wasted step one. pic.twitter.com/d9QIG0dO4B
With Johnson, it's the overt physicality that Walker played with. He's a grown man in the run game, even if his pass-rushing bag is a work in progress.
Teitum Tuioti may not have the prototypical…

title: NFL trade candidates for cutdown day, plus Pro Bowl gets canceled and ranking every roster 1-32
summary: Here's everything you need to know about the NFL for Aug. 27
full_text:
Hello football friends, and welcome to the Thursday edition of the Pick Six newsletter!
Today is the start of what should be a wild weekend in the NFL , so buckle up. The final week of the preseason is here and it starts tonight with four games. We also have 10 games on Friday and two games on Saturday, but you won't be getting a breather after that, because Sunday is cut day. That's right, cut day is happening on a Sunday.
Over the past few years, final cuts have been held on the first Tuesday after the final week of the preseason, but this year, all 32 teams will have to trim their roster down to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday. So not only are we getting 16 games this weekend, but we're also going to see nearly 1,200 players get released.
Before we get to cut day, though, we have a lot to cover today, starting with the fact that the Pro Bowl has been CANCELED. I will mostly miss the Pro Bowl because it gave us my favorite sideline interview of all time: Back in 2003, Peyton Manning famously called Mike Vanderjagt an "Idiot kicker" (You can see the interview here ). Alright, that's enough of that, let's get to the rundown.
As always, here's your daily reminder to tell all your friends to sign up for the newsletter. To get them signed up, all you have to do is click here .
The NFL owners don't usually hold a league meeting in August, but they added one to the schedule this year so that they could formally approve Vinod Khosla as the new owner of the Seattle Seahawks . That was supposed to be the biggest announcement to come from Wednesday's meeting, but then things got a little crazy.
The NFL ended up making several big announcements yesterday and we're going to cover all of them below.
In other news, Goodell said that the arrest of 49ers owner Jed York is currently under review by the league. "Yes, it's being reviewed under the personal conduct policy," Goodell said of the arrest . "We'll do that and when there's something to be reported, we'll talk."
Oh, and the owners did approve Khosla's $9.612 billion purchase of the team, but that was mostly an afterthought after everything else that happened yesterday.
It's been a busy week for Tyler Sullivan and Jordan Dajani, and I know that, because the two of them decided to sift through all 32 rosters in the NFL so that they could rank them from best to worst. Not only did they rank each roster, but they listed one good thing, one bad thing and one question that needs to be answered for each team.
So who has the best roster in the NFL? Let's check out their top three.
This entire ranking was so big that we actually had to separate it into two stories. You can see the top half (1 through 16) of the ranking here and we've got the bottom half here (Spoiler alert: The Dolphins are at the bottom).
With NFL cut day coming up on Sunday, we'll likely see several trades go down between now and then. The reason we so many deals happen is two-fold: For one, any team that has a talented player who they're being forced to cut will shop him around so they can try and get some compensation for him. The other reason we see multiple trades in the lead up to cut day is because you'll have a situation where Team A is eyeing a player on Team B's roster. If Team B cuts the player, that player is subjected to waivers and he might get claimed before Team A can get him, so making a trade for the player makes more sense.
With that in mind, Bryan DeArdo came up with a list of several players who might be dealt between now and Sunday:
DeArdo included a total of 10 players on his list of trade candidates and if you want to know who might be on the move this weekend, be sure to check out this full story here .
With cut day coming up, we also decided to take a look at 20 big names that could be released this weekend. The list includes Odell Beckham Jr . and if you want to know who else is in danger of being released, you can find out here .
In less than two weeks, Pete Prisco is going to release his first Power Rankings of the season, but until then, we have to find other things to rank, so that's what we're going to do today. Zach Pereles ranked the NFL's eight divisions and you probably won't be surprised by the one that ended up coming out on top.
Let's check out the three most difficult divisions based on Zach's ranking.
1. NFC West. The NFC West went 29-15 against non-division opponents last year, the best mark in the NFL, and it went 4-1 against the NFC North, including playoffs. So, yes, while the Cardinals won't be very good this year, there might be three NFC West teams better than the best NFC North team.
2. NFC North. First off, let me get this out in the open for the fans of NFC North teams who won't like this (still very high) ranking: The NFC North is awesome. It is incredible that four teams, all with clear flaws, posted winning records last year. And it could be awesome again.  But, when comparing it to the only division ahead of it, I see more clear flaws from its legitimate playoff contenders.
3. AFC West. Someone other than the Chiefs finally won this division last year, with the Broncos ending Kansas City's nine-year run. With the Chargers also making the playoffs, the AFC West had two playoff teams for the fourth time in the last five years.  Expect that to become five times in six years.
If you want to see where the five other divisions landed in Zach's ranking, you'll have to check out his full story here .
Earlier this week, we unveiled our All-Breakout Team for the offensive side of the ball , and now, we're going to do the defensive side. We rounded up 13 NFL experts here at CBS Sports, and we all voted on the top breakout candidates for the 2026 season.
Here are several defensive players who we think you need to keep an eye on this season:
ALL-BREAKOUT TEAM EDGE: Abdul Carter (Giants) EDGE: Dallas Turner (Vikings) CB: Travis Hunter ( Jaguars ) CB: Nohl Williams (Chiefs) S: Malachi Starks ( Ravens ) S: Kevin Winston ( Titans )
To me, cornerback is probably the most interesting position here. After trading away Trent McDuffie and letting Jaylen Watson walk in free agency, the Chiefs don't have a lot of experience left at corner, so it would really help them if Williams ends up being good. And then, we have Hunter. After splitting time on both offense and defense last season, the Jaguars star is expected to play more defense this year and it will be interesting to see how that plays out for Jacksonville.
There are a total of 11 players on our All-Breakout Team and you can see the full roster here .
It's been a busy few days around the NFL, and since it's nearly impossible to keep track of everything, I put together a quick roundup for you.
author: John Breech

title: Patrick Mahomes' status for Week 1 is still up in the air: Why Chiefs QB isn't a lock to play vs. the Broncos
summary: Patrick Mahomes is still waiting for full medical clearance after a December knee injury, leaving Justin Fields in line to start if he is not ready for Week 1
full_text:
Patrick Mahomes has been on the field for all of training camp, but that doesn't necessarily mean that he's going to be on the field when the Kansas City Chiefs host the Denver Broncos on Monday night in Week 1.
Before Mahomes can suit up in the opener, he has to be cleared for game action, which hasn't happened yet. The Chiefs quarterback tore his ACL and LCL back in December , but he wasn't down for long. By the time spring rolled around, he was cleared to throw passes at OTAs , and when the Chiefs reported to training camp in late July, he was fully cleared to participate in practice. But as the calendar gets ready to turn to September, the Chiefs' medical staff still hasn't given him the OK to play just yet, as noted by ESPN .
The last hurdle that Mahomes still needs to overcome is that he has to actually be cleared to play in a game. Chiefs coach Andy Reid was asked about Mahomes' recovery this week and whether he thought his QB would be ready for the opener and he wasn't ready to committ to the two-time MVP as his starter.
"I'm literally taking it day by day. No predictions here on anything," Reid said of Mahomes possibly starting in Week 1. "If the doctors and trainers and everybody that are involved in this give him the OK, and most of all, if he feels like he can, then we'll address that when we get there."
That's not exactly an encouraging answer.
The Chiefs will be playing in their their final preseason game on Friday against the Seahawks and Mahomes won't be suiting up, which means that for the first time in his 10-year career, he won't be be taking a single preseason snap. Mahomes wanted to play in the second preseason game , but the Chiefs held him out. On Monday, Reid was directly asked if Mahomes was held out because he hadn't been fully cleared.
"Probably not cleared enough," the Chiefs coach said.
With just 18 days to go until the opener, it seems like Mahomes' status for the game is still genuinely up in the air.
After tearing his ligaments on Dec. 14, Mahomes immediately underwent surgery the next day , and he did that because he wanted to be back on the field as soon as possible. Mahomes was told that it would take about nine months for him to rehab, and coincidentally, Kansas City's opener is being played almost nine months to the day that the injury happened.
"It's nine months, it's the amount of time [doctors] said from the beginning, that if I did everything the right way, I would be ready to play Week 1," Mahomes said this week, via ESPN . "I'm someone that, if you put [a goal] out in front of me, I want to go out and get it and maximize every single opportunity, every rep in the weight room, every hour that I can spend in the building to get my body right."
Mahomes has been targeting a Week 1 return since the day he underwent surgery, and as far as he's concerned, nothing has changed.
"This has always been the plan," Mahomes said of a Week 1 return. "From the day I got the surgery, as quick as I did, to hopefully the first game of the year, the plan will go accordingly, and I'll be able to go out there and be myself."
Although Mahomes has participated in every practice of training camp so far, he still hasn't taken any hits, and that's the big difference between being cleared for practice and being cleared for a game.
"You know, obviously I haven't played in the game and been able to get hit," Mahomes said, via KMBC.com . "But having people around me and competing and doing stuff like that, it's almost like I do everything I naturally do, and then after, it's kind of like the coaches coaching me, like, 'Hey, let's calm down a little bit.' Being a competitor, I want to go out there and win."
Playing in a game also means that Mahomes will be scrambling and making cuts, something he hasn't really had to do in camp.
"I try to not make those hard cuts and stuff like that. But at the end of the day, I'm a competitor, and it kind of just takes over sometimes," Mahomes said. "So you want to still prove to yourself that you can do it. And I've been able to do that in certain spots, making quick cuts, making reactionary cuts, which I think is the biggest thing when it comes to this, and felt great doing it."
If Mahomes isn't cleared to play, then Justin Fields will get the start for Kansas City.
With Mahomes coming off a serious knee injury, the last thing the Chiefs want to do is bring him back too quickly. If his knee isn't quite ready to go and he reinjures it, Kansas City's season would be over before it even really starts. One thing the Chiefs will have to keep in mind here is that if Mahomes does play, that means he's going to have to open the season by playing two games in six days.
Opening the season on a Monday night is a positive, because it gives the QB's knee one extra day to get back to 100%, but it's also a negative, because it means the Chiefs will be on a short week heading into their Week 2 game against the Colts .
Mahomes ability to heal has been impressive. Micah Parsons tore his ACL on the exact same day (Dec. 14) and the Packers star has already said that he won't be back on the field until Week 6 at the earliest. Mahomes tore his ACL and LCL while Parsons only tore his ACL, so Mahomes' injury was actually worse, but the QB is still expected to be making his return at least six weeks before Parsons.
Parsons and Mahomes obviously play different positions, so it's not the same rehab, but it's certainly worth noting that Mahomes is on track for an extremely quick recovery. title: What's next for Shedeur Sanders? NFL sources question whether Browns QB has a starting future
summary: After Deshaun Watson won Cleveland's starting job, NFL coaches and front-office officials explain why Sanders faces an uncertain future -- and why some teams wouldn't trade for him even if he became available
full_text:
Leading up to the Browns ' preseason game against the Bills last week, there was a widespread expectation inside the Cleveland building that Deshaun Watson would prevail over Shedeur Sanders to win Cleveland's starting quarterback job.
While it was fair to question afterward whether the sloppy showcase from Watson in that game, and even more so his well-publicized postgame comments, could impact head coach Todd Monken's thought process with the competition, it didn't end up deterring Monken from going with the quarterback he believes clearly gives the Browns the best chance to win -- Watson, whom he officially named as Cleveland's starting QB Monday morning.
However, because of Saturday, the Browns are left with additional external skeptics that Watson will have any success as Cleveland's starting quarterback. It's also led to another question among some in NFL coaching and front office circles: What's next for Sanders now that he's officially lost this competition?
The short answer: There aren't many,  if any, NFL front office staffers that view him as an NFL starting-caliber quarterback.
"Him not even being able to beat out Deshaun (who hasn't played in an NFL regular season game since his first Achilles injury in 2024) is probably telling," an NFL front office staffer told CBS Sports.
To be clear, there have been some positives from Sanders these last two years in Cleveland, including the 24-year-old finishing 9-for-11 against the Bills on Saturday with a touchdown pass and an interception that was a byproduct of a catchable pass tipping into the air off of the hands of his intended receiver. There's also still a clear chance he could end up starting at some point this season depending on the play of Watson.
However, it shouldn't come as a surprise that the universal expectation around the league is that the future of the Browns' quarterback room is currently playing for a college team and that it's not Sanders, Watson, 2025 third-round draft pick Dillon Gabriel or rookie sixth-round selection Taylen Green . There are also even questions about Sanders' fit as a backup, including -- fair or not -- because of the celebrity and distraction components that come along with him being such a high-profile and polarizing figure.
That factors into why front office officials from multiple NFL teams have told CBS Sports that they wouldn't have interest in trading for Sanders even if he were available.
"Do you really want to deal with that (especially with someone who's not your starting quarterback)?" a front office staffer said.
It's not like any of this should come as a shock.
Sanders slipping to the fifth round of last year's NFL wasn't just because of some pre-draft team interviews that reportedly didn't go well or concerns about him being a distraction. Frankly, there were a number of personnel and scouting sources who'd told CBS Sports during the buildup to the draft that they didn't have starter grades on Sanders and that -- just from a skill set perspective -- they questioned his capability to become an effective starter at the NFL level.
Though Sanders wound up being the Browns' starting quarterback for their final eight games last season, his QB rating (68.1) ranked last in the NFL among quarterbacks with more than 22 pass attempts. NFL sources also still see clear weaknesses in his game -- beyond just arm strength that's far from elite -- such as holding onto the ball too long and being a slow processor at times.
And while many who have been around Sanders describe him as likable and genuinely being of good character, there have also been sources critical of his preparation at different points and who have referenced him being challenging to manage at times, including last year for example when he knew he wasn't going to be starting.
It's why there are even some around the NFL who even wonder if Gabriel would be a better fit as Cleveland's backup, referencing things such as his work ethic and the ability to function on short notice.
Nevertheless, at least for now, the Browns have indicated they're moving forward with Sanders as their backup quarterback and it remains to be seen how badly Watson would need to struggle for Sanders to get an opportunity to replace him as Cleveland's starter.
"All Monk cares about," a source said, "is being in the best position to win."
