(Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Buffalo Bills will close out the preseason Thursday night when the Pittsburgh Steelers come to Highmark Stadium, and while there are still more than a few roster spots up for grabs, one of the pivotal positional battles appears to have been settled heading into Week 3 of the preseason. Today’s edition of Buffalo Rumblinks leads off by recapping the latest news out of One Bills Drive, including how returner Alec Anderson has reportedly won the starting left guard battle, edging out Austin Corbett. Check out the assessments below and then let us know your thoughts on the latest Bills news in the comments section. Alec Anderson appears to have won the starting LG job ESPN Buffalo Bills reporter Alaina Getzenberg was the first to report the news that Alec Anderson will be Buffalo’s starting left guard this year. Anderson, who was originally signed by the Bills as an undrafted rookie free agent following the 2022 NFL Draft, has played in 34 games over the last two seasons, including making six starts as a valuable backup on the offensive line. summary: The Carolina Panthers will close out the preseason following joint practices this week against the Houston Texans. Head Coach Dave Canales stated that the starters will not play this week in this final game, so we’re getting our last in game look at the backups. While this is never the most exciting part of the […]
full_text: CANTON, OHIO - AUGUST 06: Claudin Cherelus #53 and Trevin Wallace #32 of the Carolina Panthers tackle Bam Knight #20 of the Arizona Cardinals during the first quarter of the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame Game at Tom Benson Hall Of Fame Stadium on August 06, 2026 in Canton, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Carolina Panthers will close out the preseason following joint practices this week against the Houston Texans. Head Coach Dave Canales stated that the starters will not play this week in this final game, so we’re getting our last in game look at the backups. While this is never the most exciting part of the preseason, on defense in particular the Panthers still have some questions to answer with their depth pieces all along unit. Let’s dive into what to watch for. Zakee Wheatley and Lathan Ransom setting the tone We’ve seen some crushing hits from Lathan Ransom all throughout the preseason, but his running make and fellow late day pick for the future Zakee Wheatley had himself a nice cruncher himself against the Texans offense during joint drills. Both have the capacity and skillset to potentially play a lot of snaps in this defense during the regular season, so these additional snaps could really sell the coaching staff on that particular fact. Both have played pretty well during their limited action, and I expect them to be starting together for this final game. EDGE rusher final battle With Patrick Jones and Jaelan Phillips slated to be the starters and Princely Umanmielen figuring heavily into the rotation, one of the underrated story lines of the preseason has been what goes on behind them. Cam Gill, Thomas Incoom, and Trevis Gipson have all flashed as pass rushers throughout the preseason, and they’ll be going up against a fairly good backup quarterback in Davis Mills for some time in this game. The backup offensive line rotation is always difficult to project during the depth showing periods, so it is hard to say who they will line up against. But a good showing could make a big difference between being another key piece of the rotation or the last spot on the depth chart, potentially even being relegated to the practice squad. Inside linebacker still unclear It doesn’t appear that Claudin Cherelus or Trevin Wallace has really taken the reigns of that starting inside linebacker spot, and while I’d expect one of them to end up winning, there’s an outside shot of Bam Martin-Scott or Jackson Kuwatch snaking away some snaps come the regular season if the job isn’t won decisively. Since they’ll all be playing behind a who’s who of defensive linemen, it may be difficult to push the conversation much further aside from major splash plays. But this I arguably the biggest position to be watching if you make the decision to watch the entirety of the final preseason game. What are you watching for this week, Panthers fans?

title: Panthers vs Texans: Offensive Preview
summary: Dave Canales really killed most of the intrigue with this game when he announced that the starters would not be playing after getting a heavy workload in joint practices with the Houston Texans. Those apparently did not go well for the offense, so it’s probably a good thing that they won’t get subjected to more […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 21: Jimmy Horn Jr. #15 of the Carolina Panthers runs against the Jacksonville Jaguars during the first half of the preseason game at EverBank Field on August 21, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Dave Canales really killed most of the intrigue with this game when he announced that the starters would not be playing after getting a heavy workload in joint practices with the Houston Texans. Those apparently did not go well for the offense, so it’s probably a good thing that they won’t get subjected to more torture in front of a significant audience on the television. Instead, their last preseason action will be a solid drive against the Jaguars that ended with a touchdown run from Jonathon Brooks. It’d be nice to have more positives to look at going into the regular season, but I guess we’ll have to make do with what we’ve got, and that’s a couple nice practices and one good drive against the Jaguars. On Friday, we’ll watch the backups get one last chance to make an impression and earn more looks or even a spot on the roster going into the regular season. Here’s what we cant watch for: Will a rotational receiver separate themselves from the pack? Jimmy Horn Jr. has frequently been lauded for his work in practices with his speed and ability to take the top of the defense. He’s had some flashes in preseason games as well, including a 39 yard run on an end around last week and four catches for 44 yards in the preseason opener. Ja’seem Reed has been the annual training camp wide receiver standout and has scored a touchdown. John Metchie III has shown some underneath receiving chops, and Roc Taylor has a nice touchdown catct. There are a lot of receivers jockeying for position behind Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker (and I guess Xavier Legette). All of them are going to get opportunities to show out one more time before the coaching staff sets the final roster. A standout showing could get someone some more looks once the regular season gets started. What does the offensive line depth look like? It’s been a mixed bag for the offensive line depth. They did a good job against the Jaguars not allowing a single sack, but they gave up three sacks on Kenny Pickett against the Bills and have had some shaky moments throughout camp. The Texans have one of the nastiest defenses in the league, and even their reserves are likely to cause some problems for the offensive line. If they hold up, it’ll instill some confidence for what the group can do if any are pressed into action during the regular season. Generate some explosives! I know the preseason usually isn’t a place for chunk plays, but I’d like to see some just so we know the offense is capable of it. Kenny Pickett was notorious for his conservative passing style in Pittsburgh and has done more of the same in the preseason thus far. The receivers are going to be looking for opportunities to show out, and I’d like to see Pickett (and Kyle Trask) push the ball down the field and give the receivers a chance to make some plays.

title: 2026 Season Opener Countdown: 17 Days Remaining
summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - NOVEMBER 16: DeAngelo Williams #34 of the Carolina Panthers against the Atlanta Falcons during their game at Bank of America Stadium on November 16, 2014 in Charlotte, North Carolina. Atlanta won 19-17. (Photo by Grant Halverson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #17. DeAngelo Williams The Carolina Panthers used the 27th overall pick in the first round of the 2006 NFL Draft to take a dynamic running back out of Memphis. Williams was explosive in college, rushing for over 6,000 yards including back to back seasons of over 2,000 total yards and 42 total touchdowns across his junior and senior seasons. Because Williams didn’t play in a major football conference, he wasn’t in the Reggie Bush tier of pre-draft buzz. Still, he was the third of four first round running backs taken that year. The Panthers still had Deshaun Foster as the starting back, so Williams only had about 500 rushing yards his rookie season. After a couple seasons of splitting carries with Foster, the Panthers gave Williams the starting job in 2008. He rewarded that faith with over 1,500 rushing yards and a career high 18 touchdowns, earning him the PFWA Most Improved award and a Second Team All-Pro nod for his breakout season. That production outburst may have been in response to the Panthers using the 13th overall pick in the 2008 Draft to take another running back: Jonathan Stewart. Taking two first round running backs in three years ended up being great for the Panthers and Williams’ longevity, though he never matched the stat production from that 2008 season. The following season, Double Trouble as they became to be known became just the sixth pair of teammates to both rush for over 1,000 yards in the same season. 2010 was a rough year all around for the Panthers, and Williams was no different. He suffered a foot sprain just halfway through the season that landed him on IR, in part because the Panthers season was already essentially over. Everything turned around in 2011 for the Panthers as a whole with the addition of Cam Newton at quarterback. For Williams, though, that meant an already crowded backfield added another ball carrier. Williams was still productive when called upon, averaging about 50 yards per game over the next three seasons. In 2014, Williams’ career with the Panthers came to an unfortunate end. After missing ten games due to various injuries, the team released Williams. He signed with the Pittsburgh Steelers, playing two seasons before retiring. Though Williams’ departure from the team was less than amenable, with rumors of hurt feelings due to a lack of team attendance at his mother’s funeral, his time with the team was undeniably successful. Williams was the rare combination of elite highs and overall longevity, especially at the running back position. His two year run in 2008 and 2009 put him near the top tier of running backs league wide, and his nine years with the team cemented him in the Panthers record books. He is the second leading rusher in Panthers history and third in rushing touchdowns, and his 2008 season still stands as the record for most rushing yards and most rushing touchdowns in a single season. Since you can’t tell the history of the Panthers without Double Trouble, DeAngelo Williams lands at No. 17 in our countdown.

title: Chicago Bears Question of the Day: Are you okay with them having an offense-first identity?
summary: This isn’t the first time, but it sure feels more real. The 2026 Chicago Bears will be a team that showcases a potent offense and a middling (or worse) defense. If you’re older than 5 years old, you’re probably used to the star players on the Bears being named Mack, Peppers, Tillman, Urlacher, Singletary, Dent, […]
full_text: This isn’t the first time, but it sure feels more real. The 2026 Chicago Bears will be a team that showcases a potent offense and a middling (or worse) defense. If you’re older than 5 years old, you’re probably used to the star players on the Bears being named Mack, Peppers, Tillman, Urlacher, Singletary, Dent, or Butkus. Sure, there have been some noteworthy offensive talents in the history of the Chicago Bears — the likes of Payton, Forte, Marshall, and Kreutz come to mind. But these were more isolated talents than cogs in a dominant system. The 2026 Bears should be at a minimum a top 10 offense in the NFL. The goal should be a top 5 unit. They boast above average to elite units across their offense. Offensive Line: Thuney, Wright, and Jackson already make this above average. The return of Trapilo and the fits of Bradbury and Jones could raise the ceiling even higher. Wide Receivers: Rome Odunze and Luther Burden have an enormous combined ceiling. The potentials of Jahdae Walker and Zavion Thomas with the savvy presence of Kalif Raymond makes this unit talented and deep. Tight Ends: The trio of Colston Loveland, Cole Kmet, and Sam Roush is the best in the league. Include Hayden Large and Stephen Carlson, and this is one of the best position groups in the league. Running Backs: D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai were a duo that led an elite rushing attack last year. There should be no expectation for this group to slow down. Quarterbacks: Caleb Williams is already in the conversation to be a top 10 QB in the league, and has the skills and drive to be even better. Play Caller: Ben Johnson is elite. He has been and will remain one of the best offensive minds in the league. He is one of only a few significant difference makers as playcallers in the league. This offense should shoot for the moon this year, because that is their potential. They should also do that because, well, the defense has a lot more question marks. Defensive Line: This unit was underwhelming last year and really only has one serious difference maker in Montez Sweat. Everyone else is either slated to be a rotational piece, doesn’t have enough proven, or is an aging veteran. Add in the fact that Gervon Dexter is on the chopping block and the defensive line could be a major liability this season. Linebackers: While there is reason for optimism with the addition of a player like Devin Bush, there are still questions about health within this unit. TJ Edwards, Noah Sewell, and Keyshaun Elliot are all trying to return from injuries this season. Cornerbacks: There is sooooo much talent in this cornerback room. But who can you truly trust? Jaylon Johnson is a year removed from looking like a CB1 after an injury riddled season. Tyrique Stevenson is meteoric in both directions. Kyler Gordon may never return from injury. Malik Muhammad is still learning how to play. Terrell Smith hasn’t played a meaningful snap in over a year. This unit has a ton to prove. Safeties: This room was overhauled in the offseason — adding talents in Dillon Thieneman and Coby Bryant. With Bryant’s injury, the Bears look exposed on the back end. While Thieneman might eventually be a very good player, he is still very green. Pairing him with Bryant would have been a strong pairing, but the Bears have been searching for Bryant’s replacement, with Xavier Woods looking like the main guy. It’s possible the Bears offense doesn’t live up to expectations. It’s also possible that the Bears defense exceeds expectations. With that said, it’s hard to imagine a reality where the defense outperforms the offense. This is the likely reality for Ben Johnson teams moving forward, which leads me to my question: Are you comfortable with the Bears being an offense-first identity? My answer – absolutely. I have loved the defenses of Bears history. Watching pass rushers swallow up QBs, punch out the ball, or return an INT for a touchdown has been a consistent joy for Bears’ fans. Unfortunately, this formula hasn’t led to a lot team success. Much of the talent and resources have historically been placed on the defensive side of the ball, leading to frustratingly inconsistent offensive play. There are exceptions, true. Under Marc Trestman, the Bears were a far superior offensive ball club than defensive, where Mel Tucker led a near bottom of the league unit. The difference between 2026 and 2013? Ben Johnson is not Marc Trestman and Dennis Allen is not Mel Tucker. Many fans have been pining for a team that dominates offensively, and we finally have the construction for one. I can remember draft classes headlined by Leonard Floyd and having five out of the first six picks being defensive. Remember the Kyle Fuller, Ego Ferguson, and Will Sutton 1-2-3 punch? Let’s give the Sam Roush pick a little bit of slack — it might just work. It’s very possible that the Seattle Seahawks have redefined success after their defense dominated its way to the 2025 Super Bowl. However, I think it’s a lot more common to look at sustained successes from the Kansas City Chiefs, Patriots, Rams, Niners, and Eagles over the last decade and see dominant offenses being the key to success. And don’t twist my words — these teams still had strong defensive units, but they were usually headlined by one game-wrecker (Donald, Jones) that complements dominant offenses. So I am fighting my urge to ask for balance. I am here to trust this new direction. Defense be damned. Let the 2026 Bears run up the score!

They flew off to Nashville today for a joint practice on Thursday with the Tennessee Titans, and the two teams play their preseason finale on Saturday at 5:00 pm (CT). There was some on-field action, as Mason Williams of the Times of Northwest Indiana shared that Caleb Williams was 4 for 6 in a 7-on-7 red zone period capped off with a touchdown to Jahdae Walker, and that Tyson Bagent had the day’s best ball to Scotty Miller for a touchdown in the same 7-on-7 red zone period. He was limited, but this is a positive sign for the Bears season opener on September 13 in Carolina. title: Marvin Lewis shares insight on Mike Brown and Bengals ownership
summary: As a small-market team, the Cincinnati Bengals have always been a franchise the national media picks on and spins narratives about each and every year. The front office has built a reputation over the past several decades but has slowly changed its ‘ways’ to help build a successful team around Joe Burrow. The Bengals extended […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OH - DECEMBER 23, 2018: Head coach Marvin Lewis of the Cincinnati Bengals on the field prior to a game against the Cleveland Browns on December 23, 2018 at FirstEnergy Stadium in Cleveland, Ohio. Cleveland won 26-18. (Photo by: 2018 Nick Cammett/Diamond Images/Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images As a small-market team, the Cincinnati Bengals have always been a franchise the national media picks on and spins narratives about each and every year. The front office has built a reputation over the past several decades but has slowly changed its ‘ways’ to help build a successful team around Joe Burrow. The Bengals extended Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins, something every media outlet claimed would never happen. The Bengals traded their first-round pick for superstar defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence, something the franchise has never done and everyone assumed would never happen. The Bengals have invested in the offensive line and have all five starters from last season returning to protect Burrow, something the media gripes on every single day. The Bengals spent roughly $125 million on defensive free agents to help bolster a defense that needed serious help, yet the media says the front office doesn’t spend money. The bottom line is the Bengals front office has changed their ways right in front of our eyes, and former head coach Marvin Lewis shared some interesting insight this week on how the front office operates, specifically Mike Brown. “Let’s talk about the Brown family,” Lewis said in an appearance on the Inside Football podcast . “Mike Brown doesn’t give a shit about money. Don’t waste it. All his money goes to that football team. The man has no outside habits other than reading big ass thick books that I used to just look at on his desk or beside me on the plane. He just wants to win football games the way he wants to win.” Lewis continued, “He doesn’t want to mortgage the franchise on one year and one player. He sees a 3 or 4 year projection and that is different than how some organizations work.” The former head coach went on to give examples of free agents the Bengals front office lost, and that forced them to pivot and figure out another option. He also shared his thoughts on Burrow being the voice for ownership… What Burrow wants, ownership wants to make happen. “I am telling ya, his (Burrow’s) words trigger action, ain’t no question in my mind because that man (Mike Brown) loves quarterbacks and wants to win in the worst way,” Lewis stated. It is neat to hear this perspective from Lewis because he was in the Bengals building every day for years and years.

The Bengals really shot for the moon when they drafted their two Young defensive tackles. Unfortunately, they seemed to have missed. Lamar Jackson says health limited his mobility in 2025, will still do ‘whatever it takes to win’ “It really would not [have] put my team in a good position if I was just running hurt — losing yards, things like that [were] happening,” Jackson said, via ESPN. “But whatever it takes to win, that is what I am all about and [I have] always been about that too.” We will see how much Jackson will truly run, and how much he was held back by health. NFL elevates Pro Bowl selection; AFC-NFC Pro Bowl game will no longer be staged “The Pro Bowl has always been about recognizing the players who distinguish themselves as the very best in the NFL,” said Peter O’Reilly, NFL executive vice president, club business, international and league events. “A Pro Bowl selection will return to its original purpose, honoring the best of the best. title: The 7 biggest decisions for the Cincinnati Bengals’ 53-man roster
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals‘ preseason finale against Philadelphia isn’t likely to change the outlook for players who have already locked up their roster spots. But for the players on the bubble, it could be enormous. One strong performance could secure a roster spot. One mistake could open the door for a competitor. And in some cases, […]
full_text: Aug 13, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Cincinnati Bengals defensive tackle Landon Robinson (96) reacts after a play in the first half against the Detroit Lions at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cincinnati Bengals ‘ preseason finale against Philadelphia isn’t likely to change the outlook for players who have already locked up their roster spots. But for the players on the bubble, it could be enormous. One strong performance could secure a roster spot. One mistake could open the door for a competitor. And in some cases, the final decision may have very little to do with individual performance. Special teams value, positional flexibility, injuries, and overall roster construction could ultimately determine who gets the final few jerseys. That’s what makes this year’s roster so fascinating. The Bengals appear to have considerably more depth than they did entering last season. Now they have to figure out how to fit all of it into 53 spots. The final preseason game can’t come soon enough. Absolutely. I’d make this version feel much more grounded in what we’ve actually seen during the 2026 camp and preseason, rather than simply revisiting a generic 53-man projection. The Bears game, in particular, changed the equation in several spots. One note: I was able to access the current 2026 reporting and roster information surrounding the podcast topic, but the YouTube page itself isn’t exposing the video’s transcript/comments through the web interface, so I don’t want to invent or misattribute quotes from that specific podcast. I’ve therefore built this around the actual 2026 developments and can seamlessly add the podcast quotes if you paste the transcript or the relevant portions. 7 Bengals Roster Questions That Could Decide the Final 53 The Bengals have one preseason game remaining, and the final 53-man roster is becoming considerably more difficult to predict. That’s a good problem to have. After years in which Cincinnati’s roster depth — particularly on defense — left something to be desired, the Bengals now have legitimate NFL players competing for what could be just a handful of available spots. The additions of Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen, Kyle Dugger and others have dramatically changed the complexion of the roster. At the same time, several young players and newcomers have made legitimate pushes during training camp. The first two preseason games have only made things more interesting. The Bengals are 2-0 after beating the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears, and Cincinnati’s backups handled Chicago’s starters particularly well in Saturday night’s 27-9 victory. Dohnte Meyers continued his remarkable preseason; rookie defensive tackle Landon Robinson made another impact, Josh Johnson threw two touchdown passes, and several other players strengthened their cases. Now comes the difficult part. Here are seven roster questions that could help determine which players are wearing Bengals uniforms when Week 1 arrives. 1. How many wide receivers can Cincinnati keep? This might be the most difficult offensive decision. Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Andrei Iosivas appear firmly entrenched. The real battle is behind them, where Colbie Young, Dohnte Meyers, Mitchell Tinsley, Charlie Jones and Ke’Shawn Williams are competing for a limited number of spots. And after Week 2 of the preseason, Noah Thomas now has a say. The two preseason games have made the decision significantly more difficult. Meyers has gone from an intriguing CFL addition to someone who increasingly looks like a player the Bengals need to find room for. Against Chicago, he caught five passes for 41 yards, added a nine-yard run, and contributed as a returner. His versatility has become a major part of his argument. Then there’s Young, who caught a touchdown against Chicago and has consistently looked like a player capable of making an impact at the NFL level. Tinsley hasn’t disappeared from the conversation, either. That could create a difficult decision involving Jones, who brings legitimate NFL experience and has been one of Cincinnati’s most valuable return options. The question may ultimately become less about who deserves a roster spot and more about how many receivers the Bengals can afford to carry. Six feels increasingly difficult to predict. Will the team like the size/speed combos provided by both Young and Thomas? Or, will they prefer “the devils they know,” in terms of Tinsley and Jones? Seven might be necessary. 2. Who gets the final linebacker spot? The linebacker competition hasn’t received quite as much attention as wide receiver or defensive line, but there could be a fascinating decision at the bottom of this group. The Bengals have veterans and young players competing for a limited number of positions, and special teams are likely an important factor. That’s particularly relevant because Cincinnati has players who can contribute beyond defensive snaps. Swayze Bozeman , for example, has continued to make noise with his special teams play, while other players such as Joe Giles-Harris, Shaka Heyward, and the younger linebackers are fighting for positioning. The Bengals don’t necessarily need to carry a huge linebacker room. But they do need players who can contribute on special teams and give Al Golden some flexibility defensively. That could make the final linebacker decision less about who has the best pure defensive upside and more about who can help Cincinnati win in multiple phases. 3. Josh Johnson or Sean Clifford — or both — to the practice squad? This is a much more interesting question after what happened against Chicago. The Bengals have Joe Burrow and Joe Flacco at the top of the quarterback room, meaning the real competition for Johnson and Clifford is likely about what happens after the 53-man roster is established. Johnson certainly helped himself. The 40-year-old veteran completed 15 of 23 passes for 156 yards and two touchdowns against Chicago, including scoring strikes to Colbie Young and Tanner Hudson. He showed command of the offense and handled the situation particularly well against a Bears defense that featured starters. Clifford also had a strong night, throwing a touchdown to Noah Thomas. That creates a fascinating decision. Even with the new rules, Cincinnati likely won’t keep three quarterbacks on the roster. Will they go with youth or experience on the practice squad? Or, even more intriguing, is the possibility of a trade. Does Cincinnati prefer Johnson’s experience or Clifford’s youth and developmental upside? Johnson has spent years navigating NFL offenses and has the type of experience a team might want in an emergency quarterback. Clifford is younger and could benefit more from another season of development. Both making the 53 seems unlikely. Both making the practice squad? It’s a possibility. 4. How many tight ends can the Bengals keep? The tight end room has quietly become one of the biggest roster headaches. Mike Gesicki and Drew Sample appear to be the safest bets, but after that, there are several players with legitimate arguments. Tanner Hudson has proven NFL production and a strong connection with Cincinnati’s quarterbacks. Erick All Jr. is returning from injury and offers intriguing versatility. Rookie Jack Endries has been one of the more impressive young players of camp. Cam Grandy has contributed on special teams and even took a snap at long snapper against Chicago, while Josh Kattus remains another developmental option. That’s seven players for a position where Cincinnati may only want to carry three or four. Endries’ emergence is particularly noteworthy. He was already showing promise in the preseason opener, and the Bengals continued to find ways to get him involved. The official roster outlook entering camp described the group as a combination of experienced pass catchers and blockers, with the returning All adding another dimension. Now the Bengals have to decide…

summary: Despite multiple injuries, Joe Burrow has established himself as one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL. Burrow has many attributes that make him an incredible quarterback, but one piece of his game that may not be talked about as much is his movement ability. Quarterback expert Jordan Palmer recently hopped on the Rich Eisen […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - AUGUST 13: Joe Burrow #9 of the Cincinnati Bengals steps back to pass against the Detroit Lions at Paycor Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Despite multiple injuries, Joe Burrow has established himself as one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL. Burrow has many attributes that make him an incredible quarterback, but one piece of his game that may not be talked about as much is his movement ability. Quarterback expert Jordan Palmer recently hopped on the Rich Eisen Show and discussed the talent of Burrow and specifically his efforts as a mover in and around the pocket. “What Joe’s done to help out o-line play is become a more efficient mover,” said Palmer. “It’s turned him into one of the most difficult guys to tackle behind the line of scrimmage despite not having tier one top-end athleticism.” Palmer didn’t stop there and shared a specific story. “I went up to the Super Bowl, and I was on the plane with…I’ll just say an All-Pro defensive player. And I asked him to ‘Rank this guy, rank this, rank this’, and this guy kind of said Joe (Burrow) in almost every category. And one of them was most difficult to tackle. So I think that’s what he’s done to control what he can control is continue to become an efficient mover. I think that he’s mastered controlling what you can control, which is why you don’t hear him venting about anything.” There are plenty of clips that come to mind of Burrow supporting Palmer’s comments, and his ability to extend plays causes incredible strain on opposing defenses. On the flip side, this is a piece of Burrow’s game that puts him in situations that can cause injury, so it will be interesting to see how much scrambling he does moving forward rather than throwing the ball away and playing for the next down.

summary: The NFL is making some major changes to its player-safety rules ahead of the 2026 season. On Wednesday, the NFL and NFLPA announced several changes that will likely spark controversy, since they could result in player suspensions. Going forward, players who commit three violations in any of these categories in a season will be suspended […]
full_text: Dec 21, 2025; Arlington, Texas, USA; Detail of NFL logo on a goal post pad before a game between the Los Angeles Chargers and Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The NFL is making some major changes to its player-safety rules ahead of the 2026 season. On Wednesday, the NFL and NFLPA announced several changes that will likely spark controversy, since they could result in player suspensions. Going forward, players who commit three violations in any of these categories in a season will be suspended for one game: Hip-drop tackle Horse-collar tackle Launching Hit on a defenseless player Blindside block The league is now placing greater emphasis on eliminating these fouls, which means we could see more calls this season. The hip-drop tackle in particular is something that is still being worked on since the ban on them came in 2024, just two years ago, and it’s not something that’s been called much so far. That is likely changing this year, so we could not only see it flagged more often, but also see it lead to suspensions. Now, all players will begin 2026 with a clean slate. That’s the good news. Another controversial decision is that violations will carry over into future seasons. So a player could potentially commit, let’s say, two of these violations in 2026. Then, if said player commits another one in 2027, he could be suspended for a game. So, what are your thoughts on these changes? Is a three-strikes-and-you’re-out approach the correct method for these types of infractions?

title: NFL ends Pro Bowl Games
summary: The NFL finally waved goodbye to the Pro Bowl Games on Wednesday, as the league announced it would no longer hold its annual skills competition. This was a long time coming, as the annual all-star event had continued to lose interest over the years. It was once a major event that was effectively a real […]
full_text: Jan 30, 2025; Orlando, FL, USA; AFC wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase of the Cincinnati Bengals (1) during the Pro Bowl Skills Challenge at Nicholson Fieldhouse. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The NFL finally waved goodbye to the Pro Bowl Games on Wednesday, as the league announced it would no longer hold its annual skills competition . This was a long time coming, as the annual all-star event had continued to lose interest over the years. It was once a major event that was effectively a real football game played among the NFL’s best. But over the years, it became lighter and lighter due to player safety, eventually becoming nothing more than a glorified flag football game. Then that was also scrapped in favor of a skills competition spread across several days. Still, viewership continued to dwindle, so it’s not too surprising to see it finally get the axe. The league will still have Pro Bowl selections and a voting process that fans can be part of. That means Bengals fans could still see guys like Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Dexter Lawrence earn Pro Bowl honors. There just won’t be any games or skill competitions taking place. Farewell, old friend.

title: More proof that Dohnte Meyers has made the Bengals’ 53-man roster
summary: It’s hard to overlook what former CFL wide receiver Dohnte Meyers has done thus far into training camp and the preseason. In fact, Meyers’ performance has likely secured his spot on the Cincinnati Bengals’ 53-man roster. A 26-year-old product of Delta State University, Meyers was someone who didn’t get much attention heading into training camp, […]
full_text: Aug 22, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Dohnte Meyers (81) runs after a catch during the first quarter against the Chicago Bears at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It’s hard to overlook what former CFL wide receiver Dohnte Meyers has done thus far into training camp and the preseason. In fact, Meyers’ performance has likely secured his spot on the Cincinnati Bengals ’ 53-man roster. A 26-year-old product of Delta State University, Meyers was someone who didn’t get much attention heading into training camp, and rightfully so. Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are the best wide receiver duo in football, while Andrei Iosivas is a solid No. 3 option. Meanwhile, rookie Colbie Young was always likely to make the roster as a fourth-round draft pick, while Mitchell Tinsley and Charlie Jones have done enough in the past to think their spots were secure entering camp. Not so fast, as Meyers has been arguably the most pleasant surprise on the entire roster thus far. That includes his two preseason outings thus far, in which he caught eight of 10 targets for 70 yards to go with two runs for 22 yards. He’s also returned two kickoffs for 54 yards and three punts for 45 yards. That seemed to be enough for Meyers to make the roster, but as mentioned above, there’s some stiff competition with Jones and Tinsley for those final spots. However, Wednesday’s practice likely ended any debate that Meyers is making the cut. It first began during practice when Meyers was actually running with the starting offense and catching passes from Joe Burrow. That lone is a sign that Meyers is in no danger of being cut. Burrow connects with Dohnte Meyers for a TD in 7 v 7 #Bengals @FOX19 pic.twitter.com/Upa6leBJLQ — Gabi Sorrentino (@GSorrentinoTV) August 26, 2026 But that’s not all. After practice, Burrow and Meyers reportedly spent about 40 minutes working together. 40 minutes after #Bengals practice ended, Joe Burrow and Dohnte Meyers walked into the locker room after an extended post-practice throwing session. I'll have more on what Dohnte said about it shortly. — Jay Morrison (@ByJayMorrison) August 26, 2026 That’s not something a veteran quarterback like Burrow is going to do with someone who’s getting a pink slip this weekend when final cuts are made. In other words, Dohnte Meyers is all but guaranteed a spot on the Bengals’ 53-man roster when it’s finally set on Sunday following final cuts.

Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cleveland Browns quarterback competition is finally over ; long live the Cleveland Browns quarterback competition . With the Browns final preseason game kicking off on Thursday night , fans will get a chance to see the other two quarterbacks after Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders have been the focus all offseason. With most Cleveland fans expecting Watson to play six or fewer games, Sanders could see the field quickly, leaving Dillon Gabriel and/or Taylen Green waiting in the wings to be the next man up, depending on how the initial 53-man roster plays out . After seeing Gabriel start last season, many fans are excited about what the athletic Green could do on the field. Luke Easterling actually called Green the Browns “most talented quarterback” as he looked at underrated rookies that could make an impact this year : That would be Green, who brings a rare skill set with his combination of size (6-6, 230), arm strength, and elite speed/athleticism. He still needs a ton of refinement when it comes to being an efficient, consistent passer from the pocket, but he was well worth a sixth-round pick after the promise he showed at Arkansas. It’ll take some time, but Green’s potential is through the roof. Seth Walder of ESPN believes that Green will be starting by the end of this season and compete with whoever Cleveland selects early in the 2027 NFL draft: Cleveland’s 2027 quarterback competition will be between a first-round pick and … Taylen Green. This essentially is a bet that Green will be starting for the Browns by the end of 2026. He might be the fourth-string quarterback at the moment, but I hardly think this is far-fetched, considering the poor track records of Watson (as a Brown), Sanders and Dillon Gabriel. Given HC Todd Monken’s love for explosive plays from the quarterback position, Green’s ability to run and his big arm could become more and more intriguing if any combination of Watson, Sanders, and/or Gabriel falters as the 2026 season rolls on. summary: Every NFL preseason, guys are lost for the year, or end up injured at some point and miss games. full_text: CLEVELAND, OH - AUGUST 22: Cleveland Browns quarterback Taylen Green (15) warms up prior to the National Football League preseason game between the Buffalo Bills and Cleveland Browns on August 22, 2026, at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland, OH. (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Every NFL preseason, guys are lost for the year, or end up injured at some point and miss games. While the Cleveland Browns play against the New England Patriots on Thursday Night on Prime Video, both teams have decided to get one last look at the bottom third of their roster, and rest the starters. Even some key backups won’t be playing as well, such as backup QB Shedeur Sanders,. RELATED: WATSON QB1 – HOW DID WE GET HERE AGAIN? The decision to rest starters is nothing new. Forever, teams have followed the lineup of no starters in game one, starters play two series in the second contest, then play a half, and finally, sit in the fourth exhibition game. However, now NFL teams only play three practice games. So sitting the starters is now what occurs in the final preseason contest. Browns head coach Todd Monken explained: “I talked to Coach (Mike) Vrabel; we had talked about initially wanting to play our starters and get them a series or two. They really hadn’t played their guys. But we both felt like we were thin, especially up front on both sides of the ball, and we just felt like we’d be better off not playing our starters in the game Thursday night.” In today’s preseason landscape, teams have been using their starters for when they host another club and share practice sessions before their exhibition game at the end of the week. For Cleveland, they hosted the Buffalo Bills and then played them last weekend. But few starters played in the actual game, whereas all of the starters on offense and defense were in full pads during the weekly scrimmages. Even though this Browns offense is new and has had its fair share of bumps in the road, this unit has a distinct advantage: they are able to scrimmage against a defense that last year was ranked #4 in the league. For Cleveland’s offense against the Patriots, QB Dillon Gabriel will play the first half while the second half will feature sixth-round rookie Taylen Green, who hasn’t taken a snap so far this preseason. Dillon will play with the second-team offense while Green will trot out with the third-string. Dillon’s place on this roster has been questioned , as most NFL teams only keep three signalcallers. The final cutdown is Sunday, August 30. Gabriel might be retained, or perhaps traded. Monken stated that in the last game against the Bills, Gabriel was inserted in the final quarter with the third-string offense against Buffalo’s third-team defense and threw just one pass. In this contest, Monken wants to see Gabriel leading the second-team offense and see what he can do: “We’re not playing them because we’d like to see Dillon (Gabriel) more. It worked out last game, that was unfair to him. So, in order to do that, to see more of him and see Taylen (Green), there’s just not enough reps. That’s the reason, there’s really nothing else.” Green hasn’t taken many snaps in preseason and has yet to throw a pass. He played sparingly against the Bills. The coaching staff is anxious to get him some extensive live action and see how he handles it. Green has been tabbed for development. He is a gifted athlete and is an incredible runner, one of Monken’s favorite traits in his quarterbacks. But Green has an accuracy issue that will take time to cure. “Just trying to see Taylen after he played pretty well in the limited reps he had against the Bills, and we want to see more of Dillon. It just hasn’t worked out trying to get those other guys reps. That’s the reason.” The Browns haven’t won a preseason game yet, but that is not important. Exhibition games are designed to give players live action so that the coaches can see how they react in stressful game situations. After all, the bottom third of the roster is fighting for not only jobs but a place on the final roster.

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 17
summary: It is Day 17 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: Football: NFL Playoffs: Dallas Cowboys QB Roger Staubach (12) in action vs Los Angeles Rams at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Los Angeles, CA 1/7/1979CREDIT: Walter Iooss Jr. (Photo by Walter Iooss Jr. /Sports Illustrated via Getty Images)(Set Number: X23042 TK! R2 F24 ) It is Day 17 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Here’s it is, Day 17 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit the defensive masterpiece that sent Dallas to a second consecutive Super Bowl. After playing nearly three quarters without scoring, the Cowboys forced one mistake after another and transformed a tense NFC Championship Game into a complete dismantling of the Los Angeles Rams. Sunday, January 7, 1979 — 5:00 p.m. ET Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, Los Angeles, California Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 28, Los Angeles Rams 0 The matchup was steeped in history and filled with hostility. Both teams had finished 12-4, but Los Angeles held the home-field advantage and had defeated Dallas 27-14 at the Coliseum earlier that season. The Rams were determined to overcome years of postseason frustration, while the defending champion Cowboys sought their fifth Super Bowl appearance. The opening half was a defensive struggle, with Dallas unable to find a consistent rhythm against the Rams’ talented front. Meanwhile, Los Angeles squandered its best chances when Frank Corral missed two field goals. As a result, the teams entered halftime tied 0-0, leaving the conference championship undecided. The Doomsday Defense turned the tide of the game midway through the third quarter. Charlie Waters intercepted Pat Haden and returned the ball to the Los Angeles 10-yard line. Five plays later, Tony Dorsett scored on a five-yard run, giving Dallas the first points of the afternoon. After Jackie Wallace’s punt return gave them possession at the Dallas 23, the Rams immediately threatened to respond. Los Angeles reached fourth-and-short at the 14, but Randy White and Larry Bethea stopped Jim Jodat before he could score. This pivotal stand preserved the lead and denied the Rams their best scoring opportunity to that point. Waters struck again near the end of the third quarter, intercepting another Haden pass and returning it to the Rams’ 20-yard line. During the play, Haden injured his throwing hand on Randy White’s helmet and left with a broken thumb. Just 58 seconds into the fourth quarter, Roger Staubach found Scott Laidlaw for a four-yard touchdown, extending the lead to 14-0. Vince Ferragamo, the backup quarterback, briefly gave Los Angeles hope by connecting with Willie Miller for 65 yards to the Dallas 10. However, Cullen Bryant mishandled the handoff on the following play, and Harvey Martin recovered the fumble at the 11. The Rams had moved within sight of the end zone, only to leave without points once again. Dallas’s next drive sealed the game. Dorsett burst through for 53 yards on the first play, amassing 70 yards in the ensuing 89-yard possession. Staubach capitalized with an 11-yard touchdown pass to Billy Joe DuPree, securing a commanding 21-0 lead for the Cowboys. Thomas “Hollywood” Henderson supplied the final exclamation point. After spending the week openly questioning whether the Rams could handle the moment, Henderson intercepted Ferragamo and returned the ball 68 yards for a touchdown with 1:19 remaining. His score completed the shutout and turned his pregame talk into one of the defining stories of the game. This game belongs on the countdown because it demonstrated the ruthless postseason quality of Landry’s Cowboys. Dallas absorbed everything the Rams offered during a difficult first half, remained patient and then punished every mistake after halftime. What began as a close defensive contest ended as one of the most decisive conference-title victories in franchise history. #Cowboys vs #Rams 1979 NFC Championship Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 28, Los Angeles Rams 0 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/n7AL2AG2q8 — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 27, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Dallas wore its royal-blue jerseys, making this the franchise’s last playoff victory in a blue uniform until its Wild Card win at Tampa Bay following the 2022 season. title: 3 position battles to watch in the Cowboys preseason finale
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have to trim the roster from 90 to 53 players by this Sunday at 6 PM. It won’t be easy. The Cowboys have a lot of players on the bottom of the depth chart who could contribute for other teams either on the active roster or the practice squad. When Dallas plays […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - AUGUST 22: Marist Liufau #35 of the Dallas Cowboys pass rushes during a preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have to trim the roster from 90 to 53 players by this Sunday at 6 PM. It won’t be easy. The Cowboys have a lot of players on the bottom of the depth chart who could contribute for other teams either on the active roster or the practice squad. When Dallas plays on Friday against the New Orleans Saints, there will be high stakes. For who? Who are locked in for one last audition to prove they belong on the team or deserve actual reps, and who are those players up against on their team? Here are some key position battles to watch in tomorrow’s game. Marist Liufau vs. Sam Williams The Cowboys have a good mix of veteran and young talent to lead their pass rush group. Adding Rashan Gary and Von Miller, who has plenty left in the tank, provides the team with excellent experience. Along with them are Malachi Lawrence and Donovan Ezeiruaku, who have the talent to explode for double-digit sacks. The bottom of the pecking order is left to fight for a roster spot and reps, and that has created a heated battle with Marist Liufau and Sam Williams, who are clinging to a possible spot on the team. Sam Williams has put together a nice camp for himself and has shown up in the first two games. Williams recorded a sack against the Arizona Cardinals last week. Meanwhile, Marist Liufau hasn’t recorded a sack officially in the preseason, but he has been able to create some pressure with his speed off the edge, and contributes greatly on special teams. Williams doesn’t have the same versatility as Liufau to drop back in coverage or play inside if needed. Yet, Liufau doesn’t have the natural pass rush arsenal that Williams has since Liufau has recently moved to the position. Both players are competing with James Houston for a roster spot, who has also been consistent as a pass rusher. Look for Williams and Liufau to have extended snaps to show us who is the best man to earn a spot on the team. Malik Davis vs. Jaydon Blue for RB2 & Israel Abanikanda vs. Phil Mafah for the roster It was all good just a little while ago. When training camp started, it was Jaydon Blue who had the leg up on the primary job to back up Javonte Williams. In fact, Malik Davis was behind both second-year players Blue and Phil Mafah. Fast forward to the present, and Davis hasn’t gone away quietly and has pushed to earn the second running back spot outright. After the first preseason game, Malik Davis looked to have surpassed Blue, and then he showed more of the same with a good performance against the Cardinals. Blue answered back with multiple highlight plays showcasing his agility and speed. Blue led the team in rushing, with both runners playing to a proverbial stalemate last Saturday. That’s only one running back battle to check out this week. Let’s assume the Cowboys go heavy at running back and keep four along with Hunter Leupke; who would win the last spot? Phil Mafah or Israel Abanikanda? Phil Mafah had only one carry last week, but he made the most of it, avoiding a sure tackle for loss, changing direction, and racing past the Cardinals defense for a late score. Phil Mafah zooms in for a Cowboys TD 👏 DALvsAZ on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/gUktkzSGVo — NFL (@NFL) August 23, 2026 As for Abanikanda, he too has had a good training camp and has shown not only his speed in practices but the strength to keep the chains moving with his power and willingness to finish runs. Abanikanda and Mafah could split reps in the second half for a final push to make the team in the game’s dwindling moments. Joe Milton vs. Sam Howell Up to this point, Joe Milton should feel like he’s comfortably ahead in the race for QB2. Through two games, he has been stellar. He has completed 75% of his passes for 286 yards and three touchdowns for a passer rating of 142.8. He has made tremendous strides to improve his timing and touch on his throws. As of now, this is his job to lose. Milton can’t afford to regress against the Saints or allow doubt to creep back into the mind of the decision-makers. Howell played well in the preseason opener, posting stats almost identical to Milton. Joe Milton LAUNCHES it for a 53-yard TD pass to Jonathan Mingo 🚀 DALvsAZ on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/3LgWRZrsii — NFL (@NFL) August 23, 2026 With Milton ahead in the race, don’t be surprised if the team gives him a brief appearance for about a quarter and leaves Howell to finish the rest of the way. The offensive line also has a lot to prove as the team sorts out the offensive line rotation. Expect the best out of that group as well as receivers Jonathan Mingo and Anthony Smith, who need to deliver for Howell. Mingo and Smith also have an opportunity to make the team. Still, let’s be transparent: For Howell, he’s in the bottom of the ninth and needs a grand slam just to tie the game with Milton. He has to have a huge game this week.

title: Cowboys once again predicted to sign free agent LB Bobby Wagner
summary: Training camp has officially come and gone, and just one preseason tune-up stands between the Dallas Cowboys and the start of the 2026 regular season. Friday night will be the final chance for Cowboys players on the roster bubble to make their case, as Dallas hosts the New Orleans Saints in the preseason finale. At […]
full_text: Training camp has officially come and gone, and just one preseason tune-up stands between the Dallas Cowboys and the start of the 2026 regular season. Friday night will be the final chance for Cowboys players on the roster bubble to make their case, as Dallas hosts the New Orleans Saints in the preseason finale. At this point in time, there is no denying that Dallas’ roster, at least on paper, looks better than it did a year ago today. While the Cowboys seem to be in a better spot, they are nowhere close to a finished product. The Cowboys could benefit from adding some more depth, particularly on the defensive side of the ball, before the start of the regular season. If Dallas looks outside the organization to make an upgrade, linebacker will likely be near the top of their priority list. While the Cowboys did bring in Dee Winters during the spring, the long-term health concerns surrounding DeMarvion Overshown and the inexperience of rookie Jaishawn Barham may push Dallas to add another capable body to the group. While most instant-impact free agents are no longer on the open market, a few players still available could be solid contributors on contending teams. At this point in the summer, those guys are looking to latch on with a team before the start of the year in any way possible. One of those players is veteran linebacker Bobby Wagner. Wagner, who played the last two seasons with the Washington Commanders, has been linked to the Cowboys many times in the past few years. Just this week, that connection was rekindled once again in the speculation realm. In an article predicting where the top remaining free agents will sign before the start of the regular season, Wagner is predicted to end up in Dallas. When it comes to big names left on the market, there is none bigger than Bobby Wagner. The future Hall of Famer is a six-time first-team All-Pro who has racked up 2,000 tackles over 14 seasons. He also remains a starting-caliber off-ball linebacker. Wagner, who is the reigning Walter Payton Man of the Year, started all 17 games for the Washington Commanders last season and finished with 162 tackles, 4.5 sacks, eight tackles for loss, and two interceptions. There is no shortage of teams that could use a defensive leader of Wagner’s caliber, but the Dallas Cowboys might make the most sense. Dallas has taken an aggressive approach to rebuilding its defense this offseason—one that has included adding Miller—and head coach Brian Schottenheimer spent time with Wagner with the Seattle Seahawks. “You’re looking at one of the biggest Bobby Wagner fans in the world,” Schottenheimer told Kay Adams of Up & Adams in March. “…I love that guy.” Wagner may want to skip the rigors of training camp and land with a team after roster cuts, but the 36-year-old is likely to play again in 2026. The prediction here is that he jumps from one NFC East team to another. The Cowboys/Wagner pairing makes almost too much sense for it not to happen. While the former All-Pro is not the player he once was, he would be an extremely valuable depth piece for a Cowboys team that could desperately use another linebacker with consistent starting experience. Adding Wagner would not just make the Cowboys better right now; it would give them some much-needed insurance in case either Winters or Overshown is unable to stay healthy throughout the entirety of the regular season. If the Cowboys do end up being in the market to sign a veteran free agent before September 13th, there is a decent chance Bobby Wagner will be that guy. Would you sign Wagner? Which free agent still out there do you have your eye on?

title: Dallas Cowboys 2026 Opponent Preview: San Francisco 49ers
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have completed their West Coast portion of 2026 training camp in Oxnard, California, as well as two preseason tests against NFC West opponents, the Seattle Seahawks and Arizona Cardinals. The Cowboys won both games, both against opponents they will see again when it matters. It is time to wrap up the NFC […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - OCTOBER 8: Deebo Samuel #19 of the San Francisco 49ers runs after making a catch during game against the Dallas Cowboys at Levi's Stadium on October 8, 2023 in Santa Clara, California. The 49ers defeated the Cowboys 42-10. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) *** Deebo Samuel | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have completed their West Coast portion of 2026 training camp in Oxnard, California, as well as two preseason tests against NFC West opponents, the Seattle Seahawks and Arizona Cardinals. The Cowboys won both games, both against opponents they will see again when it matters. It is time to wrap up the NFC West when it comes to our regular season opponent preview series, concluding with the San Francisco 49ers. The Cowboys will host the 49ers in week ten, San Francisco’s first trip to Arlington since a 2022 Wild Card game. The 49ers knocked the Cowboys out of the playoffs the following year as well, the start of three straight home wins for Kyle Shanahan’s team against the Cowboys, getting the better of the Mike McCarthy/Dan Quinn defense 42-10 in 2023 and then McCarthy/Mike Zimmer in what proved to be the final year of McCarthy’s tenure and one and only season for Zimmer, 30-24. This entire point in time for the Cowboys was defined very directly by how they played against the 49ers and other teams that brought the same type of physicality, failing to matchup in the trenches in numerous big games or play with enough creativity on offense. This comparison has come and gone right at a point where the Cowboys are showing intention to dominate the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball unlike any of these other recent seasons, but also late enough where the 49ers have taken a step back from being the class of their division. Cowboys fans find themselves much more worried about back-to-back December games (with a bye in between) against the 49ers rivals, the Seahawks and the Rams. What has caused these issues for the 49ers, and in what ways could they still be a surprise team in 2026? Let’s look at their offseason to find out. 49ers Key Free Agent Signings/Departures * SIGNED IN FREE AGENCY WR Mike Evans LB Dre Greenlaw LB Luke Gifford (Re-signed) WR Deebo Samuel CB Nate Hobbs WR Christian Kirk RB Zamir White * DEPARTED IN FREE AGENCY WR Jauan Jennings WR Kendrick Bourne RB Brian Robinson WR Skyy Moore DE Clelin Ferrell CB Jason Pinnock LB Curtis Robinson (Cowboys) Another super interesting point of comparison to start with between the 49ers and Cowboys reveals itself when looking at this free agency incoming and outgoing list. Dallas not having the right mix at wide receiver or enough depth to their pass catching group has been something that’s held them back, and now the 49ers find themselves going through as drastic of a retool at WR as they’ve had under Shanahan. Jauan Jennings, Kendrick Bourne, and Skyy Moore are gone, while Mike Evans, Christian Kirk, and the former bay area star Deebo Samuel are in. Klay Kubiak will be the new offensive coordinator trying to make it all tick, as the team seems poised to lean on the injury-prone Christian McCaffrey more than ever. On defense, another new coordinator that was a former head coach has replaced Robert Saleh who had the same accolades, this time being Raheem Morris. Saleh’s defense saved the 49ers in countless games last season by playing above their talent level. The 49ers will look to lean into Morris’ pressure style of defense with Dre Greenlaw back in the fold, and former Cowboy Osa Odighizuwa acquired via trade. Greenlaw and former running mate Fred Warner will have to be able to cover a lot of ground playing behind a defensive line that will prioritize getting up the field in Morris’ scheme, a line that still has Nick Bosa on the depth chart as well. A lot of good pieces are still in place at key positions for this 49ers team, but all of the familiar ways where they’ve been known to have an edge against opponents in past championship-contending seasons feel like they’ve been subdued going into 2026. For a Cowboys team that has not been shy about showing off the strength of their culture this offseason in year two of Brian Schottenheimer’s tenure, coach Schotty has built this culture with a small but crucial core of players that have the skins on the walls from those past 49ers losses. A week 10 win would be a massive boost to the confidence of this culture really meaning the Cowboys are different. With this game coming near the midpoint of the season, it will also be a good evaluation point to see how much Dallas is getting from their rookie class, with several picks getting off to a strong start this preseason. The 49ers will also likely need this injection of young talent to their roster to stay in contention through this point of the season, which brings us to their draft class. 49ers 2026 Draft Class Round 2, Pick 1 (33 Overall): WR De’Zhaun Stribling Round 3, Pick 6 (70 Overall): EDGE Romello Height Round 3, Pick 26 (90 Overall): RB Kaelon Black Round 4, Pick 7 (107 Overall): DT Gracen Halton Round 4, Pick 27 (127 Overall): OT Carver Willis Round 4, Pick 39 (139 Overall): CB Ephesians Prysock Round 5, Pick 14 (154 Overall): LB Jaden Dugger Round 5, Pick 39 (179 Overall): OT Enrique Cruz For a team without a first-round pick, the 49ers still did a good job in April of bringing in high value prospects at positions of need with talent floors capable of seeing the field in 2026. Their top pick was an extension of the retool they’re going through at wide receiver, bringing in Ole Miss’ De’Zhaun Stribling. The duo of Stribling and newcomer Christian Kirk, and of course George Kittle at tight end, puts the 49ers in good position to get back to something they’ve also shredded opposing defenses with the ability to do – attack the seams and create run-after-the catch opportunities over the middle. Romello Height is another piece to the pass rush puzzle for Morris to move around, while the defense also found help on all three levels with Ephesians Prysock at corner in the fourth round and the instinctual Jaden Dugger at linebacker in the fifth. Kaelon Black could prove to be one of the highest value picks of the draft, as the 49ers always find a way to get their backs involved, and Black has the big play potential and versatility to earn a role. With the Rams punting on immediate help with their first-round pick and going quarterback instead, and the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks using their first two picks on a running back and safety, the 49ers getting this 2026 draft class up to speed and contributing quickly could be their biggest key to remaining in contention for the division. 49ers 2026 Coaching Staff * New to staff this season: Defensive Coordinator Raheem Morris Special Teams Coordinator Brant Boyer Defensive Backs Ray Brown Assistant Head Coach (Defense) Matt Eberflus Defensive Pass Game Coordinator Jerry Gray The 49ers have good continuity returning in the secondary, but in addition to learning a new scheme overall with Raheem Morris, they’ll have a new defensive backs coach coming from the college ranks, Ray Brown, a new pass game coordinator, Jerry Gray, and last year’s Cowboys defensive coordinator “flavor of the season”, Matt Eberflus. When it comes to the 49ers coaching staff, the general consensus is that as long as Kyle Shanahan is the one leading them into battle, they’ll always be prepared, a tough opponent to beat, and control the game with their offense as Shanahan calls the plays. The Cowboys will equally have an offensive-minded play-calling head coach in 2026, as well as a new defensive coordinator and staff on that side of the ball. It will be telling which side in this head-to-head matchup this season feels better about their overall coaching situation by week 10, and one way to evaluate that is which head coach has the most distractions to deal with beyond calling their offenses. At this exact moment, it feels like…

title: Cowboys can do something for first time in over 40 years this Friday night
summary: Wins and losses in the preseason do not matter. The most important thing when it comes to the preseason is evaluating your roster and making decisions as a result to best help your team for when the games actually do count. We all agree. All of that being said, a win on Friday night for […]
full_text: FRISCO, TEXAS - AUGUST 25: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer of the Dallas Cowboys watches practice at The Star in Frisco on August 25, 2026 in Frisco, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images Wins and losses in the preseason do not matter. The most important thing when it comes to the preseason is evaluating your roster and making decisions as a result to best help your team for when the games actually do count. We all agree. All of that being said, a win on Friday night for the Dallas Cowboys would matter just a teeny bit. Cowboys can do something for first time in a while The Cowboys have been doing a lot of this throughout the preseason. When they won their first preseason game it was the first time since 2017 that they started the preseason 1-0. When they won their second game they reached 2-0 status in the preseason for the first time since 2007. You guessed it, there is something similar on the line should the Cowboys win this week, too. If the Cowboys win on Friday night then they will go 3-0 in the preseason, obviously, and finish the period with an undefeated record (also obviously). The thing about the previous years listed though is that they, like most of NFL history, are from a time in which the preseason was four games. This makes some of this a bit weird. With a win on Friday the Cowboys would finish undefeated (3-0 as opposed to 4-0) for the first time in the preseason since 1985. That was over 40 years ago. Way before we knew what The Drought™ was/is. While the Cowboys haven’t gone undefeated in a preseason since 1985 they have won three games in one as a result of it usually being a four-game variety. The last time that Dallas won at least three games in a single exhibition window was not quite as long ago, it was 2002. Given that “final” (it will change) 53-man rosters are due by Sunday, the true and ultimate purpose of this game is obviously coming away with enough knowledge to set it with full confidence. But, it would be kind of cool if the Cowboys won and kept erasing droughts of different kinds. Maybe that would lead to them erasing the ultimate one. Would it matter to you if they went 3-0 in preseason?

title: Cowboys news: Dallas defense playing faster under Christian Parker
summary: Christian Parker is bringing a new scheme to the defense of the Cowboys, and it’s already showing some huge benefits. The battle for the backup quarterback spot was a hot topic, but Joe Milton has taken control of the situation. Dallas hit the practice field on Wednesday, and rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham and cornerback Shavon […]
full_text: Christian Parker is bringing a new scheme to the defense of the Cowboys, and it’s already showing some huge benefits. The battle for the backup quarterback spot was a hot topic, but Joe Milton has taken control of the situation. Dallas hit the practice field on Wednesday, and rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham and cornerback Shavon Revel Jr. got some snaps with the starters. The final preseason for the Cowboys is on Friday, and the unofficial depth chart came out. Christian Parker’s defense allowing DeMarvion Overshown, Cowboys ‘to play fast’ – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys are looking to be a much more effective defense in 2026. According to DeMarvion Overshown, Christian Parker’s scheme is letting them play with more speed. Over the course of the last few months, Overshown has seen Dallas’ defense grow the most in trusting what they see. In his eyes, Parker, who was heralded by the Cowboys front office and Brian Schottenheimer as a great teacher when he was hired as defensive coordinator, has passed along his lessons in a way that all 11 players on the field know their jobs and the jobs of those around them. “He allows us to play fast just by putting us in the right calls, just by testing us in the meeting rooms, making sure everybody knows who they’re tied to, what the other 10 people are doing on the field,” Overshown said. Joe Milton is showing poise in Cowboys’ QB2 battle. What led to his ‘high level’ development – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News Dallas came into the season with a question mark at the backup quarterback position. However, during training camp, Joe Milton has started to separate himself. Milton’s poise and patience has been different in his second season playing for the Cowboys and learning from Schottenheimer. Part of the credit goes to the birth of his daughter last October. “Having a girl is different,” said Milton, who’s entering his third season in the NFL. “If I had a boy, I think I’d probably be the same as last year.” The Dallas Cowboys tease potential shakeup to starting lineup ahead of the preseason finale – Mauricio Rodriguez, AtoZ Sports The Cowboys did something very interesting on Wednesday. Linebacker Jaishawn Barham and cornerback Shavon Revel Jr. were running with the starting unit. Two “new” starters emerge on Cowboys defense In each of the two Cowboys team drill periods, there were a couple of changes to the starting lineup. One, rookie Jaishawn Barham started at inside linebacker alongside DeMarvion Overshown, pushing Dee Winters off the lineup. Additionally, CB Shavon Revel Jr. started at outside cornerback, with DaRon Bland on the other side. Cowboys release final unofficial depth chart of preseason – RJ Ochoa, Blogging The Boys Dallas is set the play in their final preseason game on Friday. The last unofficial depth chart has now been released. There is one exhibition remaining before the Dallas Cowboys have to put together their “final” 53-man roster, and it takes place on Friday evening at AT&T Stadium against the New Orleans Saints. NFL rules dictate that teams must offer depth charts for these preseason games and they continually stress that they are “unofficial.” Below you will find the latest and final one for the Cowboys this preseason period. Mick Shots: Roster remodel makes a difference – Mickey Spagnola, DallasCowboys.com There’s been a lot of roster turnover for the Cowboys heading into this season. It’s something they desperately needed. “The biggest thing for me, if you take our roster from last year and laid it down next to our roster from this year, there is no question the depth and talent is higher, and some of that is us developing some young players … but also the addition of a number of pieces. And that is a credit to Jerry and Stephen (Jones) and Will McClay and his staff, and our coaches have a hand in that. “This is a good football team – just got to make the right decisions when we get to cut-down day, which we will.” Stock Up: Which Cowboys are trending heading into preseason finale – Mike Crum, Cowboys Wire Dallas will battle the New Orleans Saints as they wrap up the preseason. Here’s a look at what is trending upward. The running back room has a top-end starter in Williams, and the depth begins with the guy nobody seems to want, Malik Davis. He isn’t flashy, but he doesn’t have major holes in his game. He gets what’s blocked for him on run plays, he can bring in a pass, his blocking is as good as Williams, and he plays special teams at a high level. In the latest preseason game, he caught a touchdown pass, blocked in pass protection to set up a big play, and rushed for nearly 6 yards per attempt. Dallas has their main backup, and the change-of-pace option finally showed up in Arizona. Daily discussion question: Who needs a big game to secure a roster spot?

title: NFL axes Pro Bowl game, alternates for 2026 and beyond
summary: On Wednesday, the NFL announced that it would be ending the annual Pro Bowl game starting with the upcoming 2026 season. Players will still receive recognition as being named Pro Bowlers, but it will simply be an awarded honor without any game attached to it. The Pro Bowl has been in existence in some form […]
full_text: Feb 4, 2024; Orlando, FL, USA; NFC tight end Jake Ferguson of the Dallas Cowboys makes a catch during the 2024 Pro Bowl at Camping World Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con On Wednesday, the NFL announced that it would be ending the annual Pro Bowl game starting with the upcoming 2026 season. Players will still receive recognition as being named Pro Bowlers, but it will simply be an awarded honor without any game attached to it. The Pro Bowl has been in existence in some form or fashion going back to 1939, when it was called the National Football League All-Star Game. We’ve seen it morph over time, especially in recent years as the league’s increased focus on player safety has made this extra game less desirable. As its competitive nature has increasingly waned, fan interest has continuously decreased. This means there will no longer be Pro Bowl alternates. #NFL should do this retroactively from a record keeping standpoint so there’s uniformity across eras Put all replacement Pro Bowl honors in a separate bucket https://t.co/QiGi1lGtU2 — Mike Sando (@SandoNFL) August 26, 2026 This change also means that there will no longer be a need for alternates to be named to Pro Bowl rosters. In the past, either because they were participating in the Super Bowl, were injured, or otherwise declined to play, original Pro Bowl selections have had to be substituted for. Last year, 15 replacements were needed to make up for absences from the original 88 players. This new format will eliminate that entirely. The impact of that could be greater than it sounds. For example, Cowboys TE Jake Ferguson is a two-time Pro Bowl alternate from the 2023 and 2025 seasons. Under this system, he would never have been. That could matter when it’s time for players to talk contracts, or when Hall of Fame credentials are being discussed. Even if agents and owners see through that stuff, it will certainly impact fan perceptions. Going on a player’s Wikipedia page and seeing “2x Pro Bowler” means something to many, as does the absence of such recognition. There may be a bigger adjustment here for some of those than it sounds on paper. As this takes effect immediately, we won’t have to wait long to gauge the impact. Hopefully, we’ll be too excited about the Cowboys’ Super Bowl appearance to worry much about it. So long, Pro Bowl! We’ll miss you. Well, some of us. Maybe.
