title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 18
summary: It is Day 18 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: Hall of Fame quarterback Roger Staubach (12) of the Dallas Cowboys rolls out and tries to elude Redskins defensive end Dallas Hickman (82) during the Cowboys 34-20 loss to the Washington Redskins on November 18, 1979 at RFK Stadium in Washington, D.C. (Photo by Nate Fine/Getty Images) It is Day 18 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. It’s Day 18 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit one of the greatest rivalry games and late comebacks in Cowboys history. Dallas trailed Washington by 13 points with less than four minutes remaining, but Roger Staubach produced one final display of his “Captain Comeback” magic in what most call “The Wreath Game”. Sunday, December 16, 1979 Texas Stadium, Irving, Texas Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 35, Washington Redskins 34 Both teams entered the regular-season finale at 10-5, making the stakes straightforward. Dallas could claim the division and a first-round bye with a victory, while Washington needed to win to reach the playoffs. The rivalry was already heated after Washington had beaten the Cowboys 34-20 four weeks earlier. The Cowboys could hardly have started worse. Fumbles on their first two possessions helped Washington build a 10-0 lead through Mark Moseley’s 24-yard field goal and Joe Theismann’s one-yard touchdown run. Theismann then connected with Benny Malone for a 55-yard score early in the second quarter, placing Dallas in a 17-0 hole. Dallas finally responded behind rookie running back Ron Springs, who was starting in place of the injured Tony Dorsett. Springs scored from one yard out before Staubach found Preston Pearson for a diving 26-yard touchdown with nine seconds left in the half. The Cowboys had cut a 17-point deficit to 17-14 before entering the locker room. The comeback continued after halftime. Robert Newhouse scored on a two-yard run to give Dallas its first lead at 21-17, but Washington regained control during the fourth quarter. Moseley made another 24-yard field goal before John Riggins scored from one yard out following a Staubach interception. Riggins then broke free for a 66-yard touchdown, moving Washington ahead 34-21 with 6:54 remaining. The game appeared finished until Randy White recovered a Washington fumble with 3:49 left. Staubach needed only three plays to find Springs for a 26-yard touchdown, reducing the deficit to 34-28 with 2:20 remaining. Dallas still needed its defense to provide another opportunity. Washington faced third-and-one with a chance to protect the lead, but veteran defensive tackle Larry Cole stopped Riggins for a two-yard loss. Following the punt, Dallas took possession at its own 25-yard line and asked Staubach to travel 75 yards with the division title hanging in the balance. Staubach answered with a seven-play drive. He completed passes of 20 yards to Tony Hill and 22 and 25 yards to Preston Pearson, quickly moving the Cowboys into the red zone. From the Washington eight-yard line, Staubach lofted a pass to Hill for the winning touchdown with 39 seconds remaining. Rafael Septién converted the extra point to complete the 35-34 comeback. The drama continued after the final whistle. A funeral wreath had been delivered to the Cowboys before the game, apparently suggesting their season was about to die. Dallas players believed it had come from Washington supporters, although later accounts said a Cowboys fan had ordered it through a florist in Maryland. Harvey Martin carried the wreath to Washington’s locker room and threw it inside. From there the game got its enduring nickname. This game belongs on the countdown because it combined everything that defined the Cowboys-Washington rivalry. It was division-title stakes, hostility, controversy and an extraordinary finish. It was also the final victory of Staubach’s career. #Cowboys vs #Wasington 1979 The Wreath Game Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 35, Washington Redskins 34 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/kA5JkQ5cl9 — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 26, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game The funeral wreath thrown by Martin struck Washington kicker Mark Moseley’s knee, reportedly leaving a cut that required three stitches. Martin later apologized for his actions. title: 5 potential trade candidates for the Dallas Cowboys
summary: With just one remaining preseason game left to play against New Orleans Saints, the cutdown date for the Dallas Cowboys and the rest of the league to get under the 53-man roster is quickly approaching. That means tough decisions will have to be made about who receives a pink slip or which players could potentially […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - NOVEMBER 23: Marist Liufau #35 of the Dallas Cowboys looks on from the sideline during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images With just one remaining preseason game left to play against New Orleans Saints, the cutdown date for the Dallas Cowboys and the rest of the league to get under the 53-man roster is quickly approaching. That means tough decisions will have to be made about who receives a pink slip or which players could potentially become trade candidates. Today, we’ll take a look at a handful of players that Dallas could possibly trade away. LB Marist Liufau Dallas’ third-round pick in 2024 has gone from playing like a future starter as a rookie to quickly falling out of favor in just a few years time. He currently looks like a man without a position after being switched outside linebacker. His best bet to make it through roster cuts is his special teams ability, but even that may not be enough. While his value in Dallas has continued to nosedive, another team looking for LB help may think otherwise. If true, the Cowboys would be happy to receive a future late-round pick instead of cutting him. TE Luke Schoonmaker After losing the TE2 job to Brevyn Spann-Ford, Schoonmaker’s tumble down the depth chart looked inevitable with the emergence of Michael Trigg, but may be stalled/delayed for now. Trigg’s toe injury may get him stashed on IR in order to secure his services, saving Schoonmaker’s job. That doesn’t mean the Cowboys won’t or shouldn’t shop him though. He’s in the final year of his rookie deal with someone waiting in the wings to replace him. Maybe someone will part with a future pick on the former second-round TE. WR Camden Brown Would the Cowboys really part with a young, promising WR on a very team-friendly contract? For the right price, sure. Brown joined the Cowboys in an undrafted free agent, but has since put his name on the map with his performance in training camp and especially in preseason. Being buried on the depth chart he may not play much as a rookie even if he makes the roster, but could be part of the future depending on what happens with George Pickens. A future pick probably wouldn’t do it, but a player who would upgrade things elsewhere on the roster could possibly sway the Cowboys. OL T.J. Bass Bass is probably a starter on many team’s around the league, but with the Cowboys he is a depth piece, albeit an important one. He seems to be the contingency plan to start at guard if the Cowboys have nay issues there. Outside that, he’s just another backup who won’t see the field much. If the Cowboys like what they see and second-year OL Ajani Cornelius or maybe even Nick Leverett, trading Bass away could net them a future mid-round pick. Playing on a one-year deal it’s worth considering. QB Joe Milton The talent was always there, but it looks as if Milton has finally started to come into his own. So much so, he’s been playing like a future starter in preseason and QB-needy teams around the league have probably taken notice. With Sam Howell as a capable QB2, Dallas may want to try to strike while the iron is hot. Milton could potentially fetch a mid-round pick, which would be an improvement on the sixth-rounder they sent to the Patriots to acquire him in the first place. Trading away such talent would be hard, but potentially worth it. Would you trade any of these players? For how much? Which player did we miss that is a good trade candidate?

title: Broncos vs. Vikings: 3 players to watch in Week 3 of NFL preseason
summary: The Denver Broncos struggled in their 33-13 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 2 of the NFL preseason. This Friday, the Broncos will host the Minnesota Vikings in their preseason finale. It’s the last chance for a lot of players trying to make the final 53-man roster. Here are three players I’ll be […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - JULY 31: Defensive tackle Tyler Onyedim (98) of the Denver Broncos laughs with others before practice on Friday, July 31, 2026, at Broncos Park in Centennial, Colo.(Photo by Timothy Hurst/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images The Denver Broncos struggled in their 33-13 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 2 of the NFL preseason. This Friday, the Broncos will host the Minnesota Vikings in their preseason finale. It’s the last chance for a lot of players trying to make the final 53-man roster. Here are three players I’ll be watching closely in tomorrow night’s game. Justin Joly — Tight End Adam Trautman and Evan Engram will be the top duo at tight end for the Broncos this season. However, the battle for who gets the depth spots behind them is still underway. One player in the mix is rookie tight end Justin Joly, who the team drafted in the fifth round this past April. During his collegiate career, Joly was one of the most productive tight ends. He was a versatile player who played inline, on the move, as well as even lining up in the backfield on occasion. We haven’t seen much of that versatility yet through two preseason games. Thus far, Joly has been targeted three times this preseason. He has caught all three targets but only has 10 receiving yards. I’m hoping he gets a few more looks in the preseason finale versus the Vikings. In college, he performed well on middle of the field concepts and showcased a penchant for moving the chains on third down. It would be nice to see him get some targets down the field. Tyler Onyedim — Defensive Lineman The Denver Broncos boast an impressive four-man defensive line rotation with Zach Allen, D.J. Jones, Malcolm Roach, and Eyioma Uwazurike. Even without John Franklin-Myers in the fold, they should do a great job holding their own in the trenches. However, they will need one of their younger players on the roster to step up and be the key fifth man that can come in and get some meaningful playing time. A third-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Tyler Onyedim is one of those players in the mix. In his NFL debut against the Falcons, Onyedim saw just 23 snaps. Last week against the Packers, his snap count went up to 32 plays. Against the Vikings, I’d expect similar, if not a little bit more. Onyedim’s main competition for the spot is second-year defensive lineman Sai’vion Jones. Each have had similar playing time in the preseason, but neither has really stood out above the other. I’m interested to see if Onyedim can flash some of the promise and pass rushing traits that stood out during his collegiate career in the preseason finale on Friday. J.L. Skinner — Safety When the Broncos signed Taylor Rapp, they had presumably found their third safety in their rotation. However, he was released by the team yesterday. Head Coach Sean Payton hinted a reunion is likely down the road. But for now, that opens up the opportunity for another player to take that spot for the time being. Last year, the Broncos kept five safeties on the final 53-man roster. As of now, I’d say Devon Key is making the squad considering he was an All-Pro in the game’s third phase last season. The other player in the secondary I’m going to keep a close eye on is fourth-year player J.L. Skinner. Skinner has been a standout on special teams for Denver. He has logged 632 snaps there the past two seasons placing him in the top three amongst all Broncos players. However, the former sixth-round pick has very little experience on defense with just 54 snaps in game situations over the first three years of his career. I’m still enthralled with Skinner’s physical traits and upside based on how he stood out at Boise State. You can’t teach his size, and he made a lot of big plays in college. I think there is still a lot of untapped potential there and expect he will get a lot of playing time on Friday night. What about you, Broncos Country? What three players are you hoping to see perform well and flash in the preseason finale against the Vikings? Sound off in the comments section and let me know.

title: Sean Payton and Broncos set to make tough decisions as roster cutdown day looms
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country. The Denver Broncos preseason finale against the Minnesota Vikings is this Friday. For many players on the roster, their spots are safe and secure. Most of those veterans will likely be on the sidelines against the Vikings. They have nothing to prove and the Broncos certainly don’t need to risk an […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - AUGUST 3: Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos speaks during training camp at Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Monday, August 3, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country. The Denver Broncos preseason finale against the Minnesota Vikings is this Friday. For many players on the roster, their spots are safe and secure. Most of those veterans will likely be on the sidelines against the Vikings. They have nothing to prove and the Broncos certainly don’t need to risk an injury to a key starter. With respect to a handful of others, their performance against the Vikings will mean everything. It’s their last chance that could make or break their shot at earning a spot on this year’s Denver Broncos squad. After the game, Head Coach Sean Payton and the rest of the Broncos’ coaching staff will have some tough decisions to make. They will have until 6:00 PM (EST) on Sunday, August 30th to finalize their 53-man roster for the 2026 season. A bit of a curveball in the roster shakedown hit the media waves yesterday. Payton announced that Taylor Rapp had been released to address things on the home front. When he was signed, it was expected he would have the third safety role on lock. For now, he won’t be on the team’s roster to begin the season, though it was mentioned Rapp’s return to the team was likely. That opens up the door for one of Denver’s depth players to make the team. If not one of them, it could be someone off waivers from another team. Yesterday after practice, Payton spoke about some of the ways the team is formulating their plan to round out their roster prior to the deadline. Based on his statements, perusing the waiver wire will certainly be in play to build the best team possible for the upcoming season. “Once you find one or two, you’re addicted to trying to find them. It doesn’t have to be that type of player, it’s just whoever. It’s just someone that, in the perfect world, it’s that other team’s top practice squad player and so that’s the goal,” stated Payton. The Broncos will have ample collegiate and professional tape, as well as grades from their player personnel department to help navigate the process. While the team has a loaded roster at a lot of positions, there is no doubt they could use some help rounding out depth at several positions. Denver will also be using analytics to try and come up with a model that shows what types of players and what positions are most likely to be claimed off waivers. He admitted to reporters yesterday that will have a big impact on who will makes their team, as opposed to risking losing them by placing them on the 16-man practice squad. “I think that gets weighed in a lot. I’ll turn to the analytics and a lot of it is what kind of tape the opponents are seeing and that gets weighed in a lot. Who do we feel like is more likely to get claimed? Certain positions are more likely to get claimed. So that’s always a challenge,” added Payton. What do you think, Broncos Country? What are some of the toughest decisions the Broncos will have to make as cutdown day looms? Is there a certain position or two you feel Denver will kick the tires on a waiver wire claim as opposed to a player who has been battling it out through the offseason? Let me know in the comments section. As always, thank you for reading. Here is today’s slate of articles for Horse Tracks .

Payton told reporters he would not go through the roster telling them who will or will not play, but said Nix “probably will not […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - AUGUST 21: Bo Nix (10) of the Denver Broncos leads Sam Ehlinger (4) and Jarrett Stidham (8) onto the field before the game against the Green Bay Packers at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Friday, August 21, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton met with the media after today’s practice and was asked if Bo Nix and other starters would play in their preseason finale on Friday Night. Breaking: Bo Nix will probably NOT play in the team’s preseason finale on Friday, Sean Payton announced. Next time he’ll see the game field will be Week 1 on Monday Night Football against the Chiefs. pic.twitter.com/FkVc3yGreL — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 26, 2026 I am assuming that if Nix is not playing in the finale, we will not see many of the Broncos’ key starters suit up for the preseason opener on Friday Night. If Nix does not indeed play on Saturday Night, he will have sat out two of the three Broncos preseason games. However, in the one game he did play, he led the Broncos offense to a touchdown and then followed that up with a field goal. 10-points in limited action is a good enough sample size for me. With Nix likely not playing, we will likely see the Broncos’ backup quarterback competition continue. Veteran Jarrett Stidham had the start in the opener and was the first quarterback off the bench last week, so we’ll see if he gets the start or not vs. the Vikings. title: Safety Taylor Rapp is dealing with personal issues, and there’s a ‘better-than-good chance’ that he will be re-signed
summary: It was announced earlier this afternoon that the Denver Broncos have released veteran safety Taylor Rapp. This was weird because he just signed with the team a few days ago, and Payton and defensive coordinator Vance Joseph spoke highly of him to the media. This led to some confusion this afternoon in Broncos Country, but […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - OCTOBER 20: Taylor Rapp #9 of the Buffalo Bills looks on during the second quarter against the Tennessee Titans at Highmark Stadium on October 20, 2024 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was announced earlier this afternoon that the Denver Broncos have released veteran safety Taylor Rapp. This was weird because he just signed with the team a few days ago, and Payton and defensive coordinator Vance Joseph spoke highly of him to the media. This led to some confusion this afternoon in Broncos Country, but we now have our answer. Payton met with the media today after practice and told reporters that Rapp is dealing with personal issues and “needs some time at home.” However, he added that there’s a “better-than-good chance” that he will be back and re-signed with the team at some point. HC Sean Payton said the team met with safety Taylor Rapp and that he “needs some time at home.” Said a situation came up that needed to be addressed. Said that there’s a “better than good”chance that he’ll be back with the team at some point. — Aric DiLalla (@AricDiLalla) August 26, 2026 When he signed, it seemed like Rapp would be penciled in as the Broncos’ third safety. However, the sudden release was a surprise, especially after Payton’s comments a few days ago, but now we have an understanding of the situation Payton told reporters that Rapp was a player they liked and was available, and they wanted to work him out and sign him if possible. “Yes, [he’s a] veteran player we liked, had good grades on and just more talent at that position. It was really more… It wasn’t like us pounding the table, ‘We need a safety.’ It was, ‘Hey, this player’s available,’ and ‘Let’s work him out and sign him if possible.’ So I’m glad he’s here. We’ve had experience playing against him. He has real good football instincts and awareness that serves you well at that position. So I think it was more availability than necessity, if that makes sense.” Taylor Rapp is only 28 years old and is a former 2nd-round pick in the 2019 NFL Draft by the Los Angeles Rams. He is an experienced safety with plenty of starting experience who has spent time with the Rams and previously with the Buffalo Bills. During his seven seasons in the NFL, Rapp has appeared in 93 games and started 72 of them. Last season, he appeared in six games for the Buffalo Bills before a knee injury ended his season, and he was placed on the injured reserve. Throughout his career, Rapp has totaled 488 tackles, 11 tackles for a loss, 2 sacks, 12 interceptions, 31 pass deflections, and 2 forced fumbles. No timetable was given on when Rapp is expected to re-sign with the team, so it’ll be interesting to see how his pending return impacts their 53-man roster construction this coming weekend.

This news comes from NFL Network’s lead league insider Ian Rapoport. This is a […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - AUGUST 23: Taylor Rapp #9 of the Buffalo Bills runs onto the field prior to an NFL preseason football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on August 23, 2025 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, that was quick. After signing with the Broncos just a few days ago, the Broncos have now released veteran safety Taylor Rapp along with wide receiver Kyre Duplessis and have signed defensive tackle Israel Antwine and offensive tackle Foster Sarell. This news comes from NFL Network’s lead league insider Ian Rapoport. The #Broncos are making a couple roster moves ahead of their third preseason game, signing DT Israel Antwine and T Foster Sarell, per source. Newly signed safety Taylor Rapp was released and WR Kyre Duplessis was waived. — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) August 26, 2026 This is a bit of a surprise considering Payton’s comments on Rapp just a few days ago. As for Duplessis, he was signed after the Broncos were down multiple receivers due to injury and had little to no shot at making the roster or practice squad. With those two roster spots open, the Broncos have signed defensive tackle Israel Antwine and offensive tackle Foster Sarell. Antwine is a former undrafted free agent who spent time with the Jaguars, played in the CFL, and most recently in the UFL. In all likelihood, Antwine is simply a preseason body for the finale on Friday Night, but we’ll see if he can push for a practice squad spot during his short time with the team. As for Foster Sarell, he was just released by the Washington Commanders and has spent time with several teams, including the Baltimore Ravens, New York Giants, Los Angeles Chargers, and Washington Commanders. During his career, he has appeared in 41 games, all with the Chargers, and has 4 career starts. With Frank Crum dealing with an injury, it appears the Broncos have added some tackle depth ahead of their preseason finale. He is an experienced player, so he may have a shot at a practice squad spot, but it’ll be difficult to latch on after joining a team this late in the process. We’ll see how he does on Friday Night. As for the safety position, this changes things a bit again. It seemed like Rapp was penciled in as the third safety. He’s an experienced player, and head coach Sean Payton spoke highly of him just a few days ago. Now, with him suddenly released, it opens things back up for JL Skinner, Devon Key, Tycen Anderson, and rookie Miles Scott. I still wouldn’t rule out the team addressing the safety position prior to Week 1, but we’ll see how it goes in the coming days.

title: Detroit Lions sign CB Eric Scott Jr. on final day of training camp
summary: The Detroit Lions are holding their final training camp practice of the 2026 offseason on Thursday, but that doesn’t mean the front office is done trying to find solutions for the roster. The Lions still have one preseason game remaining, and with a few injuries in the secondary, they’ve signed corner Eric Scott Jr. to […]
full_text: Jul 22, 2025; St. Joseph, MO, USA; Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Eric Scott Jr. (45) walks down the hill to the practice fields during training camp at Missouri Western State University. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions are holding their final training camp practice of the 2026 offseason on Thursday, but that doesn’t mean the front office is done trying to find solutions for the roster. The Lions still have one preseason game remaining, and with a few injuries in the secondary, they’ve signed corner Eric Scott Jr. to their 90-man roster. Scott started his college career at Illinois State and worked his way up through Butler Community College to Southern Mississippi. He started the next two and a half seasons for the Golden Eagles and was selected by the Dallas Cowboys, who traded up into the sixth round of the 2023 NFL Draft to secure him. He made the roster as a rookie, but didn’t see the field as he was declared inactive each game. In 2024, the Cowboys waived Scott near the end of training camp, and the Kansas City Chiefs claimed him off waivers (ironically, the team the Cowboys traded with to draft Scott). Scott ended up on the Chiefs’ practice squad that season; then, the following training camp, he suffered an injury that forced him to injured reserve and cost him the 2025 season. Ahead of the Lions’ final training camp practice, coach Dan Campbell noted that he’s not sure if he’ll play his starters in the final preseason game (it’d be surprising if he did), and with a couple of injuries in the secondary—most notably Nick Whiteside at corner—adding a player like Scott could give the Lions the depth they need to close out the preseason. While the road to a spot on the roster is steep for Scott, there’s a chance for him to get some extended playing time and put some things on tape for the Lions and 31 other NFL teams. If he shows well, a spot on a team’s practice squad could be in his future. The Lions have not announced a corresponding move at this time.

title: NFL roster cuts: 4 rules you need to know and what they mean for Detroit Lions
summary: NFL roster cuts are right around the corner. By 6 p.m. ET on Sunday, Aug. 30, all teams must have their rosters reduced to the 53-man maximum. It’s a dark day in the NFL, and it involves some really tough decisions from front offices. Player talent will drive most of those decisions, but there are […]
full_text: From left, Detroit Lions team president and CEO Rod Wood, general manager Brad Holmes, and head coach Dan Campbell walk off the field after practice during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Monday, August 10, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co NFL roster cuts are right around the corner. By 6 p.m. ET on Sunday, Aug. 30, all teams must have their rosters reduced to the 53-man maximum. It’s a dark day in the NFL, and it involves some really tough decisions from front offices. Player talent will drive most of those decisions, but there are also some very important NFL guidelines that will guide NFL general managers and coaches as they trim rosters to 53 players. Here are four NFL rules you need to know, and how they may impact Detroit Lions roster cuts this year. Released vs. waived When a player is cut, they are either “released” or “waived,” depending on how long they’ve been in the NFL. If a player has four accrued seasons in the NFL, they are released. If they haven’t been in the league that length of time, they get waived. A player who is released has their contract fully terminated and is free to sign with any other team immediately. A player who is waived is subject to waivers, where any team can put in a claim for him. The team who puts in a claim with the highest waiver priority—set by the original 2026 NFL Draft order prior to trades—will be awarded the player and his current contract. If no team claims the player, they become an unrestricted free agent, free to sign anywhere. What it means for the Lions: Oftentimes, we see teams release a veteran player with an understanding that they’ll sign back with the team vs. cutting a young player who will be subject to waivers. For example, if the Lions were concerned about losing UDFA linebacker Erick Hunter while on waivers, they may have him make the 53-man roster. They could, instead, choose to release a veteran linebacker like Joe Bachie, but let him know they intend to re-sign him at a later date. As long as the player agrees to come back—which is certainly not guaranteed—there would be no risk. 2 IR-to-return spots available PRIOR to cuts If a player is placed on injured reserve right now, it means they are out for the year. The only way they could play again is if they are released with an injury settlement. That puts a lot of teams in a bind right now, because they are currently rostering players who have longer-term injuries, but won’t be out for the season. Rather than release these players, they are waiting to put them on the “regular season” IR list, where players can return to action after four weeks. Previously, these players would have to make the original 53-man roster, then be placed on IR, and backfill their roster spot. However, a few years ago, the NFL added a rule that lets teams place two players on IR on cutdown day and allows those players to return after a minimum of four games. What it means for the Lions: Cade Mays’ injury is expected to last at least another month, which means he will likely take up one of the two IR-to-return spots on cutdown day. Rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder could be a second. Thanks to this new rule, neither Mays nor Rolder would have to make the original 53-man roster. New practice rule for players on PUP This year features a new rule that will very likely impact the Lions. Here’s the exact wording of the rule: Permit players on Reserve/Physically Unable to Perform to begin a 21-day practice period after the club’s second game of the regular season. To summarize, prior to this rule, players who enter the season on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list would have to sit out the first four games of the regular season. That also means missing practices for those first four weeks. However, under the new rule, while players on reserve/PUP still must miss the first four games, they can start practicing after just two weeks, enabling those players to have a ramp-up period and potentially putting them in position to actually play in the team’s fifth game. What it means for the Lions: Detroit currently has two players who may start the season on reserve/PUP: Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph. The Lions may opt to remove them from the PUP list prior to the regular season (and therefore take up spots on the 53-man roster) because it sounds like their timeline is very close to returning to practice by Week 1 ; there is now incentive to save those roster spots. It would likely take both players at least a few weeks of practice to be game-ready anyways, so even if they made the 53-man roster, they likely wouldn’t be ready to play until Week 3 or 4 at the earliest. But with the new rule, Detroit can save two roster spots and still have Branch and Joseph ready by Week 5, if they’re physically good to go. Veteran guaranteed salary The “vested veteran” rule states that if a veteran player (four or more accrued seasons) is on the roster in Week 1, their salary becomes fully guaranteed. That has led some teams to circumvent that rule by releasing a player during roster cuts and signing them back to the roster in Week 2. It’s not the most player-friendly tactic, but for teams in financial strain, it’s a way to save a few bucks. What this means for the Lions: Obviously, the Lions will likely only do this in extreme cases. They have to be willing to be without that player for the opening week, and it wouldn’t be worth it if the player already has significant salary guarantees on the books. While I don’t think Detroit will go down this route, players that fall into those categories include Khalil Dorsey ($0 salary guarantees), Josh Dobbs ($375,000), Tom Kennedy ($0), Ben Stille ($0), Trevor Nowaske ($395,000).

title: Detroit Lions mailbag: Is the defense finally good?
summary: The Detroit Lions defense has been on display this preseason. They’ve had the edge on the offense for most of training camp, and in the two preseason games, they’ve held opponents to just 22 total points. On Wednesday, coach Dan Campbell even expressed his confidence in the defense’s front seven. “I feel really good with […]
full_text: Detroit Lions defensive tackle Alim McNeill (54), right, and defensive end Aidan Hutchinson (97) walk off the field after practice during OTAs at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Friday, May 29, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions defense has been on display this preseason. They’ve had the edge on the offense for most of training camp, and in the two preseason games, they’ve held opponents to just 22 total points. On Wednesday, coach Dan Campbell even expressed his confidence in the defense’s front seven. “I feel really good with where our D-line is at right now and really that front seven,” Campbell said. “I feel that group of guys, plus the bench. I feel really good, man. I feel like it’s a good group. It’s a versatile group. There’s depth in there. There are pieces. You can ask them to do different jobs. And so yeah, you’re asking me right now, I feel really good about it.” But we’ve been fooled before. The secondary looked incredible during the 2025 preseason and training camp, then fell off when the regular season started. This isn’t the first time the defense has looked ahead of the offense, and it’s almost always been the offense that ends up looking better. Plus, how much can we really tell from practices and the preseason? The defensive line has undoubtedly been playing well in August, but they’ve been going against a Lions offensive line that is still a work in progress, and two preseason teams with serious questions on their offensive line. And as Campbell was quick to point out, the true test is when the regular season starts. “Until we get in a real game that really counts, real minutes, New Orleans will be our first big barometer,” Campbell said. “That’s when we’ll really know where we’re at.” But is it okay to start believing now? Are there signs this training camp that the defensive improvement is for real? Are some of the new things the Lions defense is doing this year going to translate into much better production for the 2026 season? Erik Schlitt and I discuss reasons for and against optimism for Detroit’s defense at length in this week’s Midweek Mailbag podcast. Other topics on the show include: How much could Christian Izien’s injury impact the Week 1 secondary Is the offensive line worse off than last year? Which veterans could be cut and brought back? Should we start worrying about Isiah Pacheco? How much run defense can we expect from Derrick Moore, Skyler Gill-Howard? Why is special teams so important? What makes it so hard for good players on offense/defense to play on special teams? Who could be the last 2-4 players out on roster cuts? How do the Lions’ superstars look in training camp thus far? Catch the entire episode on whatever your favorite podcasting platform is, or use the Spotify embed below. As always, you can also catch video of the Midweek Mailbag over on YouTube or Twitch , which also features a bunch of bonus content.

title: Discussion: Who has been the biggest surprise of Detroit Lions training camp?
summary: On Thursday, Detroit Lions training camp will come to a close. It’s been a busy month, with players shooting up and down the depth chart, injuries forcing the Lions’ hands, and some late additions who have made strong cases for the 53-man roster. Yet, despite the furious amount of information coming Detroit’s way, their front […]
full_text: Detroit Lions defensive end Ahmed Hassanein (99) practices during OTAs at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, June 11, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co On Thursday, Detroit Lions training camp will come to a close. It’s been a busy month, with players shooting up and down the depth chart, injuries forcing the Lions’ hands, and some late additions who have made strong cases for the 53-man roster. Yet, despite the furious amount of information coming Detroit’s way, their front office will have just 72 hours following their final training camp practice to decide which players will make the 53-man roster and who will be on the outside. “This is difficult,” coach Dan Campbell said on Wednesday. “So, you have got to have a pretty good idea where you’re at before you go into that (preseason) game, knowing there are a few spots left. But you better have a pretty good idea because it’s a quick turnaround.” Despite there being one more practice left, let’s look at the entirety of training camp and decide… Who has been the biggest surprise of Detroit Lions training camp? My answer: I’m going to list my top three. WR Tay Martin Martin is the leading candidate for the Lions’ WR5 job. Now, he’s been aided by some unfortunate injuries (Kendrick Law, Cedrick Wilson), but he also deserves a ton of credit. The player our staff ranked literally 90th out of 90 players (I had him 88th), we clearly underestimated Martin’s productivity in the UFL this year (42 catches, 483 yards) and his skill set on special teams. EDGE Ahmed Hassanein Hassanein has always been a great story and an intriguing player, but realistic expectations for him in 2026—after missing most of his rookie season with an injury—were that he would be a fringe roster bubble player who would mostly play on special teams this season. Instead, he’s been fantastic for nearly all of training camp and has worked his way into roster-lock territory. He’s now expected to play some sort of defensive role on gamedays, and he’s just scratching the surface while he continues to learn the nuances of the big end position. QB Luke Altmyer I had very little expectations for an undrafted rookie quarterback. Not because of anything Altmyer did in college, but because the Lions have almost always preferred their backup to be a veteran. Even before Teddy Bridgewater’s sudden retirement, Altmyer looked like he could push for the job with steady play, decent accuracy, and a good enough arm. Now with Bridgewater’s retirement and a slow start from Josh Dobbs, we’re near a very real reality where Altmyer could be Jared Goff’s backup on Day 1. title: 9 standouts from Day 18 of Detroit Lions training camp
summary: Wednesday’s practice was originally planned to be a more intense session, potentially even a scrimmage. However, Dan Campbell opted to be smart with the workload after the team was “humming yesterday in a good way,” electing to dial things back for a one-hour practice in shells. The practice was still competitive, but given its concise […]
full_text: ALLEN PARK, MICHIGAN - JULY 29: Amon-Ra St. Brown #14 of the Detroit Lions looks on during Detroit Lions Training Camp at Detroit Lions Meijer Performance Center on July 29, 2026 in Allen Park, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images Wednesday’s practice was originally planned to be a more intense session, potentially even a scrimmage. However, Dan Campbell opted to be smart with the workload after the team was “humming yesterday in a good way,” electing to dial things back for a one-hour practice in shells. The practice was still competitive, but given its concise nature, limited team periods—with each offense getting only three drives—and lack of full contact, there weren’t a substantial number of notable plays. Throw in a sloppy number of penalties, and the takeaways from Wednesday should be taken with a pinch of salt. With that in mind, here are nine somewhat notable standouts—and their rep situations—from Wednesday’s practice. Offense WR Amon-Ra St. Brown — St. Brown broke loose for an impressive 32-yard catch-and-run touchdown over the middle on a fourth down, play-action pass, then opened the end-of-game scenario with a 15-yard reception on a crosser. He was also part of a nearly flawless trick play that converted on fourth down but unfortunately ran out the clock to end the scenario. St. Brown continues to feast in the intermediate middle of the field. RB Jahmyr Gibbs — With the practice heavy on play-action and end-of-game situations, there weren’t many opportunities for Gibbs in the run game. But on two of his three carries, Gibbs turned bottled-up outside zone runs into gains of 9 and 8 yards, cutting backside on a dime and weaving through the defense, including past Aidan Hutchinson on one run (Hutchinson beat Blake Miller for a sack on the very next play). Gibbs also added a 7-yard reception near the sideline during the end-of-game scenario while lined up out wide. During warmups, he snagged a rocket from Jared Goff on an angle route that made my eyeballs go full Looney Tunes. LG Ben Bartch — Bartch handled the full workload at left guard with both the second- and third-team offensive lines as he’s finally able to get doused in the reps that were originally intended for him. With one competitive practice and the final preseason game remaining, Bartch has an opportunity to earn the coaching staff’s trust as the primary backup at offensive guard. WR Tay Martin — Martin is fighting to secure a spot on the 53-man roster and looking to move past his drop in Saturday’s preseason game. He became an outlet for back-to-back Luke Altmyer completions, first on a drag route that Devin White diagnosed well and limited to 6 yards, then on a 17-yard reception over the middle to move the chains after beating Khalil Dorsey in coverage. Defense DE Eric O’Neill — O’Neill feels like he’s pulled ahead of Anthony Lucas as the most likely defensive end to be stashed on the practice squad and followed up his strong training camp with another active practice. He sniffed out a pitch to Sione Vaki for a run stop and later drove Devin Cochran back into Altmeyer, forcing a fluttering incompletion that appeared a split-second away from potentially becoming a forced fumble. DL Ben Stille — Another day, another Stille splash play. Stille combined with Amen Ogbongbemiga for a sack of Altmyer that forced the offense into a very long third down. Stille continues to prove his value despite joining the team after training camp began and remains one of Detroit’s biggest roster-bubble decisions. LB Malcolm Rodriguez — Rodriguez received all of the third-linebacker reps with the first-team defense Wednesday, while White was relegated to reps with the second team. How that situation is handled during Thursday’s practice, and the final preseason game, will be telling. Rodriguez also delivered a strong block during the 3-on-2 kick-return gauntlet drill that elicited a big reaction from the coaches and players gathered around. DB Keith Abney II — Abney received all of the nickelback snaps Wednesday with both the first- and second-team defenses, as the coaching staff appears to be loading him up with reps in preparation for Week 1 with Christian Izien possibly out . Abney also helped end the second-team defense’s end-of-game scenario, generating pressure on a nickel blitz during a 20-plus-yard fourth-down Hail Mary and forcing an inaccurate pass. S Aamaris Brown — With several injuries at safety, Brown received all of the first-team reps as the third safety, operating as a half-field deep safety during the obvious passing situations that was the end-of-game scenario. Brown also chased down Jameson Williams on the fourth down trick play, stopping him inside the 10-yard line and short of the goal line.

title: Lions training camp injury report: 2 EDGEs miss practice
summary: The Detroit Lions scaled back training camp practice on Wednesday after coach Dan Campbell said they were “humming” during Tuesday’s practice. That was reflected on the injury report, where a few Lions returned from injury, but we also saw a couple of new faces out. Returned to practice: Small made a step toward returning to […]
full_text: Detroit Lions edge Ahmed Hassanein(99) during OTAs at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Friday, May 29, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions scaled back training camp practice on Wednesday after coach Dan Campbell said they were “humming” during Tuesday’s practice. That was reflected on the injury report, where a few Lions returned from injury, but we also saw a couple of new faces out. Returned to practice: RB Jabari Small (concussion) OL Miles Frazier (undisclosed) DB Nick Whiteside (undisclosed) Small made a step toward returning to action on Wednesday, suiting up for Detroit’s short practice. The running back took part in positional drills, but when team drills began, he ran sprints with a trainer for the rest of practice. Small is still in contention for the Lions’ RB4 job with Jacob Saylors, so if he can recover quickly enough to play in Saturday’s preseason finale, he could still make a case for the spot. Fraizer, too, was held out of team drills, but he was back after missing a practice. His left leg not only has a brace on it, but also a pretty significant wrap. To accommodate his absence, the Lions had Devin Cochran run double duty at left tackle with the backups and third stringers, and Ben Bartch work with the second and third teams at left guard. Whiteside was back after leaving Tuesday’s practice early. With the Lions so shorthanded at cornerback, most of his work on Wednesday was at safety with the second-team defense. Not practicing: RB Isiah Pacheco (knee) OT Giovanni Manu (NFI) C Cade Mays (wrist) G Michael Niese (leg) EDGE Payton Turner (back) EDGE Derrick Moore (unknown) EDGE Ahmed Hassanein (unknown) LB Jimmy Rolder (leg) LB Trevor Nowaske (leg) S Thomas Harper (ankle) S Christian Izien (undisclosed) S Kerby Joseph (PUP, knee) S Brian Branch (PUP, Achilles) Detroit was without both Derrick Moore and Ahmed Hassanein on the edge. There is currently no explanation for their absences, as they did not appear to leave Tuesday’s practice early. We’ll see if they are back out there for Thursday’s training camp finale. Coach Dan Campbell offered an encouraging update on Trevor Nowaske after he left Tuesday’s practice early. “We think it’s just a little strain or sprain,” Campbell said. “So, I think we’ll be okay here, let it calm down, so I’m not as worried about that.” He sounded a little more worried about safety Christian Izien, who could miss the team’s opening game against the New Orleans Saints in just over two weeks. “It’ll probably be a little bit here,” Campbell said. “I don’t know if we’ll have him for the opener or not, but we’ll have him. I mean, we’re going to get him here. If it’s not then, we’ll get him here early in the season at some point.”

title: Lions injury updates: Christian Izien could miss season opener
summary: Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell provided a couple of brief injury updates ahead of their penultimate training camp practice, and it’s mostly good news. Defensive back Christian Izien, who is in competition for the starting nickel job and is also depth at safety, suffered an injury recently and missed Tuesday’s practice. Campbell would not specify […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - AUGUST 13: Christian Izien #27 of the Detroit Lions warms up prior to a preseason game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell provided a couple of brief injury updates ahead of their penultimate training camp practice, and it’s mostly good news. Defensive back Christian Izien, who is in competition for the starting nickel job and is also depth at safety, suffered an injury recently and missed Tuesday’s practice. Campbell would not specify what the injury is, and he said Izien could miss the season opener, but not much beyond. “It’ll probably be a little bit here. I don’t know if we’ll have him for the opener or not. But we’ll have him,” Campbell said. “We’re going to get him here; if it’s not then, we’ll get him here early in the season at some point.” Izien’s absence will certainly hurt a defensive backfield that is currently going through some injury issues. Starting safeties Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch continue to trend toward starting the season on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list, Thomas Harper is expected to miss another week of practice, and Nick Whiteside has been battling some injuries as of late. The better news comes about reserve linebacker Trevor Nowaske, who left Tuesday’s practice during individual drills. Detroit will play it safe with the veteran linebacker, but they aren’t concerned about him missing time. “We think it’s just a little sprain or strain,” Campbell said. “So I think we’ll be okay here, let it calm down. So I’m not as worried about that.” Nowaske has been one of the Lions’ core special teamers over the last few years. In the last two seasons combined, he has 590 special teams snaps on top of another 406 on defense. We’ll have a more comprehensive injury report after Wednesday’s training camp practice.

title: Packers RB Josh Jacobs charged with battery and criminal damage to property
summary: The Brown County District Attorney’s Office announced on Thursday that the county has officially charged Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs after he was initially arrested for a domestic abuse complaint back in May. Jacobs was let out of county jail after a short stint this spring, as the county continued to investigate the […]
full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JUNE 09: Josh Jacobs #8 of the Green Bay Packers participates in drills during the Green Bay Packers mandatory minicamp at Don Hutson Center on June 09, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Brown County District Attorney’s Office announced on Thursday that the county has officially charged Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs after he was initially arrested for a domestic abuse complaint back in May . Jacobs was let out of county jail after a short stint this spring, as the county continued to investigate the situation before officially charging Jacobs with a crime. Per the DA, Jacobs is now charged with two misdemeanors: one count of battery and one count of criminal damage to property. During his May arrest, Jacobs had five charges on the books: battery — domestic abuse, criminal damage to property — domestic abuse, disorderly conduct — domestic abuse, strangulation and suffocation (one charge) and intimidation of a victim. According to The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero , the NFL is “monitoring all developments in the matter,” but the league has not announced a ruling on whether or not Jacobs will or won’t be suspended at some point during the 2026 season. The NFL doesn’t necessarily have to decide on the Jacobs situation right this second, as they tend to want to gather all possible information about a potential suspension before ruling one way or another.

title: Green Bay Packers to sign TE Jonnu Smith
summary: NFL insider Jordan Schultz is reporting that the Green Bay Packers are signing tight end Jonnu Smith, who has previous experience playing for Packers head coach Matt LaFleur when they were together with the Tennessee Titans. This report has been confirmed by other news breakers like ESPN’s Adam Schefter. Smith will join the Packers on […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 28: Jonnu Smith #81 of the Pittsburgh Steelers warms up prior to a game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on December 28, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images NFL insider Jordan Schultz is reporting that the Green Bay Packers are signing tight end Jonnu Smith , who has previous experience playing for Packers head coach Matt LaFleur when they were together with the Tennessee Titans. This report has been confirmed by other news breakers like ESPN’s Adam Schefter. Smith will join the Packers on a one-year deal, according to reports, as the former Pro Bowl tight end just turned 31 years old. Smith has been a part-time starter over the last four seasons, each with a different team: the New England Patriots, the Atlanta Falcons, the Miami Dolphins and the Pittsburgh Steelers. In total, the Packers will be Team #7 for Smith in his NFL career. Smith’s playing style is that of a hybrid ball-in-hand tight end-fullback, as he tends to be off the ball more than in an in-line position. What makes this addition interesting is that the Packers are likely to keep Tucker Kraft (who has been discussed as starting the season on a pitch count) and Josh Whyle (who is also in a similar mold as Smith), with Luke Musgrave starting the season on the physically unable to perform list with a neck injury. Smith’s addition likely displaces Drake Dabney on the 53-man roster, but the Packers may still go shopping for a true Y behind Kraft, something they lack right now, with Whyle’s roster spot after cutdowns. The FIU product is a vested veteran, meaning that his salary will be fully guaranteed once he makes Green Bay’s roster in Week 1. Notably, Smith hasn’t been a special teams contributor, as he’s played just five snaps in the kicking game over the last three seasons, compared to 1,815 snaps on offense. So far, there have been no contract details to the Smith signing, other than it’s a one-year contract.

title: Green Bay Packers News: Keisean Nixon is going to play. A lot.
summary: There’s a version of the Keisean Nixon conversation that has been playing on loop in the greater Packers chattersphere: He misses a tackle, gets flagged, gives up a completion, or maybe shows poor effort in a preseason game, and suddenly the question becomes why the Packers keep him around at all. That criticism isn’t entirely […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - JANUARY 10: Keisean Nixon #25 of the Green Bay Packers lines up against Rome Odunze #15 of the Chicago Bears during the first half of a NFC Wild Card Playoff game on January 10, 2026 at Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Melissa Tamez/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images There’s a version of the Keisean Nixon conversation that has been playing on loop in the greater Packers chattersphere: He misses a tackle, gets flagged, gives up a completion, or maybe shows poor effort in a preseason game, and suddenly the question becomes why the Packers keep him around at all. That criticism isn’t entirely unfair. Nixon does have flaws, and his 2025 season included enough maddening moments to make fan frustration quite understandable. The Packers themselves have made it clear that his role isn’t entirely guaranteed, particularly after adding second-round pick Brandon Cisse and veteran Benjamin St-Juste. But there’s a giant gap between “Nixon isn’t a great corner” and “Nixon isn’t a starting-caliber NFL corner.” Nixon started all 17 games last season and played over a thousand snaps on the outside. He also led Green Bay in pass breakups and earned Pro Bowl alternate recognition (you can take or leave that last point). The point is, that’s not the résumé of a player who should be treated as a liability every time he steps on the field. In fact, the latest evidence suggests the Packers still see lots of value in Nixon. ESPN’s Rob Demovsky reported Wednesday that Nixon had fought his way back into the top cornerback mix after spending stretches with the second- and third-team defense earlier in camp. For any fans getting annoyed at my prattling on, here’s what’s bugging me: there aren’t enough true CB1s for every team. Several teams have one, but most teams have zero. The cornerback room specifically is a hard one to fill with top tier talent. You might be able to find a very slight edge via trade. Maybe. But certainly not in free agency. Prime Ja is not walking through that door. Maybe Nixon shouldn’t be Green Bay’s unquestioned top corner. Maybe Cisse proves he’s better. Maybe St-Juste surprises us (unlikely-ish). But Nixon is a serviceable starting corner on an NFL roster, and the Packers are going to need him. He’ll play outside. He’ll move around. He’ll contribute on special teams. He’ll probably play a whole lot more football than a certain subset of Packers fans may prefer. And I think that’s okay. Nobody is pretending Nixon is a shutdown corner. But having a serviceable starting corner in a league where every team is making roster compromises, isn’t the worst place to be. And if you think it is, wait until our depth is tested at some point this season. 2026 Green Bay Packers training camp: Latest intel, updates Keisean Nixon made one of his biggest plays of camp with a leaping interception of Jordan Love, as he appears to be back in the fight for a starting cornerback job. Packers’ Keisean Nixon feud with Cardinals WR resurfaces Keisean Nixon and Michael Wilson brought some history into Wednesday’s joint practice. WATCH: Gutekunst talks Kraft extension A sunbaked Packers GM addressed the media recently, talking about TE Tucker Kraft’s recovery and potential contract extension. title: The Packers’ Disney Draft Pick vs. Every Opponent on the 2026 Schedule
summary: With the big game set to air on ABC and ESPN in February, the NFL announced a collaboration with Disney as part of Disney and ESPN’s “Year of the Super Bowl.” The press release shares that the organizations teamed up with Champion and Fanatics for a “draft” that paired a Disney-owned icon with each NFL […]
full_text: Chewbacca poses on May 15, 2018 during a photocall for the film "Solo : A Star Wars Story" at the 71st edition of the Cannes Film Festival in Cannes, southern France. (Photo by Anne-Christine POUJOULAT / AFP) (Photo by ANNE-CHRISTINE POUJOULAT/AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images With the big game set to air on ABC and ESPN in February, the NFL announced a collaboration with Disney as part of Disney and ESPN’s “Year of the Super Bowl.” The press release shares that the organizations teamed up with Champion and Fanatics for a “draft” that paired a Disney-owned icon with each NFL team. The Green Bay Packers drafted the one and only Chewbacca, the tall, furry Wookiee from Star Wars who’s originally from the planet Kashyyyk, home of the (you guessed it) Wookiees. He’s most known as Han Solo’s co-pilot on the Millennium Falcon and the one member of that crew who didn’t get a medal for his service to the Rebellion ( until way too late ). Chewy was the choice for the Packers because he’s “loyal to the cause in the cold, snow, sleet and rain,” according to the press release. “Whether it’s Hoth or Lambeau, Chewbacca stays until the job is done.” While this is purely for merchandising purposes , I began to wonder how Chewy would do against the rest of the team’s icons on their schedule this season. And thus, this article was born! I am admittedly limited in my knowledge of Wookiees, but I did some research to gauge how powerful Chewy is. His biggest strength is, well, his strength, and stature at a towering 7’6” tall. He has increased stamina and durability, is highly intelligent, and is considered an expert marksman. His weapon of choice is a “ bowcaster ” aka a laser crossbow. Week 1: @ Minnesota Vikings Opponent: Thor Location: Asgard Result: L Record: 0-1 This is a brutal way to open the season for Chewy. Going up against the God of Thunder in Asgard? Sorry, he is not winning this. Even Thor without his hammer (Mjölnir) is taking him down. Week 2: @ New York Jets Opponent: Buzz Lightyear Location: Andy’s Room Result: W Record: 1-1 Chewy’s absolutely stomping on that toy in 3.5 seconds. Even if Buzz was able to fly (which he’s not because it’s “falling with style”) it’d just look like a scene from King Kong, with Chewy just swatting him out of the sky like a mosquito. No chance Buzz even lasts one minute in this fight, even with home-field advantage. Hiding under Andy’s bed? Think again, Chewy’s picking it up and tossing that sucker out the window and squashing that plastic spaceman like a bug. Week 3: vs. Atlanta Falcons Opponent: Millennium Falcon Location: Kashyyyk Result: L Record: 1-2 Alright, this is the weirdest one on the schedule. This matchup sort of implies the ship is somehow sentient, so Chewy might have a problem on his hands. Chewy’s laser crossbow is no match for the guns on that ship. That ship has taken a beating over the years, so I think it could handle a fight with a Wookiee. If he managed to somehow get inside of it and make it self-destruct, maybe that can happen. However, with the ship’s ability to fly, I don’t see that happening. Tough L to be taken down by your own ship. Week 4: @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers Opponent: Captain Hook Location: Neverland Result: W Record: 2-2 Chewy’s back at .500 after taking down Captain Hook in Week 4. This is a 1-on-1 fight, so while Captain Hook can have his ship, the Jolly Roger, he won’t have his crew. I cannot imagine Captain Hook being smart or quick enough to go up against Chewy. Plus, Captain Hook can’t even defeat a bunch of kids with his crew. He’s not taking down a 7-foot space alien with a laser crossbow, sorry. Week 5: vs. Chicago Bears Opponent: Baloo Location: Kashyyyk Result: W Record: 3-2 While fighting a full-grown bear wouldn’t be easy, we’re talking about Baloo here. He attempted to fight the tiger Shere Khan in The Jungle Book and got absolutely embarrassed . He’s not a fighter, which is part of his charm, so I don’t see how he’s going to defeat Chewy, especially on Kashyyyk, a foreign jungle to him. Week 6: vs Dallas Cowboys Opponent: Woody Location: Kashyyyk Result: W Record: 4-2 If the fight against Buzz lasts 3.5 seconds, this one is lasting 1.5 seconds. I’m sorry, Woody, but you’re not getting out of this one. You’d be better off back at Sid’s place than fighting a Wookiee on Kashyyyk. Week 7: @ Detroit Lions Opponent: Simba Location: Pride Rock Result: L Record: 4-3 This was a close one. This one came down to home-field advantage for me. Chewy could win this if he’s able to get a good shot with his bowcaster on Simba. However, I think being in an unfamiliar place with an animal that’s known for its hunting skills could put Chewy at a disadvantage. I think it’s close overall, but ultimately Simba gets The High Ground and is able to take him down. Week 8: vs Carolina Panthers Opponent: Bagheera Location: Kashyyyk Result: W Record: 5-3 Bagheera is probably one of the tougher opponents Chewy will face this season, especially given his speed and agility. But this fight is taking place on Kashyyyk, where Chewy knows the terrain and has the home-field advantage. I think that’s enough to give him the edge. Week 9: @ New England Patriots Opponent: Captain America Location: Avengers Campus Result: L Record: 5-4 Captain America is taking Week 9. They are both fighters, however, Cap has more refined combat skills along with the speed and agility of a super soldier. While Chewy has super strength, Cap’s durability and stamina would be a problem because he “ can do this all day ”. Chewy has the blaster, but that would more than likely backfire since Cap has the vibranium shield that could just deflect it back to him. Sorry, Chewy, but America’s Ass takes the cake. Week 10: vs. Minnesota Vikings Opponent: Thor Location: Kashyyyk Result: L Record: 5-5 Home-field advantage doesn’t even move the needle in this one. Chewy doesn’t stand a chance. Chewy’s gonna need to “assemble” his pride back together after back-to-back whoopings by the Avengers. (please laugh, I have a family to feed.) Week 11: BYE WEEK Week 12: @ Los Angeles Rams Opponent: Sulley Location: Monsters, Inc. in Monstropolis Result: W Record: 6-5 After a full week of rest, Chewy is likely looking for some revenge and poor Sulley is going to face the wrath of a scorned Wookiee. While Sulley is similar in size, he’s a scarer but doesn’t actually have much, if any, fighting experience. His scare tactics ( zing! ) aren’t likely to work on Chewy, who has been in enough battles and faced real life-threatening scenarios. Week 13: @ New Orleans Opponent: Louie from The Princess and the Frog Location: Louisiana Bayou Result: W Record: 7-5 Chewy’s got this one in the bag. While an alligator in a bayou deep in Louisiana sounds terrifying, Louie isn’t exactly a fearsome character. He’s really only interested in playing jazz on his trumpet and has little fighting experience. Chewy, meanwhile, has spent his life fighting and surviving in dangerous environments. I think he takes this one easily. Week 14: vs. Buffalo Bills Opponent: Beast Location: Kashyyyk Result: W Record: 8-5 Beast is another opponent that matches Chewy’s size and fuzzy appearance, and he’s certainly no pushover. He was able to take on a pack of wolves, but we’re talking about a trained Wookiee warrior. Beast has the strength, but Chewy has the battle experience. It would be one of the tougher fights for Chewy, but ultimately, I think that experience prevails once again. Week 15: vs. Miami Dolphins Opponent: King Triton Location: Kashyyyk Result: L Record: 8-6 If this was in Green Bay or Hoth, Chewy’s got this one. However, King Triton definitely beats Chewy on Kashyyyk, despite home-field advantage. Kashyyyk does have oceans, so Triton wouldn’t have any issues surviving the terrain. But according to Greek mythology, Triton is a son of Poseidon. And if The Odyssey taught me anything, it’s that Poseidon won’t let you just mess with one of his kids without some seriously…

title: Colts activate Alec Pierce off PUP list
summary: The Indianapolis Colts got an important piece of their offense back Thursday, activating wide receiver Alec Pierce off the physically unable to perform list. Pierce had been sidelined throughout training camp after undergoing ankle surgery in March. His return to practice does not necessarily mean he is fully back to his normal role yet, but […]
full_text: WESTFIELD, IN - AUGUST 20: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce (14) watches a drill during the Indianapolis Colts and Atlanta Falcons joint training camp practice on August 20, 2026 at the Grand Park Sports Campus in Westfield, IN. (Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts got an important piece of their offense back Thursday, activating wide receiver Alec Pierce off the physically unable to perform list. Pierce had been sidelined throughout training camp after undergoing ankle surgery in March. His return to practice does not necessarily mean he is fully back to his normal role yet, but it is still a significant step as the Colts continue preparing for their regular-season opener against the Baltimore Ravens. Pierce is expected to ramp up gradually, and the goal is for him to be ready for Week 1. After missing valuable time with Daniel Jones and the starting offense during camp, every rep he can get between now and the opener becomes important. Pierce’s ankle situation had been one of the more frustrating storylines of camp. The injury bothered him last season, and after a platelet-rich plasma injection did not produce the desired result, Pierce and the Colts decided surgery was the best path forward. The goal was to address the soreness rather than have him play through the same issue again in 2026. That decision now appears to have put him in position to return before the regular season, which is a major boost for an offense that needs him. The Colts re-signed Pierce in March to a four-year, $114 million extension, making it clear they view him as one of the key pieces of their passing game. That became even more important after Indianapolis traded Michael Pittman Jr. to the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier in the offseason. With Pittman gone, Pierce is expected to take on a larger role as one of the featured receivers in the offense alongside Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and tight end Tyler Warren. Pierce earned that opportunity with the best season of his career in 2025. He surpassed 1,000 receiving yards for the first time, finishing with 1,003 yards on 47 catches. He also led the NFL in yards per catch for the second straight season, averaging 21.3 yards per reception and continuing to establish himself as one of the league’s premier vertical threats. That explosiveness is exactly what the Colts need back in the lineup. Pierce changes how defenses have to play Indianapolis because of his ability to stretch the field and punish single coverage. His chemistry with Jones will be something to monitor, especially after the missed camp time, but getting him off PUP gives the Colts a chance to build that connection before the games count. There is still some caution here. Being activated does not automatically mean Pierce is ready for a full workload, and the Colts will likely be conservative with his ramp-up. Still, after weeks of uncertainty, Pierce is finally back on the practice field, and his Week 1 outlook looks much more encouraging than it did earlier in camp.

title: Colts announce arguably anticipated move at cornerback
summary: The Indianapolis Colts announced on Wednesday that the team has waived cornerback Mekhi Blackmon and signed fellow cornerback Kenneth Harris in a corresponding roster move. As a former 2023 3rd round pick of the Minnesota Vikings, the 27-year-old Blackmon was traded to the Colts last late August for a 2026 6th round pick ahead of […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - DECEMBER 28: Mekhi Blackmon #29 of the Indianapolis Colts looks on from the sideline during an NFL football game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Lucas Oil Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts announced on Wednesday that the team has waived cornerback Mekhi Blackmon and signed fellow cornerback Kenneth Harris in a corresponding roster move. As a former 2023 3rd round pick of the Minnesota Vikings, the 27-year-old Blackmon was traded to the Colts last late August for a 2026 6th round pick ahead of the former’s final 53-man roster cuts. For a banged up Colts cornerback room, he ended up playing reasonably well in relief last season, recording 64 tackles (50 solo), a sack, 2 interceptions, and 7 passes defensed during 17 games (11 starts) in Indianapolis. However, Blackmon struggled mightily in coverage through his two preseason games, having a handful of defensive penalties. Had Blackmon remained halfway decent through preseason, he’s still probably on the Colts final 53-man roster—at least until final cuts came in early next week. As his replacement, the Colts signed Kenneth Harris, who is a 6,’0”, 192 pound undrafted rookie cornerback out of Oklahoma State and Arkansas State that largely spent this offseason with the New England Patriots ( via Colts.com ): “Harris, 6-0, 192 pounds, participated in the New England Patriots’ 2026 offseason program and training camp. He was originally signed by the Patriots as an undrafted free agent on May 8, 2026. Collegiately, Harris played in 59 career games (29 starts) at Oklahoma State (2023-25) and Arkansas State (2020-22) and compiled 113 tackles (92 solo), 61.5 tackles for loss, 1.0 sack, 28 passes defensed and three interceptions. In 2025, he saw action in 12 games (11 starts) and totaled 33 tackles (27 solo), 2.0 tackles for loss, 1.0 sack and five passes defensed.” This is likely one of those situations where after his incredibly rough preseason showing to-date, the Colts already knew they weren’t keeping Blackmon, so they’re giving him a head start to find a job elsewhere while finding another option for defensive back depth. Although at this late stage of preseason, Harris faces a really uphill battle to make the Colts’ final 53-man roster, he could still be a potential option to be re-signed to the team’s practice squad if he performs well during the upcoming preseason finale. The bottom of the Colts roster remains entirely fluid right now.
