title: Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence looks to better simulate scrambles in training camp
summary: For the first time this year at Jacksonville Jaguars training camp, Trevor Lawrence rushed for a touchdown. Granted, Lawrence hasn’t had many opportunities to run the football this summer. Quarterback safety is a priority to begin with, and the NFL’s current practice rules don’t allow for many live reps, either. “It’s extremely challenging,” offensive coordinator […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 19: Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars talks with Grant Udinski offensive coordinator of the Jacksonville Jaguars during joint training camp with Carolina Panthers at Miller Electric Center on August 19, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Dustin Markland/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the first time this year at Jacksonville Jaguars training camp , Trevor Lawrence rushed for a touchdown. Granted, Lawrence hasn’t had many opportunities to run the football this summer. Quarterback safety is a priority to begin with, and the NFL’s current practice rules don’t allow for many live reps, either. “It’s extremely challenging,” offensive coordinator Grant Udinksi said following Wednesday’s joint practice with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. “You can’t fully replicate [scramble situations] because there’s no opportunity to get hit, there’s nobody chasing you in those, but we want to try to take those opportunities to practice those reps at full speed.” “We’ll put together drills and try to build it into drills or team periods, but it’s really a different process when you know the scramble is coming versus when you have to instantaneously respond and you’re not thinking it and you’re not expecting it.” The coaching staff can try to simulate game reps as much as they can, but there’s also responsibility on Lawrence to act as if the practice setting has higher stakes. “It can be tougher in practice,” Lawrence acknowledged. “I just talked about this with Liam [Coen] and Grant, trying to make the reps in practice a little bit more real. When I do scramble, I think it’s easy in practice sometimes to get on the perimeter, take your time, wait wait wait, then you throw up a ball that you probably shouldn’t throw and maybe it gets picked or it’s in traffic.” Lawrence is amid a career-long quest to be more consistent in every area of his game. Decision-making, both in and out of the pocket, is on the list. But most of his offseason training is devoted to the first 2.5 seconds of his dropback. If Lawrence can mock broken plays with some degree of authenticity, his teammates will be better prepared when the time comes on gamedays. “I’ve had a couple of those [overextended scrambles] this training camp. Just being smart, because those are really the only times you get to work it. And making those real reps where you get out of the pocket, even if it’s seven-on-seven, get out of the pocket and let the receivers see me do that so they can get used to reacting and getting open. Because if you don’t work it in practice and then Week 1, you want these guys to run around and get open off-schedule, and they haven’t seen it all training camp, it’s probably not going to happen. So, I need to do a better job of doing it more for these guys so we can be ready to roll.” “We’ve had some really good ones in the redzone though, in team periods throughout all of training camp. But I think just taking every opportunity I can, because our defense—unfortunately for our offense, but fortunately for our defense, they covered a lot of stuff this camp where I probably could have scrambled a little bit more instead of trying to squeeze one into the backside or whatever. I think that’s something that I definitely want to continue to work on these next two weeks.” It’s easy to remember the impact that Lawrence’s legs had on the Jaguars’ 8-0 run to cap their 2025 regular season. He ranked second among all passers in rushing touchdowns (5) and rushing 1st downs (20) in that span. His most memorable highlights were downfield heaves as he rolled left after evading the pocket. Coen will continue to call designed QB runs in high-leverage situations, but there’s also a reliance on Lawrence to be a playmaker in a “backyard football” sense. Especially in scoring territory. “When we got better in the red zone last year was when Trevor started using his legs,” Coen said after a productive day in the redzone last week. “It’s so hard to scheme wide-open or open receivers in the red zone. It’s so much tighter. There’s less vertical grass. And especially versus a three-man, four-man rush, it’s challenging.” “You watch around the league of the top red-zone touchdowns every week, and 90% of them are off schedule. They’re just, ‘Hey man, you got to buy a little time. Find a window. Somebody’s got to make a little move and boom, touchdown.’ And it’s not exactly how you draw it up, but it’s football.” Real, live football is still a few weeks away. As the Jaguars prepare for their September 13 season opener, they’re looking for any kind of stepping stone to smooth the transition and start on the right foot. This week’s pair of joint practices against the Bucs was a scramble in the right direction. Notes & Quotes After injuring his shoulder on the first play of Tuesday’s joint practice, WR Brian Thomas Jr. wore an orange pinny and participated in individual drills on Wednesday. That’s very much a good sign, though his Week 1 status is still far from certain. With Thomas and WR Jakobi Meyers (hand) unavailable for team drills, the offense’s top target was WR Parker Washington on Tuesday , and TE Brenton Strange on Wednesday. He caught all 4 of his short-area targets. UDFA WR Trebor Peña also had a few receptions, including a touchdown in 7-vs-7 redzone drills, and WR/CB Travis Hunter played two or three snaps on offense for the first time in several practices. The play of the day belonged to WR Josh Cameron, who had a sick “and one” catch against Bucs CB Zyon McCollum way down the field in 7-vs-7 team drills. Lawrence leaked out of the imaginary pocket to initiate a scramble drill before quickly resetting his feet and launching the ball 40-plus yards to Cameron. The rookie wideout fought through pass interference to come down with the biggest catch of his young career. With my sights focused on the offense, I didn’t see as much of Jacksonville’s defense against Tampa Bay’s offense. But it sounded like a few second-year pros got their hands on the ball. According to SI’s John Shipley , DB Jabbar Muhammad made multiple plays in coverage, including an interception, and S Caleb Ransaw and OLB Jalen McLoud registered pass breakups as well. I believe I saw OL Cole Van Lanen, who was recently activated from the PUP list as he recovers from offseason knee surgery , play his first snap of training camp on Wednesday. It was with the second-stringers at right tackle. I’m not 100% certain that I identified the correct jersey number, but if it was indeed Van Lanen, even just one rep in team drills is a sign of progress. Jags fans, let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

title: The 5 Biggest X-Factors for the 2026 Chiefs
summary: Are you ready for some football? No, I’m not talking about preseason football. I’m talking about football with real, meaningful stakes attached to each and every play. The kind of football we haven’t seen from the Kansas City Chiefs for eight long months. It’s the longest Chiefs fans have gone without meaningful football we’ve seen […]
full_text: Are you ready for some football? No, I’m not talking about preseason football. I’m talking about football with real, meaningful stakes attached to each and every play. The kind of football we haven’t seen from the Kansas City Chiefs for eight long months. It’s the longest Chiefs fans have gone without meaningful football we’ve seen in more than a decade. And I, for one, have not enjoyed it. Over this extended offseason, I’ve had plenty of time to ponder the good and bad of the roster. We all know the biggest questions with this team: Will quarterback Patrick Mahomes look like himself after his devastating knee injury? Will the right tackle situation get sorted out? Do the Chiefs have enough at defensive end to supply a quality pass rush for the defense? Can this group of receivers finally stay healthy and perform up to their draft pedigree? Those questions have been asked and answered time and time again. We’ll certainly continue to monitor them throughout the season, but today I want to explore some lesser-discussed factors that could meaningfully impact the 2026 Chiefs’ regular-season success. These are, in my opinion, the five biggest X-factors of the 2026 Chiefs campaign. 5) Harrison Butker I know this sounds small. But can Butker please get back to making extra points look automatic? Can a kickoff look less… difficult? These little things became big things for the Chiefs last season. Butker missed three extra points in his first six games. He also kicked the ball out of bounds in the fourth quarter of a tight game against the Jacksonville Jaguars , and he kicked it short of the landing zone in a one-score game against the Denver Broncos . Butker was viewed as an automatic for much of his career. He’s made 90 percent of his career postseason field goals, including an astonishing 6/7 on kicks of 50+ yards. Whenever the Chiefs get back to January, I trust him to make the big one. I just wish I still trusted him to make the easy one. Maybe it’s unfair. But it’s something I’ll be monitoring early in the season, especially his shaky performance against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , with a missed extra point and the miss on the potential game-winning field goal. 4) Turnover Differential Do you know how hard it is to be a negative in the turnover differential with Patrick Mahomes as your starting quarterback? The 2025 Chiefs found a way to accomplish exactly that. No, these aren’t funny numbers. The Chiefs, through Week 15 last year with a healthy Mahomes, were -2 in turnover differential. It might have felt as though the Chiefs were committing turnovers left and right, but that wasn’t the case. The offense just found a way to commit the most back-breaking turnovers possible. Kansas City was actually tied for seventh in the NFL last year while Mahomes was healthy for fewest offensive turnovers in the league (13). Unfortunately, the defense forced just 11 turnovers over that same stretch. Only the New York Jets , Washington Commanders and New York Giants forced fewer turnovers through week 15. To put it simply, that can’t happen. Unfortunately, the Chiefs’ recent dip in pass rush has coincided with fewer takeaways. The Chiefs were among the top 10 in takeaways in each of Spags’ first three seasons as the defensive coordinator. Since then, the team has ranked 20th, 27th, 14th and 26th. The lack of takeaways limits opportunities for Mahomes and the offense. It puts more pressure on each drive to be perfect. A return to the top half of the league in takeaways would go a long way toward the team returning to form overall. 3) The Linebackers I’m not sure there’s a position group on the Chiefs’ roster that earned less offseason discussion than the linebackers. Much of that is based on circumstance. The Chiefs were cash-strapped while linebackers Nick Bolton and Drue Tranquill’s deals for 2026 were all but guaranteed. Those are your starters, and there’s really never been a doubt about it. How effective will they be, though? That’s a more reasonable question. Also uncertain is who the third linebacker will be when the Chiefs take the field against the Broncos on opening night. Is Jeffrey Bassa ready to take on that role? Do the Chiefs trust him enough to keep him on the field over Jack Cochrane? I certainly hope so, given how ineffective Cochrane was in base defense situations last year. But we know how this staff operates, and trust goes a long way. Cochrane (right or wrong) has earned that trust. The question with this group will always revolve around their overall lack of athleticism and ability to play against the pass. Bolton is never going to be a star in coverage, but I’m of the opinion his run defense can at times make up for some of those warts. Tranquill was a very good player for the Chiefs in his first year as a starter, but his overall effectiveness has been more erratic over the past year or two. A rebound season needs to be in the cards because both Bolton and Tranquill are going to be counted upon for an extremely heavy workload given the lack of depth at the position. 2) The Veteran Defensive Back Signings One look at the depth chart in the secondary reminds you that the top four options are more than adequate. I’m comfortable with Nohl Williams and Mansoor Delane at cornerback. Alohi Gilman and Chamarri Conner should be an adequate safety duo. After that, it gets more dicey. Who is the third cornerback? Who plays in the Nickel? Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo loves to play three safeties, but who is currently the third safety? The answer to many of these questions depends on the team’s recent defensive back signings. Can cornerback Kristian Fulton finally become a thing? If so, it could allow Delane to bump inside in Nickel situations to put the three best corners on the field. More likely, though, Fulton is nothing more than a depth piece in the secondary. That instead applies pressure on L’Jarius Sneed and Kader Kohou, the two cornerbacks Brett Veach signed this offseason as competition in the slot. Sneed has barely practiced and has yet to play in a preseason game, but I don’t get the sense that’s going to limit his opportunities. “(Sneed) and I have talked about (his versatility) a lot; he’s comfortable in both,” Spagnuolo said earlier this week. “Here’s his response, always, when I ask him: ‘Wherever you need me.’ That’s what he says. So a little bit of it will be determined by who else is out there and what they can do… LJ was always a lot like Trent (McDuffie). He was always effective inside, but when we needed him to match up on somebody outside, that kind of dictated it, so that same thing might happen. We’ll see where the other guys are.” That’s great, in theory, but it would be a lot more reassuring if we got to see it in practice. Or a game. Or, well, ever. The slot cornerback position has been a huge liability over the past year-plus when Trent McDuffie has been playing outside. Finding an answer to that problem will be critical for the defense to take a step forward. The veteran offseason additions will go a long way in determining whether that step is possible. 1) Health Okay, sure, this could be an X-factor for every team in the league. But I do believe it applies more to the Chiefs than to most. The starting quarterback is attempting to return in less than a calendar year from a serious knee injury. The top two wide receivers are returning from injuries, one of which rehabbed an offseason surgery while in jail. The left tackle is missing practices with a mysterious back issue, and the right guard saw a specialist for a hip issue that held him out of camp. Both are expected back, but will they be as effective? On the defensive side of the ball, L’Jarius Sneed hasn’t played a healthy season since the last time he was in Kansas City. Defensive end Ashton Gillotte is a question mark for opening night with a foot issue. Rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods has been dealing with an ankle issue in camp. Delane just returned from…

title: A closer look at how Chiefs’ offensive tackles have played in preseason
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs lost the second exhibition of the preseason with a 16-15 defeat to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Saturday. Despite the loss, the Chiefs had many bright spots throughout the game; however, the offensive tackle play was not one of them. Josh Simmons has been out of practice with a back injury, […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - AUGUST 22: Khalil Benson #70 of the Kansas City Chiefs blocks Rueben Bain #3 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half of a preseason game at Raymond James Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs lost the second exhibition of the preseason with a 16-15 defeat to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Saturday. Despite the loss, the Chiefs had many bright spots throughout the game; however, the offensive tackle play was not one of them. Josh Simmons has been out of practice with a back injury, so Jaylon Moore slid to left tackle, and rookie Kahlil Benson kicked inside from guard to right tackle. Benson had taken most of the first-team snaps at right tackle throughout camp, but when Trey Smith missed time with a hip injury, the team slid Benson into guard, where he had played in the Chiefs’ first preseason game in limited snaps, with Moore on the right side. The pair did not look sharp on Saturday night, allowing multiple pressures and multiple quarterback hits. The reserve tackles didn’t look great either — except for one — but with the final week of the preseason upon us and the regular season right around the corner, this should give the Chiefs some cause for concern. The first team With Moore on the left and Benson on the right, the Chiefs’ first-team offensive line struggled to protect Fields early on in the game. Not a bad stunt pickup by the KC IOL. Benson needs to be better with his hands and pad level to sit down against the bull rush. Moore starts out fine, but lets the edge swipes his hands and get to the QB. pic.twitter.com/dNV756D1dI — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 23, 2026 On the snap, Moore is initially fine out of his stance, but as the edge rusher draws near, he attempts to land both hands, and the edge quickly pulls off a swipe to get free and bend the arc. Justin Fields delivers the football in time, but is still brought to the ground. The Buccaneers recorded eight quarterback hits throughout the course of the game, with the majority of them coming from their edge rushers. While Moore was far from good, Benson struggled significantly in his first taste of NFL action at tackle. TB showing seven along the LOS pre-snap. They bring five. Benson needs to trust his slide more, but when he turns to go after Bain, it results in the hump. Moore with poor footwork out of his stance, quickly gives up the edge. pic.twitter.com/0tgsrXoMpx — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 23, 2026 Both Moore and Benson are a bit slow out of their stances, and both turn their shoulders directly to the edge rushers across from them. Moore’s shoulder turn leads to Fields getting hit, while Benson gets hit with a hump move and is knocked into the pocket. Post-game, it was revealed that the Chiefs were using a silent snap count, which could have led to some of the timing issues off the ball. With so many players walked up, Benson looks to protect the inside first before turning his attention to the edge rusher. A bit slow into his drive, the edge rusher beats him to the bend point and strips Fields. pic.twitter.com/ps1Tl4DHeT — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 23, 2026 On the snap, Benson wastes motion by throwing an inside hand and is late out of his stance. The wasted movements make him late at the bend point, so Benson turns his shoulders to try to stop the edge, but opens the door even further. The edge strips Fields, and Benson is lucky to come up with the ball. This was not an ideal first game of live NFL experience for Benson, but it could be one that helps the coaching staff decide his future with the team. The reserves The Chiefs backup tackles were a mixed bag in this game. Esa Pole played 36 snaps, Ethan Driskell 27, and Chu Godrick 14. Esa Pole Pole has looked fine so far in camp and the preseason, but this week he struggled against the Bucs’ pass rush. Pole gives up his chest, and the edge rusher uses some power to push him back in the pocket and make Fields uncomfortable. pic.twitter.com/N859kXevSO — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 23, 2026 Due to his size, Pole at times has trouble playing with leverage or playing balanced. This week, those issues hurt him, while his lack of development with his hands and ability to be moved backward in pass protection allowed edge rushers to give him issues. When Pole played in games during the regular season last year, the team typically used some kind of slide protection called a chip to assist him. During camp and the preseason, the team has used a more hands-off approach with more one-on-one situations for him to truly gauge where he is as a player. From what we have seen in the preseason so far, it appears he is still only a backup-caliber player. Ethan Driskell Last week against the Los Angeles Rams , Driskell struggled during his first live game action in over a year. Missing all of last season, he looked rusty at times, but this week he came out locked in and turned in a good performance. Good jump set here from Driskell. Quickly attacks to sell the run, then locks on and uses his long levers to his advantage. Strong hands to stay engaged. pic.twitter.com/RzM1itg7Re — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 25, 2026 Driskell didn’t see many true pass-rush snaps, but he looked good in the situations where he was blocking. Using his large frame and solid athletic ability, he blocked up multiple reserve Tampa Bay edge rushers and was able to keep the quarterback clean, not allowing a hit. Driskell had been forgotten by many, but when lined up on the right side, he looked better than on the left and could still be making his case to make the Chiefs’ active roster. Chu Godrick Entering his fourth season with the team, Godrick has only played in a handful of regular-season NFL games, but he has been a solid asset to the Chiefs as a developmental tackle on the team’s international roster exception. While he did not have any noteworthy plays on Saturday- good or bad- it seems likely he will still be involved in the Chiefs organization again this year as good insurance on the roster, given his roster status. The bottom line Two years ago, the Chiefs attempted to turn Kingsley Suamataia into their starting left tackle, and it backfired tremendously. Everything worked out well for Suamataia as his transition to guard has been successful, but the team should think carefully about what to do next with Benson. A second-round pick as a day-one starter is one thing, but a UDFA who has struggled should not be in consideration for the job. When Simmons comes back, Moore should start on the right side, but he too must play much better than he has shown this preseason. As for Pole and Driskell, neither has separated from what I have seen so far in the preseason, and neither has proven they can overtake Benson or Moore yet. That could change soon, but for now it has not. It will be interesting to see how the final preseason game on Friday pans out, and whether the Chiefs look for any outside help at tackle.
author: Caleb James

title: Chiefs News: The status of Josh Simmons’ back injury is unclear
summary: The latest When Kansas City Chiefs starting left tackle Josh Simmons first missed practice with a back injury during training camp over a week ago, nothing indicated that it was a serious issue for the second-year player. The news hit a day after Simmons had to man the third-team left tackle spot during practice. Fast […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 29: Josh Simmons #71 walks to the field during the Kansas City Chiefs training camp on Aug 11, 2026 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The latest When Kansas City Chiefs starting left tackle Josh Simmons first missed practice with a back injury during training camp over a week ago, nothing indicated that it was a serious issue for the second-year player. The news hit a day after Simmons had to man the third-team left tackle spot during practice. Fast forward to now, and Simmons still can’t practice. During a press conference on Wednesday, head coach Andy Reid revealed Simmons wouldn’t play in Friday’s preseason finale against the Seattle Seahawks and that rookie Kahlil Benson would be getting a shot at left tackle. During that time, he provided an update on Simmons, but not clarity. Chiefs HC Andy Reid Remains Cautious About Josh Simmons; Recovery Timeline Unclear | Sports Illustrated This was initially being treated as a short-term ailment that Chiefs fans didn’t need to worry about. However, Andy Reid’s comments on the situation during today’s press conference didn’t exactly give us the clarity we wanted. When asked about whether Simmons was in his recovery, Reid gave one of his classic vague answers. “Just getting his back checked out,” Reid said. “That’s the main thing. I mean, he was doing good when he was in there, [but] he’s got the back. Like any other injury, we’ve got to make sure and see if it’s right or what’s wrong with it.” Giants-Chiefs trade grades: Kansas City adds OL depth piece for late-round draft pick, per report | CBS Sports Chiefs: B- It’s a pretty simple calculation for Kansas City. The team needed offensive line depth, and identified it — at a cheap price — in Ezeudu. The Chiefs have done a really good job developing talent along their offensive line for quite a bit, and Ezeudu could be next in line. He’s a former top-70 pick who, according to Pro Football Focus, graded out decently in limited snaps in 2024 after a rough first two seasons. He’s very much a backup. If he’s playing significant snaps for you, you’re not in a good spot. But for a few drives here or there, in a pinch, he can be passable. 10 NFL players on roster bubbles going into the 2026 season | Pro Football Focus CB Kader Kohou, Kansas City Chiefs After missing all of 2025 due to a torn ACL, Kohou joined the Chiefs on a one-year contract in hopes of rekindling his prior form. As recently as 2024 with the Dolphins, Kohou showed glimpses with a 68.9 PFF coverage grade, allowing just a 76.0 passer rating when targeted. Kansas City appears to have its two primary starting corners set in Mansoor Delane and Nohl Williams, but the team has a logjam at cornerback depth in Kohou, Kristian Fulton, rookie Jadon Canady, L’Jarius Sneed and Kaiir Elam. Kahlil Benson tops list of 3 winners and 2 losers from the Kansas City Chiefs’ trade for Joshua Ezeudu | A to Z Sports Kahlil Benson Benson is perhaps the biggest winner of the trade. The Chiefs can now focus on having him exclusively play the offensive tackle position. He began this offseason as the team’s starting right tackle, but with Trey Smith injured, Kansas City shifted him to right guard during training camp and the preseason. When Josh Simmons got injured, he moved back to right tackle. Offseason In Review: Kansas City Chiefs | Pro Football Rumors Top 10 cap charges for 2026: Chris Jones , DT: $44.85MM Patrick Mahomes , QB: $34.65MM Trey Smith , G: $24.5MM Nick Bolton , LB: $19.25MM Jaylon Moore , T: $18.69MM Creed Humphrey , C: $18.1MM Kristian Fulton , CB: $13MM Mansoor Delane , CB: $7.62MM George Karlaftis , DE: $7.4MM Harrison Butker , K: $7.31MM Around the NFL NFL eliminating Pro Bowl Games, but will still name Pro Bowlers | ESPN While no AFC vs. NFC game will be held, players selected as Pro Bowlers will be invited to attend an in-person celebration in Los Angeles during the traditional weekend the Pro Bowl Games took place. “This direction came directly from our continued conversations with players and what they value most about the Pro Bowl,” NFL executive vice president of football operations Troy Vincent said in a statement. “Being selected by your peers, coaches and fans as one of the very best at your position carries tremendous meaning. We heard clearly that the distinction matters, and our focus is on making the recognition that comes with it worthy of what these players accomplished on the field.” NFL says players who return to college will be ineligible to play in 2026 | NFL.com Tight end Dae’Quan Wright originally signed with Philadelphia as an undrafted free agent out of Mississippi following the draft. He was waived by the Eagles on Aug. 10 and claimed by Cleveland the following day. He spent about two weeks with the Browns without playing in an exhibition game before being waived on Monday. He cleared waivers Tuesday and now wants to go to LSU to play for his former Ole Miss coach Lane Kiffin. Defensive lineman Zxavian Harris signed with New Orleans in May as an undrafted free agent out of Ole Miss and participated in the offseason program. He was placed on the non-football injury list at the start of training camp in July and was waived Aug. 8. He wasn’t claimed by any team and also wants to go back to college to play for Kiffin. Broncos reverse course with Bo Nix, who ‘probably won’t play’ in preseason finale | The Athletic Nix sat out the preseason opener in Atlanta on Aug. 14 and then played 15 snaps in last week’s game against the Packers. The 2024 first-round pick, who had two surgeries this offseason on the right ankle that was fractured at the end of a playoff win against the Buffalo Bills, completed 6 of 9 passes for 76 yards and a touchdown and led Denver to 10 points in his two series of work against Green Bay. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Eric Bieniemy can relate to ‘hard-headed’ Rashee Rice ”The thing I love about Rashee is he’s tough, he’s very, very tough,” said Bieniemy. “Another thing, and I’m not saying this in a bad way, he’s hard-headed, and he is stubborn.” Most people will hear this and see it as a knock against Rice, and maybe it was to an extent, but it was also an acknowledgment of Rice’s own belief in his abilities. “He feels that he is good enough at certain things,” Bieniemy continued. “I like that, because you have to get him to see it from a different point of view. When he can see it from a different point of view with a different set of eyes, now, it opens up his brain, and you can see it resonate.” From The Feed Follow Arrowhead Pride on Social Media Facebook: Like our page Instagram: @ArrowheadPride X: Follow @ArrowheadPride AP Staff on X: See complete list

title: Garrett Nussmeier will start the Chiefs’ preseason finale on Friday
summary: To end the 2026 preseason, the Kansas City Chiefs will host the Seattle Seahawks on Friday evening at Arrowhead Stadium. The opening kickoff is scheduled for 7:00 p.m. After the final practice of the week on Wednesday afternoon, head coach Andy Reid shared a list of players who will not be playing in preseason Week […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - AUGUST 22: Garrett Nussmeier #14 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs the ball during the second quarter of a preseason NFL football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images To end the 2026 preseason, the Kansas City Chiefs will host the Seattle Seahawks on Friday evening at Arrowhead Stadium. The opening kickoff is scheduled for 7:00 p.m. After the final practice of the week on Wednesday afternoon, head coach Andy Reid shared a list of players who will not be playing in preseason Week 3. In the midst of sharing it, he stopped himself to announce rookie quarterback Garrett Nussmeier as the starter for Friday’s game. The LSU product and fourth-string quarterback Chris Oladokun will share the playing time on Friday, although Oladokun needs to clear concussion protocol first. “The young kid is going to go,” Reid said, referring to Nussmeier. “He’ll start the game. Those two are going to split the game. It has nothing to do with Justin [Fields]; this is all in advance.” During this week of practice, Nussmeier has taken reps with the starting offense while Patrick Mahomes has manned the scout-team quarterback role, still uncleared to play in a live game. “He’s done a nice job,” Reid described Nussmeier in practice. “We threw him right into the fire there with the first group, and I thought he handled it well; it wasn’t a big shock to him. It looked like he stepped in and took it on, had good leadership, good tempo in and out of the huddle. It’ll pay off for him down the road.” “He’s looked good during the practices,” Reid said of Mahomes. “This week, he was the scout-team quarterback; pretty good scout-team quarterback. He’s looked strong, and obviously, his attitude is right.” If Oladokun can’t go, Reid is still dressing his second-string quarterback — but it could be all Nussmeier in the last exhibition of this year. “Justin, I told him to keep it loose there,” Reid grinned. “If not, then Garrett, I’m sure they would all like to play a full game, and now he has a chance, potentially.” Players who will not be available in Friday’s game Linebacker Jack Cochrane (Knee) Safety Chamarri Conner Defensive end Ashton Gillotte (Foot) Guard C.J. Hanson Wide receiver Jimmy Holiday Left tackle Josh Simmons (Back) Defensive end Tyreke Smith (Hamstring) An update on Kenneth Walker Starting running back Kenneth Walker has missed the last two practices, watching off to the side due to a foot injury designation. Reid clarified the severity of the lead back’s ailment. “The last couple of days, Kenneth Walker’s shoe has caused some swelling on his ankle,” Reid shared. “So we’re trying to get that down, but he’s okay; he’s going to be fine. We’re just trying to get that down.” What’s up with Josh Simmons? That answer has yet to come from Reid and the Chiefs. “Just getting his back checked out, so that’s the main thing,” Reid said of Simmons. “He was doing good when he was in there; he just had the back. Like any other injury, we have to see if that’s right or what’s wrong with it.” Ashton Gillotte is making progress “He’s off that little scooter and has a boot on,” Reid told reporters. “So we’re just taking it from there.” Will we see wide receivers Rashee Rice or Xavier Worthy in the preseason finale? It sounds like both starting receivers have been practicing this week, but Reid couldn’t give a definitive answer to this question. “I’m going to evaluate it in the next couple of days,” Reid said. “They’ve worked their tails off this week and have taken a lot of reps, so that’s been good for them. We’ll just see as we get closer to the game here.”

title: The top 10 most indispensable Chiefs ahead of the 2026 season
summary: Every team in the NFL has a core set of guys that can’t get hurt for them to have success. When teams sustain multiple injuries to their best players, it can ruin a season. So let’s rank the players most essential to the Kansas City Chiefs‘ success in 2026. Let’s start with an obvious selection: […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 06: Patrick Mahomes #15, Travis Kelce #87, and Creed Humphrey #52 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs to the field before the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium on October 06, 2025 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Every team in the NFL has a core set of guys that can’t get hurt for them to have success. When teams sustain multiple injuries to their best players, it can ruin a season. So let’s rank the players most essential to the Kansas City Chiefs ‘ success in 2026. Let’s start with an obvious selection: 1. Patrick Mahomes As long as quarterback Patrick Mahomes is on the team, he will be the most important player on the roster. He’s the engine of the entire passing offense. As the pass-catching talent has deteriorated for the Chiefs, it’s more on Mahomes to make incredible plays happen to sustain an efficient offense. The run game will be better in 2026, but it’s still all on Mahomes for the Chiefs to drive the passing offense. We’ll see how capable he is at that post-injury, but how he plays will determine how far the team goes. 2. Josh Simmons This isn’t a ranking of the best players on the Chiefs, but the most indispensable players. That means other players who play at your position matter too. If the rest of your position group is weak, your top guy becomes more valuable. That is the case with second-year left tackle Josh Simmons. If you watched the preseason Week 2 game, you’ll understand why Simmons is so valuable. Jaylon Moore, Khalil Benson, and Esa Pole all looked terrible. If two of them have to play in a game, that will be a disaster. Simmons is a great player, but he needs to stay healthy. If he misses games again, it can sink the season. 3. Chris Jones Defensive tackle Chris Jones has an argument for two in Year 11, but at least the Chiefs have more depth on the defensive line. The front office added depth at defensive tackle with signing Khyris Tonga and drafting Peter Woods. On the edge, George Karlaftis is good, and rookie R Mason Thomas has flashed in preseason. Even Felix Anudike-Uzomah has looked good in preseason. If a couple young guys pop, the defense will be deeper up front. Still, Jones is incredibly valuable. Jones needs to be a dominant pass rusher to make this work. He commands so much attention and makes big plays all the time. He’s still a dominant player, and that should continue this year. 4. Creed Humphrey The argument between center Creed Humphrey and right guard Trey Smith was interesting, but I think Humphrey gets the nod because he is the best player at his position. Humphrey makes a big difference in the run game because he can play in any scheme. Humphrey is the most complete player at his position that we’ve seen in a while. Losing that player would hurt because your backup center won’t have Humphrey’s versatility. 5. Trey Smith With that being said, Smith is still very valuable to the team, especially in the run game. Smith is one of the best run blockers in the league. He clears space and has enough versatility to play in multiple schemes. With the Chiefs leaning more on the run this year, that should make a player like Smith even better. The offense needs him to clear space to help the run game. 6. Mansoor Delane Having a rookie at sixth is high, but cornerback Mansoor Delane needs to be really good. He is the No. 6 pick, being counted on to be one of the best cornerbacks in the game. I think he’ll be a good player, and I’m confident he can get there eventually. We’ll see how he plays as a rookie, but I definitely think he’ll be a good player immediately, even if he isn’t a star. If Delane were to get hurt, you’re putting either L’Jarius Sneed or Kristian Fulton on the field. That is a huge dropoff. The Chiefs won’t be able to play man coverage with either on the field, and that limits the defense. Delane gives them the player who can cover elite receivers in man coverage, and they’ll need that to have a good defense. 7. Kenneth Walker Running back Kenneth Walker was basically the only addition to improve the offense. The team didn’t add a right tackle and waited until Day 3 to add to the skill positions. Walker was brought in to fix the biggest problem the team has had: a lack of explosive runs in the offense. Walker is one of the best in the league at that, and that will improve the run game. Kansas City needs Walker to make big plays, but also needs him to stay healthy all season. That has been an issue for Walker. The Chiefs will have to hope Walker stays healthy and can manage him well for 17 games. 8. George Karlaftis Defensive end George Karlaftis is the second-most veteran defensive lineman and crucial to helping stop the run. If Thomas or Anudike-Uzomah play more, Karlaftis’ run defense will be even more significant. He’ll help provide a power element that will complement those two players well. 9. Kingsley Suamataia Left guard Kingsley Suamataia took a big step last year, particularly in the run game. His combination of explosiveness and power is big in the run game. He’s athletic enough to cut off blocks on the backside of zone runs but has the strength to move defensive tackles vertically. If the offense is going to be more run-focused this year, the Chiefs will need Suamataia to get even better. 10. Travis Kelce Even at 37, Kelce is still an important piece of the offense. He’s big in the short areas of the field and can help move the chains. The Chiefs also didn’t add any tight ends to the room; there isn’t quality depth behind him. The Chiefs need Kelce to keep performing well until the organization adds another quality tight end.

title: Chargers QB2 battle should be decided vs. Rams
summary: The Los Angeles Chargers will start Justin Herbert for their preseason finale against the Los Angeles Rams, but he isn’t expected to play very much. Most of the snaps will go to Trey Lance and DJ Uiagalelei. Lance and Uiagalelei are fighting for the backup job behind Herbert, and it very well could come down […]
full_text: Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) and quarterback Trey Lance (5) walk on the field before an NFL football game at EverBank Stadium, Sunday, Nov. 16, 2025 in Jacksonville, Fla. The Jacksonville Jaguars defeated the Los Angeles Chargers 35-6. [Corey Perrine/Florida Times-Union] | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Los Angeles Chargers will start Justin Herbert for their preseason finale against the Los Angeles Rams, but he isn’t expected to play very much. Most of the snaps will go to Trey Lance and DJ Uiagalelei. Lance and Uiagalelei are fighting for the backup job behind Herbert, and it very well could come down to how each of them performs against the Rams. “I think it’s tight,” Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said after the second preseason game regarding the backup quarterback competition. “I don’t have a definitive status on it right now.” A year ago, Lance was on the heels of Taylor Heinecke, and he was able to win the job after an impressive preseason finale. Now, he could beat out Uiagalelei and claim the backup role for a second straight season, or there could be another upset. So far in the preseason, Lance has completed 22 for 36 passing for 223 yards and an interception with 69 rushing yards. Uiagalelei has looked better, going 13 for 24 for 200 yards and two touchdowns. That definitely gives Uiagalelei a chance going into the preseason finale. “For me, just go out there and let it rip, play loose, spin the ball. Just make some good passes and be able to lead the teammates. Be a great leader, great teammate, rally guys around me and be able to uplift teammates to the highest potential,” Uiagalelei said. Kickoff between the Chargers and Rams is scheduled for 7 p.m. PT inside SoFi Stadium.

title: Rashawn Slater among 5 Chargers to watch vs. the Rams
summary: The preseason finale is already here for the Chargers who just finished up their 20th and final training camp practice on Tuesday. Jim Harbaugh told reporters that starters will see time against the Rams, aside from Derwin James and Khalil Mack. That means Justin Herbert, the starting offensive line, and all of their skill position […]
full_text: Inglewood, - August 20: Linebacker Nadame Tucker #56 of the Los Angeles Chargers with the face mask against running back Khalil Herbert #40 of the San Francisco 49ers in the second half of a NFL preseason football game at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood on Thursday, August 20, 2026. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images The preseason finale is already here for the Chargers who just finished up their 20th and final training camp practice on Tuesday. Jim Harbaugh told reporters that starters will see time against the Rams, aside from Derwin James and Khalil Mack. That means Justin Herbert, the starting offensive line, and all of their skill position players, as well. With this also being the final audition for many of the players young players who have been grinding it out through camp, there’s going to be no shortage of effort in SoFi Stadium. Here’s who we are going to be keeping an eye on Thursday night when these two teams take the field. EDGEs Nadame Tucker & Kyle Kennard Tucker had a strong start to camp but expectations and hype around the undrafted rookie have simmered over the last two weeks, especially after a very poor outing against the 49ers that included a face mask penalty that eliminated what should have been a tackle for loss for the rookie. Both Tucker and Kennard were going to be given every chance this summer to prove they could be worthy of the fourth edge rusher spot over Bud Dupree. It would have been ideal as far as allowing the team to save some money if they wished to move on, but neither player showed enough promise. Both Tucker and Kennard need to show SOMETHING against the Rams or else I fear neither may end up making the final roster. The Chargers could easily turn to cut candidates from around the league to find a veteran pass rusher who could also perform on special teams, not unlike how Caleb Murphy was a preseason darling from a season ago. DT Nick Barrett Barrett was selected in the fifth round of this year’s draft which would lead you to believe he has the inside track to making the Chargers’ final roster amongst a crowded interior defender room that’s filled with a number of other first or second-year players. However, guys like Jahmeer Carter and TeRah Edwards have also stood just as much, if not more, than Barrett has through the first two preseason games. If final cuts were today, I don’t actually think Barrett has outplayed Edwards overall, but his status as a draft pick likely pushes him over the threshold as the team’s fifth and final defensive tackle that I expect them to keep. OG/T Trey Pipkins With Jake Slaughter switching back to full-time center following Tyler Biadasz’s injury, the Chargers thrust Pipkins straight into the left guard competition with Kayode Awosika in order to get him up to speed with the regular season fast approaching. Awosika is seemingly the starter to begin the year, but Pipkins needs to be prepared if more injuries pop up. The team cannot be just one more injury away from another wash of a season. If Awosika goes down, the Chargers want to not skip a beat with Pipkins taking his place, hence the huge surge in snaps over the last week of practice. Pipkins should have the athleticism to be effective in Mike McDaniels’ offense so this isn’t the worst move, but his ability to handle the interior pass rush is another question he’ll have to answer if/when that time comes. OT Rashawn Slater If Harbaugh was being truthful about all but two starters seeing snaps against the Rams in the preseason finale, then of course I’m pumped to see Slater take the field for the first time since the 2024 postseason. Slater looked good in practice this week and his movement skills all looked unhampered. He was exploding out of his stance at full speed and even went as far as participating in 11-on-11 drills. Be it just one snap, five, or a dozen, it’s going to be a sweet sight to see the Chargers’ star left tackle out there putting belt to a**.

summary: It was a much-less exciting game for the Chargers against the 49ers and it all came down to a very undisciplined performance from just about everyone. Unfortunately, some of the worst-graded players on the Chargers in this one were amongst the starters. Right guard Cole Strange — a literal follower of Mike McDaniel from the […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - AUGUST 16: Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Junior Colson (25) runs out of the tunnel with the team at the beginning of a NFL preseason game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers on August 16, 2025, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Greg Fiore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It was a much-less exciting game for the Chargers against the 49ers and it all came down to a very undisciplined performance from just about everyone. Unfortunately, some of the worst-graded players on the Chargers in this one were amongst the starters. Right guard Cole Strange — a literal follower of Mike McDaniel from the Dolphins — was atrocious in his first bit of game action despite being a hand-picked signing due to knowing the offense already. Veteran tight end David Njoku, another signing this offseason, could execute his assignments and was a big reason the starters only got three plays on their sole drive of the game. It was a game to quickly forget and move on from, but not before finding every bit of improvement needed. And unfortunately there was a ton to make a note of. Offense Best TE Jerand Bradley – 91.5 RB Keaton Mitchell – 75.1 OG/T Alex Harkey – 71.5 TE Oronde Gadsden II – 71.0 OT Travis Burke – 69.4 Bradley scored the Chargers’ only offensive touchdown against the 49ers and it was a very heads-up play where he was mindful about being touched down — or lack thereof — and managed to get up and scoot into the end zone. He has a very difficult path to sticking with the Chargers, but this play was nonetheless huge. Harkey was the highest-graded run blocker for the Chargers last Thursday while also being the only player to record a run block grade over 70.0 (72.3). Burke’s 81.0 pass block grade was second-best on the team to center Jacob Spomer (82.6). Worst OT Laekin Vakalahi – 33.3 OG Cole Strange – 40.5 TE David Njoku – 40.6 WR KeAndre Lambert-Smith – 41.6 OG/T Branson Taylor – 46.1 Vakalahi was overall the worst player on offense as he recorded a run block grade of 29.6 and a pass block grade of 36.4. The only worse pass block grade on the team was Strange with a horrendous 17.5. This is unfortunately not a fluke from Strange who recorded two different pass block game grades of below 20.0. Njoku’s run block grade of 27.9 was the worst among offensive players. He had just two games in 2025 where he was graded below 50.0 as a run blocker so the Chargers have to hope this was just a fluke against a well-coached defense. Defense Best LB Denzel Perryman – 90.5 LB Junior Colson – 89.1 CB Rodney Shelley – 84.6 LB Marlowe Wax – 84.3 CB Isas Waxter – 79.2 The linebacker play of the Chargers continued their strong preseason as Perryman and Colson were the team’s highest-graded defenders against the Niners. Colson specifically has impressed in his return to the field after missing most of his first two NFL seasons. His coverage grade of 90.7 was in the elite range and even topped his 89.7 grade from a week ago. Wax also kept his impressive pace with another performance that was strong in both run defense (84.1) and tackling (75.4). Through two games, Wax is the Chargers’ highest-graded defender overall at 92.1, followed by Colson at 90.8. Shelley’s 87.1 coverage grade was second only to Colson. His 76.9 tackling grade was also fourth on the team and best among cornerbacks. Worst EDGE Nadame Tucker – 29.9 S Tony Jefferson – 31.4 LB Emany Johnson – 36.7 DT Jamaree Caldwell – 37.2 S Noah Avinger – 41.6 After a strong start to camp, Tucker has fallen off a bit. We haven’t heard much in regards to splash plays during practice and this latest outing against the Niners was ROUGH, to say the least. Tucker was the lowest-graded player on the entire team and it was his 29.3 run defense grade that truly sunk him. Jefferson got beat on a pair of passes and that docked his coverage grade all the way down to 32.3, by far the worst on the team. Cadlwell’s 44.6 run defense grade was the biggest offender for him. His pass rush grade of 58.5 was middle of the pack. Avinger recorded a tackling grade of 23.6, worst on the team after missing a pair of tackes.

title: Rams trade for Tutu Atwell, send Jarquez Hunter to Miami
summary: The Los Angeles Rams traded for receiver Tutu Atwell from the Miami Dolphins on Thursday, reuniting the team with a player who has spent his entire career playing for Sean McVay. In return, the Rams sent running back Jarquez Hunter to the Dolphins after it became apparent that the 2025 fourth-round pick had fallen out […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - JANUARY 14: Tutu Atwell #5 of the Los Angeles Rams celebrates with teammates after scoring a touchdown during the second quarter of an NFL wild-card playoff football game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on January 14, 2024 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams traded for receiver Tutu Atwell from the Miami Dolphins on Thursday , reuniting the team with a player who has spent his entire career playing for Sean McVay. In return, the Rams sent running back Jarquez Hunter to the Dolphins after it became apparent that the 2025 fourth-round pick had fallen out of favor with McVay , and was no better than fourth on the depth chart. Atwell was drafted by the Rams in the second round of the 2021 draft, but was allowed to leave in free agency after a disappointing 2025 campaign in which he was paid $10 million for six catches. He signed with Miami as a free agent, but apparently that did not go well enough for him to stick. Before 2026 properly begins, Atwell is back with the Rams as Hunter heads towards his new home. Trade: Dolphins traded WR Tutu Atwell back to the Los Angeles Rams in exchange for RB Jarquez Hunter, sources tell ESPN. pic.twitter.com/S7jKSAlXCa — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 27, 2026 Atwell spent five years with the Rams — mostly up and down — before he headed to Miami. It was the fifth season that really hurt the most, as Atwell was targeted 15 times despite the eight-figure salary that Les Snead paid him to stay in L.A. By trading for his return, the Rams seem to believe that he’ll be in a better personnel situation in 2026 than he was dealt in 2025. For Hunter, he was taken by the Rams in the fourth round of the 2025 NFL Draft, but was never able to beat out Ronnie Rivers for the team’s depth role behind Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. McVay endorsed Rivers as a player he “trusts” and the coach clearly didn’t see any ways to use Hunter moving forward. Despite his strong performance in the preseason, Hunter has not cleared a role on a team with two starting quality backs. With the Rams trading for Atwell, he seems like a sure thing to make the roster, so who will the Rams let go in his place? Because it did not seem like Hunter was going to make the 53-man roster at all. Could this be bad news for C.J. Daniels? We’ll find out by Sunday’s final cuts.
author: Danny Stone

title: Chargers must get over the hump to match Rams’ success
summary: Like the Los Angeles Rams, the LA Chargers have made the playoffs in each of the last two years. However, they failed to win either time, so can they finally get over the hump in 2026 and match the Rams’ success? Both teams are tied for the fourth-most wins in the NFL since 2024, when […]
full_text: Inglewood, - August 20: Quarterback Justin Herbert #10 of the Los Angeles Chargers with head coach Jim Harbaugh of the Los Angeles Chargers prior to a NFL preseason football game between the Los Angeles Chargers and the San Francisco 49ers at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood on Thursday, August 20, 2026. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images Like the Los Angeles Rams, the LA Chargers have made the playoffs in each of the last two years. However, they failed to win either time, so can they finally get over the hump in 2026 and match the Rams’ success? Both teams are tied for the fourth-most wins in the NFL since 2024, when Jim Harbaugh left Michigan to take over the Chargers. Despite that, the Rams have been noticeably more successful in the postseason in that span, with three wins compared to the Chargers’ none. Harbaugh won at least one playoff game in his three postseason appearances with the 49ers, including three straight NFC Championship appearances. His Chargers haven’t been remotely close to winning in the playoffs. During Harbaugh’s first season, Houston locked the Chargers down and picked off Justin Herbert four times in a 32-12 blowout. In 2025, the Chargers trailed 9-3 entering the fourth quarter in a winnable Wild Card Round game against the Patriots. Somehow, it seemed an impossible task for Herbert and company to score a touchdown. Drake Maye threw a late touchdown pass to secure New England’s 16-3 win. The Chargers have won just one playoff game in the last decade. Since moving to Los Angeles in 2017, the team is 1-4 in four playoff appearances, with the lone win coming in 2018 against a rookie Lamar Jackson -led Ravens squad. They’ve won just 12 postseason games in their history. For (an unfair) comparison, the Rams have nearly matched that with 10 postseason wins in the Sean McVay era alone. It’s hard not to see the Chargers as nothing more than the Rams’ SoFi Stadium roommate based on that. Still, the Chargers deserve hype, even if they haven’t made anywhere close to the same headlines this offseason. The team has a new defensive coordinator in Chris O’Leary after Jesse Minter took the Ravens job. Don’t expect much of a drop-off in production, as the Chargers retained many of the pieces that helped them secure top-five defenses in the last two years. Plus, Mike McDaniel joins LA as its offensive coordinator alongside Herbert. McDaniel hyped up the Chargers and his dynamic with Harbaugh during a recent interview with NBC Sports analyst Chris Simms. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Chargers have the fifth-highest odds to make the AFC playoffs at -156. FanDuel Sportsbook also has them at +1600 odds to win the Super Bowl, fifth-highest in the league behind the Rams (+500), Bills (+1000), Seahawks (+1100) and Ravens (+1300). Again, even if they aren’t receiving the same love as the Rams, there are enough people out there, especially in Vegas, who believe in their chances this season. The Rams and Chargers will face off in November in a game not in a primetime slot. Their matchup deserves more fanfare, as it’s not only the Battle for LA, but a game between two legitimate Super Bowl contenders. Even with the Chargers largely flying under the national radar, they deserve respect in 2026, and might earn more hype if they finally manage to win a playoff game with the Harbaugh-Herbert duo.
author: Evan Craig

title: Thursday’s most interesting position battle will be on the Chargers
summary: The Los Angeles Rams should not be expected to play any important players during Thursday’s game against the Chargers, other than Ty Simpson, who we already know is not in the team’s plans for 2026. However, on the other team there is an interesting battle brewing on the Chargers as head coach Jim Harbaugh will […]
full_text: NGLEWOOD, CA - AUGUST 20: Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Trey Lance (5) runs through the tackle of San Francisco 49ers linebacker Ogbo Okoronkwo (59) during the game between the Los Angeles Chargers and the San Francisco 49ers on August 20, 2026 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood. (Photo by David Dennis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams should not be expected to play any important players during Thursday’s game against the Chargers, other than Ty Simpson, who we already know is not in the team’s plans for 2026. However, on the other team there is an interesting battle brewing on the Chargers as head coach Jim Harbaugh will determine who the team’s backup quarterback will be based on how Trey Lance and D.J. Uiagalelei perform against the Rams . The Los Angeles Chargers will start Justin Herbert for their preseason finale against the Los Angeles Rams, but he isn’t expected to play very much. Most of the snaps will go to Trey Lance and DJ Uiagalelei. Lance and Uiagalelei are fighting for the backup job behind Herbert, and it very well could come down to how each of them performs against the Rams. “I think it’s tight,” Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said after the second preseason game regarding the backup quarterback competition. “I don’t have a definitive status on it right now.” Lance is now five years removed from being the third overall pick in the draft, after the San Francisco 49ers traded three first-round picks (one that year, two in the future) to move up for him. If it wasn’t enough of a sign that Lance was a bad pick based on his career as a starter, consider the fact that he’s now just desperate to become a backup because he hasn’t proven himself over D.J. Uiagalelei! The former highly-touted high school recruit jumped from Clemson to Oregon State to Florida State during his college career and went undrafted in 2025. He’s not good but a good game against the Rams on Thursday could put him in position to be Herbert’s backup this season instead of Lance. And that will be the most interesting position battle you’ll see Thursday. Yes, to some degree Simpson is in a “battle” against Stetson Bennett, but Bennett may not play any snaps on Thursday. Even if Simpson performs poorly, it could just force L.A. to go make one final pitch to Jimmy Garoppolo, rather than being a great sign for Bennett. So that position battle is not quite on display as the one brewing for “the other team” that calls SoFi Stadium their home. Meanwhile, Sean McVay is inclined to sit every other player expected to make the team. Perhaps he will keep Max Klare and C.J. Daniels out there, but probably not for long. And if Daniels is out there for long, it’s not a great sign for his chances of making the roster. These are unusual circumstances for Klare, as despite being a second-round pick, he’s so far down the depth chart that he won’t factor into the team’s immediate plans. Instead, the focus could be more on the L.A. Chargers just based on the fact that Harbaugh looks to be using starters and backups in the first half of the game. McVay doesn’t usually do that, so Rams fans may just have to wait until Week 1 to see the big names.
