title: Puka Nacua ranked No. 7 on NFL Top 100 players of 2026
summary: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua has reached another milestone in his rapidly developing NFL career, as he was named No. 7 on the NFL’s Top 100 Players of 2026, giving the Rams three players inside the top 10. The ranking, which is voted on by NFL players, represents a massive jump for Nacua […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 25: Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams runs with the ball during the NFC Championship NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on January 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua has reached another milestone in his rapidly developing NFL career, as he was named No. 7 on the NFL’s Top 100 Players of 2026, giving the Rams three players inside the top 10. The ranking, which is voted on by NFL players, represents a massive jump for Nacua after he entered last year’s list at No. 41. His 34-spot rise is the largest jump among the players ranked Nos. 10 through 7. No. 7 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @RamsNFL WR Puka Nacua! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/oTY2tJutWi — NFL (@NFL) August 27, 2026 The ranking is a reflection of just how dominant Nacua was during the 2025 season. Nacua appeared in 16 games and finished with 129 receptions for 1,715 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns. He averaged 13.3 yards per reception and established himself as one of the most productive offensive players in the league. Perhaps the most impressive number was his 129 receptions, which led the NFL and tied for the seventh-most receptions in a single season in league history. Nacua also led the league with 107.2 receiving yards per game while finishing second in total receiving yards and tied for sixth in receiving touchdowns. He also recorded a league-best 80 receptions that resulted in first downs and four games with at least 150 receiving yards. Those numbers helped establish Nacua as much more than a promising young receiver. He became the centerpiece of Sean McVay’s passing attack and one of the most difficult players in the NFL to defend. Nacua’s efficiency was just as impressive as his production. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, he averaged 3.8 yards per route run in 2025, the second-highest mark of the Next Gen Stats era among players with at least 100 routes. The three players before Nacua were Micah Parson, Jahmyr Gibbs, and Patrick Surtain II. Green Bay Packers linebacker Micah Parsons came in at No. 8 despite being injured at the end of the 2025 season. Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs was No. 9. Denver Broncos cornerback Patrick Surtain II cracked the top 10. For the Rams, however, Nacua’s ranking is another indication of the star power on their roster. With Nacua at No. 7, Matthew Stafford and Myles Garrett are still waiting to be revealed, meaning Los Angeles could ultimately have three players inside the NFL’s top seven. The final six players will be revealed one per weekday beginning Monday, Aug. 31, with No. 1 scheduled to be unveiled Friday, Sept. 4. After a historic 2025 season, Nacua has officially established himself among the NFL’s elite. The only question remaining for Rams fans is how high his teammates will land—and whether Los Angeles will ultimately have the player voted No. 1 in the league.
author: Steven Ridings

title: Rams could eye these 3 players on roster cutdown day
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have spent the offseason building a talented roster, but the work will not necessarily end once the team settles on its initial 53-man group. With NFL teams required to trim their rosters to 53 players by August 30, a number of experienced players around the league will suddenly become available. For […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 16: Roger McCreary #25 of the Los Angeles Rams gets set during the second half of an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at SoFi Stadium on November 16, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams have spent the offseason building a talented roster, but the work will not necessarily end once the team settles on its initial 53-man group . With NFL teams required to trim their rosters to 53 players by August 30, a number of experienced players around the league will suddenly become available. For the Rams, that could create an opportunity to add depth without making a major investment. Even teams with strong rosters will be forced to release players who may have legitimate NFL ability simply because there are only so many spots available. Los Angeles could monitor those moves closely and identify potential additions at positions where it needs additional competition or insurance. Sean McVay and the Rams’ front office have already shown a willingness to develop overlooked talent. Once the league’s roster cuts begin rolling in this weekend, Los Angeles could have another chance to strengthen its roster with players who were simply victims of the numbers game elsewhere. 1. Sam Williams, EDGE, Dallas Cowboys Sam Williams entered the NFL with the potential to become a key piece of the Dallas Cowboys’ pass rush. Selected in the second round of the 2022 NFL Draft, Williams recorded 8.5 sacks during his first two seasons, showing flashes of the explosive edge-rusher many expected him to become. However, his development was interrupted by a season-ending injury in 2024. When he returned, Williams struggled to regain his previous form, finishing with only one sack despite playing a career-high 474 defensive snaps last season. There is a legitimate possibility that Williams could need a fresh start with another team. Dallas appears to have several edge rushers firmly positioned to make the roster, including Rashan Gary, Donovan Ezeiruaku, rookie Malachi Lawrence and veteran Von Miller. If those players secure their spots, the remaining competition could become extremely difficult for Williams. He may find himself battling Marist Liufau and James Houston for one of the final available roster spots. Liufau could have an advantage because of his contributions on special teams, giving the Cowboys another reason to keep him around. The Rams would have been able to get a respectable look at Sam Williams during their joint practice with Dallas. Another factor to keep in mind is that Byron Young is a free agent after this year. While the team has Josiah Stewart ready to replace Young. The team could use a rotational piece like Williams. A question could be: do the Rams like Wesley Bailey more or a high ceiling player like Sam Williams? 2. Kristian Fulton, DB, Kansas City Chiefs Similar to Sam Williams, the Rams will have been able to get a good look at Kristian Fulton compared to other external players based on their first preseason game against Kansas City. Fulton logged 29 snaps, the third most for the second string defense. Fulton carries a sizable cap hit this year – $13 million. The Chiefs could save $5 million by cutting him. The Rams could continue to add to their secondary that is comprised of former Chiefs. Behind Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson, the Rams do not have much. Emmanuel Forbes is CB3 and he has disappointed for the large portion of his career. 3. Roger McCreary, DB, Detroit Lions According to Detroit reports, head coach Dan Campbell said McCreary has had an “up and down” camp so far. The Lions signed McCreary this offseason to a one-year, $1.4 million deal. Detroit’s secondary has been a weakness over the past few seasons making it hard to imagine McCreary would not be able to grab a 53 man spot but judging by Campbell’s comments, this summer’s performance might cost him. The Rams are logical landing spot since Les Snead traded for McCreary at last year’s deadline. McCreary did not play as much as fans expected or hoped but when he did play – he was actually a bright spot in the secondary.
author: Steven Ridings

title: Former Rams Super Bowl winner cut by Broncos
summary: The Denver Broncos signed safety Taylor Rapp last week but have already released him from the team as of Wednesday. However, head coach Sean Payton indicated that the cut was not football related and that Rapp could be back with the team shortly. Rapp, a popular player with Los Angeles Rams fans during his four […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 13: Taylor Rapp #9 of the Buffalo Bills runs on field prior to an NFL football game against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 13, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos signed safety Taylor Rapp last week but have already released him from the team as of Wednesday . However, head coach Sean Payton indicated that the cut was not football related and that Rapp could be back with the team shortly. Rapp, a popular player with Los Angeles Rams fans during his four years with the team from 2019 to 2022, has spent the last three seasons with the Buffalo Bills. The Bills released Rapp this past March and he had yet to land with a team until signing with Denver. Rapp played just six games in 2025, but it doesn’t sound like the 28-year-old believes his career is over, just that he is on a hiatus. If the Broncos do bring him back, the Rams should see him on the field on September 27 when L.A. travels to Mile High Stadium. Question of the Day: Which Rams on the bubble are you rooting for? The Rams play their final preseason game of the season against the Los Angeles Chargers on Thursday night. This will be the last chance for some of the players to make either team, are there any players on the Rams that you hope to see make the active roster or practice squad? Are there any players you hope to see stick around the NFL and maybe come back to the Rams later? Any players you are rooting for in general? Maybe there are only six players on Thursday for Rams fans to watch . There also may be someone else who catches your eye! Lineman are fighting for final spots , Ty Simpson is getting some looks , running backs are fighting for their spots , which storylines are you following? Plenty to think about for the Rams as they get ready for SWeek 1 and beyond. The regular season is coming. Rams Roster Bubble: The Case For and Against 10 Players Fighting for the Final 53 (si.com) “ Wesley Bailey Case For: It may have initially been seen as a long shot for Bailey to make the 53-man roster as an undrafted free agent. However, following his performance against the Saints , it’s going to be difficult to keep him off. Bailey had 10 pressures and a forced fumble. If he hits waivers, another team will likely claim him.“ Al’zillion “AZ” Hamilton turning extra practice reps and lessons from veterans into a preseason interception for the Rams (therams.com) “WOODLAND HILLS, Calif. — On third and long, Saints quarterback Zach Wilson dropped back to pass during the second quarter against the Rams. Cornerback Al’zillion “AZ” Hamilton was in coverage and decided to switch up his approach after indications from the sideline. “I was off at first, but I heard my coach saying, ‘Go press it.’ That’s something we preach a lot over here, so I went to go press,” Hamilton told therams.com, recalling the play. On a curl route, the receiver cut back, but Hamilton was right with him. Wilson made a split second decision to fire it over the middle, but the receiver had already cut back and that gave Hamilton the perfect opportunity to jump the route. “So I kind of dove out there and just made a play,” Hamilton said. “Just getting a pick was a dream come true, I dreamed of getting a pick in the NFL.” Rams confident in Bennett and Simpson despite ‘up-and-down days’ (ramswire) ““I’ve seen good stuff. I think the hard part is there have been up and down days,” McVay said of his backup QBs. “I think our defense does a good job of being able to give a lot of challenging looks. What I have seen in both the games is the guys have good command. I think Ty did a great job against Kansas City and last week getting in and out of the huddle, the operation, being able to get through progressions. I think he’s consistently making good decisions. And then I thought Stetson last week where he got a little bit more opportunities, he showed some of the playmaking with his ability to extend plays with his legs.” LA Rams debate a significant change to Stetson Bennett’s role in final preseason game (dawnofthedog) “The Rams debated not playing Stetson Bennett during their first two preseason games. Most NFL teams choose to rest their established players during the preseason to avoid injuries, and Bennett has been in the Rams’ organization for three years now so he doesn’t need the reps that rookie quarterback Ty Simpson does to learn the offense. Bennett ultimately started both games though and played well in the first game before exploding during the second game . Head coach Sean McVay however said that fellow quarterbacks Ty Simpson and Matthew Caldwell will play on Thursday, so there may not be any available playing time for Bennett. Bennett and Simpson split time during the first two games while Caldwell never saw the field. If the Rams want Caldwell to play now it seems difficult to make time for three quarterbacks to all play, so that is why Bennett more than likely won’t see the field during the Rams’ final preseason game.“ Are Rams or Chargers starters playing on Thursday night? (ramswire) “McVay doesn’t play any starters in the preseason, no matter the situation. That trend will continue this week. Matthew Stafford, Puka Nacua, Trent McDuffie, Myles Garrett and every other starter will sit out Thursday’s game, getting ready for the regular season in a few weeks. McVay uses joint practices to get his starters reps against other teams, allowing backups to play all of the snaps in the preseason. It’s possible McVay will even hold out Stetson Bennett, saying he’s unsure whether the fourth-year quarterback will play. Ty Simpson will definitely suit up, and undrafted rookie Matthew Caldwell could also get some snaps. Are the Chargers’ starters playing? Head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters this week that the Chargers’ starters will play against the Rams. He said he envisions them playing six to nine plays, so it’s not as if they’ll be on the field very much.“ Rams Super Bowl Champion Gets Good News After Broncos Exit (heavy.com) “One practice is all Taylor Rapp ended up having in Denver. We’ll see what Sean Payton says after practice today,” The Denver Post’s Parker Gabriel posted in reaction to the news, adding, “Rapp had agreed to a vet minimum $1.3 million deal with just a nominal guarantee, per NFLPA records and sources.” This is not the end for Rapp in Denver, though. “Taylor Rapp came in. Spent some time with him. He needs a little time at home, and completely get where he’s at,” Broncos head coach Sean Payton told reporters on August 26. “There’s a good chance, better than good chance that–I know how he felt being here. And so, I think sooner than later that’s going to happen. But this, obviously, took precedence. So, we’ll just leave it at that.” Rams backup quarterback competition concludes Thursday vs. Chargers (latimes.com) “Under coach Sean McVay , the Rams’ final preseason games routinely are showcases for players vying for spots on the practice squad, not the roster. But Thursday night’s game against the Chargers at SoFi Stadium will offer another look at perhaps one of the most important players for the Rams ’ future: Rookie quarterback Ty Simpson . Simpson, the 13th pick in the NFL draft, has been competing with fourth-year pro Stetson Bennett to back up Matthew Stafford, though Bennett took the vast majority of second-team reps during training camp and preseason workouts.“ Rams game at SoFi Stadium costs families $422 more than Chargers game (nypost) “The building is the same. The parking lot is the same. The hot dogs, beer and $8 sodas don’t suddenly taste better when the Rams are playing. But the price tag certainly changes depending on who is playing. With the Rams and Chargers scheduled to collide in the preseason on Thursday night at SoFi Stadium, we thought we’d look into the cost for a family of four to attend a Rams game compared with a Chargers game for the upcoming NFL season. A family…
author: Danny Stone

title: Rams’ preseason finale only matters for six names
summary: We cannot pretend that Thursday night’s preseason finale between the Los Angeles Rams and Los Angeles Chargers is a 90-man audition. The most noteworthy outcomes from the game will be who Sean McVay decides not to subject to an exhibition and are therefore likely safe to make the team. Thursday night is a job interview […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 22: Ty Simpson #15 of the Los Angeles Rams looks down field during a preseason game between the New Orleans Saints and the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images We cannot pretend that Thursday night’s preseason finale between the Los Angeles Rams and Los Angeles Chargers is a 90-man audition. The most noteworthy outcomes from the game will be who Sean McVay decides not to subject to an exhibition and are therefore likely safe to make the team. Thursday night is a job interview only for a select few. The rest are hoping to put out positive film so they can stick elsewhere. It’s the difficult truth of the Rams’ preseason that you’ll hear from only the most realistic voices. Backup quarterback Insuring Matthew Stafford is Stetson Bennett’s job until it isn’t—and the veteran’s grip on the title has slowly loosened since rookie Ty Simpson’s breakout game in Kansas City. While Bennett lit up the box score in the second preseason game against the Saints, throw-for-throw this was not an overwhelmingly positive performance . Ignore the box score. Look for throws into tight windows. The ball was sailing on Bennett last week, and he’s demonstrated a frequency in which he throws behind his receivers. That isn’t promising in terms of running an efficient offense. As for Simpson, will the Rams let him attempt a pass beyond 20 yards? It’s the last box he needs to check in order to dethrone Bennett and serve as Stafford’s full-time understudy. The rookie has been pinpoint accurate on short and intermediate throws. He needs to remain consistently effective at this while showing the world he can also hit the deep ball. The last running back (if there is one) McVay and the Rams are telling us that the top three backs at set: Kyren Williams, Blake Corum, and Ronnie Rivers. There is no telling if the team will even be willing to carry four running backs. With the surplus of positive preseason performances between Jarquez Hunter, Dean Connors, and Jordan Waters, LA may feel compelled to release all three and then stash one or two of them on the practice squad. The roster is very talented and highly competitive. The Rams may need to steal a spot here or there in order to keep their best 53 players. If LA does keep four running backs, there seems to be no clear favorite between Hunter and Connors. Both bring a different style to the backfield. Hunter is a physical presence that can hit top-end speeds. Connors’ best preseason production has come as a receiver, which is a nice change of pace from the three leaders on the depth chart. Is there room for standout offensive linemen? Alaric Jackson is facing a possible suspension. Rookie Keagen Trost will likely miss the start of the regular season due to injury. Justin Dedich returned to practice this week. If the offensive line depth feels uncertain ahead of the cutdown to the 53-man roster, that’s because it largely is. Two names to keep an eye on are Bill Murray and Austin Blaske, of which you can read a deeper dive on them here . If the Rams are going to keep a surprise player on the OL, I’d lean more towards Blaske. The rookie UDFA has played both tackle spots in the preseason and performed well. The Rams have a more urgent need at tackle short-term than they do at guard. Blaske may be the right man at the right time. Wesley Bailey—a man in his own category I give Wesley Bailey a 25% chance to make the Rams’ 53-man roster. He faces uphill odds. The biggest reason is that LA is already set at the top four edge rusher spots with Myles Garrett, Byron Young, Josaiah Stewart, and Desjuan Johnson (who did not play versus Saints). Yes, it is absolutely impressive that Bailey earned 10 pressures in Saturday’s game against New Orleans. However, for every pass rush win there is an offensive lineman that takes a loss—and the Saints’ right tackle allowed nine pressures individually. It’s also telling that Bailey played long enough to accumulate the volume of pressures he did. If the Rams were truly impressed, he wouldn’t have been on the field. Bailey likely isn’t battling to make the 53-man roster. He’s a better fit for the practice squad, assuming another team isn’t willing to claim him off waivers. The only way Bailey makes the roster is if the Rams want to protect him from other teams poaching them, and LA has a recent bad taste in their mouth after losing standout offensive lineman Willie Lampkin a year ago. Bailey isn’t competing against anyone directly. He needs another standout performance in order to force LA’s hand. That is a very high bar to clear after he already has one preseason game without a pressure. Just remember— don’t get too attached to preseason standouts . They don’t have a great chance at no fault of their own.
author: JB Scott

title: The Rams’ two unheralded linemen to keep an eye on for 53-man roster
summary: The Los Angeles Rams must trim their roster to 53 players by Sunday at 3:00 pacific time. Two players making the team’s decision difficult ahead of Thursday night’s preseason finale are standout offensive linemen Bill Murray and Austin Blaske. Murray leads LA’s offense with a near-elite Pro Football Focus (PFF) grade of 89.0. Blaske ranks […]
full_text: Inglewood, - August 22: Quarterback Stetson Bennett IV (13) high fives teammate offensive tackle Austin Blaske (64) of the Los Angeles Rams after running for a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints in the first half of a NFL preseason football game at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood on Saturday, August 22, 2026. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams must trim their roster to 53 players by Sunday at 3:00 pacific time. Two players making the team’s decision difficult ahead of Thursday night’s preseason finale are standout offensive linemen Bill Murray and Austin Blaske. Murray leads LA’s offense with a near-elite Pro Football Focus (PFF) grade of 89.0. Blaske ranks second with an overall mark of 75.8. Neither player were on the radar at the start of training camp. But through two games the Rams have been able to run the ball effectively and their quarterbacks rarely get touched. Murray and Blaske have made important contributions leading to these outcomes. So who are they? Bill Murray Signed as an undrafted free agent by the New England Patriots in 2020, Murray doesn’t have much regular season playing experience under his belt. He was on the field for 42 snaps with the Chicago Bears in 2024 and earned a PFF grade of 82.4 with an impressive pass blocking mark of 85.7. He’s posted near-elite marks consistently over the last two preseasons. With the Rams, Murray has primarily played at left guard. He has demonstrated size flexibility after five seasons and had dabbled some at right tackle. Has Murray finally showed enough in the preseason to stick with a team full-time, whether it’s the Rams or someone else? Austin Blaske The Rams signed Blaske as an undrafted free agent this spring. He comes to the NFL by way of the North Carolina Tar Heels. Blaske’s preseason so far is somewhat of a tale of two games. He split reps at left tackle and left guard in the opener against the Kansas City Chiefs and earned a PFF grade of 80.9. In the second exhibition contest, Blaske mostly manned the right tackle spot (66 snaps) and had 12 snaps at right guard. His performance in Week 2 was weaker with an overall grade of 67.0, although his run blocking grade of 76.4 was effectively the same as the opener. The rookie UDFA has quality film at four of the five offensive line spots. That level of flexibility is valuable, especially since the Rams’ depth chart is uncertain because of injuries and Alaric Jackson’s potential suspension . How convincing is Blaske’s case? He’ll make his final arguments in the preseason finale on Thursday night.

title: The Pro Bowl is officially cancelled
summary: The NFL is ending the Pro Bowl. According to a report by The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones, the NFL is no longer going to hold a Pro Bowl game, instead focusing on celebrating players who were nominated for the Pro Bowl and ending the usage of alternates. It is about time. The Pro Bowl, besides not […]
full_text: SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - February 1: Jared Verse #8 and Byron Young #0 of the Los Angeles Rams walk together during a Pro Bowl team practice during the NFL Pro Bowl Games at Moscone Center South on February 1, 2026 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL is ending the Pro Bowl. According to a report by The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones, the NFL is no longer going to hold a Pro Bowl game, instead focusing on celebrating players who were nominated for the Pro Bowl and ending the usage of alternates. It is about time. Exclusively at @TheAthletic : After years of noncompetitive play and tweaks, the NFL will no longer hold a Pro Bowl game, becoming the first major U.S. league to end its all-star event. The NFL will focus its celebration on Pro Bowlers with no alternates. https://t.co/m34IZDmReq — Jonathan Jones (@jjones9) August 26, 2026 The Pro Bowl, besides not being a good event that represented the NFL well, had gotten out of hand with how bad the players were that became elected to the game due to being alternates and others opting out for various reasons. The most important reason of all being that nobody cares. Why should a good quarterback with tens of millions of dollars waste his time on the Pro Bowl? We could probably blame the whole thing on Shedeur Sanders. The rookie quarterback who had seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions last year was a Pro Bowler. He is not a starter anymore despite sitting behind Deshaun Watson, arguably the worst-looking starter in the NFL today. The Rams had four Pro Bowl players last season. Matthew Stafford, Puka Nacua, Jared Verse, and Byron Young. This is bad news for any player who has bonuses tied to Pro Bowl nods because now there will be a lot fewer of them. It’s for the best.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Rams have a familiar option to consider if Giants cut OBJ
summary: Odell Beckham Jr. is on the roster bubble in New York, and if things don’t pan out there, the Los Angeles Rams are an option. The Rams could be a landing spot for many big-name players if cut ahead of the season, and an OBJ reunion in Hollywood still makes (some) sense, even at this […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - AUGUST 22: New York Giants wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. (3) leaps for a pass in the end zone but can't hang on during the preseason NFL game between the New York Giants and the Miami Dolphins on Saturday, August 22, 2026 at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami, FL (Photo by Peter Joneleit/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Odell Beckham Jr. is on the roster bubble in New York, and if things don’t pan out there, the Los Angeles Rams are an option . The Rams could be a landing spot for many big-name players if cut ahead of the season, and an OBJ reunion in Hollywood still makes (some) sense, even at this stage of his career. If NY cuts ties with the veteran receiver during roster cutdowns, here’s why the Rams should or shouldn’t consider a reunion. There might be enough juice left in Beckham’s tank The Giants re-signed Beckham in June. So far, his second stint with the team that drafted him hasn’t been the smoothest, which is why his status is fairly unclear ahead of the 2026 season. Beckham has played sparingly this preseason and hasn’t lit up the box score. In two games, he’s caught four passes for 23 yards. Yep, that’s all, but that doesn’t mean he hasn’t had some flashes here and there. During the 26-3 win over the Dolphins on Saturday, he caught a 12-yard pass on first down in the second quarter that looked somewhat like vintage OBJ if you squint. OBJ with the jukes 😮‍💨 NYGvsMIA on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TX0VQ11Dpl — NFL (@NFL) August 22, 2026 The jukes on that reception showed that he still has some elusiveness left after the catch. While he did have a touchdown slip through his hands in the game, his hands are largely still unmatched. Beckham more than made up for the drop this week in practice as he caught his signature one-handed pass. View this post on Instagram Nothing about those clips indicates that he’s about to have a monster season (by his recent standards), yet it proves the aging wideout might have enough left in the tank to be fairly productive. Plus, the Rams do not have a clear No. 3 receiver behind Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, so they could use any depth piece they can find. There are plenty of options, including Jordan Whittington, rookie CJ Daniels and Konata Mumpfield, but none have solidified the position in training camp. Read more – Rams 53-man roster: Consensus projection shows expectations That’s not to say that Beckham would immediately anchor down that spot if he were to re-sign with LA. However, his veteran presence would be enough to at least hold down the fort until one of those youngsters hopefully steps up. OBJ is nowhere close to being the player he once was Now, let’s play devil’s advocate. Even when Beckham signed with the Rams during the 2021 campaign, he was far removed from the player he was to begin his career. Beckham was coming off a season cut short by injury. He tore his ACL and played in just seven games in 2020, and the Browns released him in November of that year. With the Rams, he was productive enough to help get them over the hump and win the Super Bowl, but even then, he had one 100-yard game in his 12 games with the team. A troubling decline in production and injuries have followed OBJ throughout the back half of his career. For starters, he hasn’t had a 1,000-yard campaign since the 2019 season with Cleveland. Beckham has also amassed 620 receiving yards and three touchdowns in 23 games played since ‘21 with the Ravens and Dolphins. A torn ACL kept him from playing the entire 2022 season. Last season, he played in nine games with Miami and began the year on the reserve/PUP list after recovering from surgery for an unknown injury. His lack of availability since leaving Los Angeles is concerning, and it’s unlikely to improve in his age-33 season. If the Rams were to reunite with Beckham, the front office would have to know they wouldn’t be getting him for a full season. As much as the team needs greater depth at wide receiver, signing the star wideout likely poses too much risk, regardless of the investment. What happens next Whether Beckham stays in the Big Apple remains to be seen, but an opportunity to snag a roster spot might’ve opened up. Calvin Austin III tore his ACL in practice this week, creating a hole at slot wide receiver for the Giants. The injury, which is unfortunate for New York right before the start of the season, could be best-case for Beckham to earn a spot on the roster. Between his recent injury history and noticeable lack of production since leaving the Rams, a spot is obviously not guaranteed. This will certainly be something to monitor as roster cutdowns begin after the final slate of preseason games this weekend. Expect the Rams to keep a watchful eye on their old friend, especially if the Giants cut him. A reunion is unlikely, but not improbable, as the team seeks to improve the roster ahead of what could be a special season in LA.
author: Evan Craig

title: 5 Las Vegas Raiders rookies to watch in preseason game against San Francisco 49ers
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are set to play their final preseason game, facing off against the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday night. Kickoff is at 5p.m. PT. This will also mark the end of training camp, as the NFL’s cutdown day is right around the corner on Sunday, raising the stakes for every player on […]
full_text: AUBURN, ALABAMA - SEPTEMBER 21: Nose tackle Keyron Crawford #24 of the Auburn Tigers during their game against the Arkansas Razorbacks at Jordan-Hare Stadium on September 21, 2024 in Auburn, Alabama. (Photo by Michael Chang/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are set to play their final preseason game, facing off against the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday night. Kickoff is at 5p.m. PT. This will also mark the end of training camp, as the NFL’s cutdown day is right around the corner on Sunday, raising the stakes for every player on the bubble to make the 53-man roster. So, this week’s rookies to watch are heavily focused on the Raiders’ undrafted free agents, with one third-round pick thrown in the mix. Keyron Crawford As the 67th pick of the draft, it’s highly unlikely that Crawford is in danger of getting cut. Also, the Auburn product was a project coming out of college and wasn’t expected to have a big role this year after Las Vegas signed Kwity Paye, re-signed Malcolm and had the Maxx Crosby trade fall through during free agency. However, Crawford has generated just one pressure in the first two preseason games, per Pro Football Focus , and hasn’t been a factor against the run, either. Meanwhile, S&BP’s Bill Williamson listed three other edges —UDFA Cian Slone and veterans Patrick Johnson and Jahfari Harvey—as players to watch against San Francisco, and all three have outperformed Crawford this month. Again, the third-rounder’s roster spot should be safe, but he’s looking at getting buried on the depth chart if he doesn’t step up on Thursday night. E.J. Williams Klint Kubiak didn’t mince words when talking about the team’s wide receivers after last week’s game, saying “ they gotta get a lot better and fast ”. The coaching staff is clearly looking for someone to step up and provide some depth out wide, giving Williams an opportunity to earn a roster spot with a strong outing against the 49ers. He had a 41-yard catch a couple of weeks ago, but hauled in just one grab for six yards in Houston. Granted, the Indiana product hasn’t had many opportunities with just 13 offensive snaps in both games combined, per PFF . But the final preseason game is typically where players on the bubble get the most action, meaning Williams should have plenty of chances to prove himself. He and fellow UDFA wide receiver Chase Roberts, who also could be listed here, did get a shoutout from Kubiak after the Cardinals matchup to seemingly increase their odds of making the team. Roman Hemby With uncertainty surrounding the extent of Ashton Jeanty’s injury and thus whether he’ll be ready to play at the beginning of the regular season, an extra roster spot for a running back could be open. Hemby has an uphill battle to beat out Dylan Laube and Dare Ogunbowale , since those two have outproduced him in the preseason so far. But the former Hoosier still has a fighter’s chance with a big performance on Thursday night. Even if he’s headed to the practice squad, Hemby could use a confidence booster to show he belongs in the NFL. Gary Smith III Smith’s chances of making the roster took a nose dive last week after the Raiders signed Folorunso Fatukasi and Fatukasi played well against the Houston Texans. But the defense could use more than just one quality run defender on the interior defensive line, and the unit should be looking for a young player at the position who can provide some future value. That gives the 24-year-old UCLA product a glimmer of hope. Smith had a good outing last week, recording a pair of run stops on just eight snaps against the run, per PFF . He’s also second behind Fatukasi for the best PFF run defense grade among Vegas’ defensive tackles in the preseason with a 69.9 mark . Ultimately, the former Bruin will likely begin the regular season on the practice squad, but he does have one more opportunity to prove himself. Xavian Sorey Jr. Sorey is another guy who looks like a long shot to make the 53-man roster, partially because he only received 24 defensive snaps in the first two preseason games combined. So, this Thursday night is more about showing what he can do on a larger sample size. One way to do that is to make plays on special teams, and the Arkansas product hasn’t gotten many opportunities in that phase of the game either, with just five special teams snaps and one of those coming on a field goal block, according to PFF . In other words, the 49ers matchup should be Sorey’s best chance to show the coaching staff what he can contribute in a game.

title: Final Las Vegas Raiders’ 53-man roster prediction ahead of San Francisco 49ers preseason game
summary: It’s hard for me to believe that the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 training camp is almost over because it feels like they were just getting started not too long ago. But here we are, with the Raiders preparing for their third and final preseason game of the campaign against the San Francisco 49ers and the […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 13: Head coach Klint Kubiak of the Las Vegas Raiders looks on as players warm up before a preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals at Allegiant Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Cardinals defeated the Raiders 27-14. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s hard for me to believe that the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 training camp is almost over because it feels like they were just getting started not too long ago. But here we are, with the Raiders preparing for their third and final preseason game of the campaign against the San Francisco 49ers and the league’s cutdown day looming on Sunday, Aug. 30. That also means it’s time for my final 53-man roster prediction. The ‘previously’ sections below refer to the prediction ahead of the Houston Texans game . Quarterback (2) Previously: Starter: Kirk Cousins Backups: Fernando Mendoza (R) Cut: Aidan O’Connell , Jacob Clark (R) Updated : Starter: Kirk Cousins Backups: Fernando Mendoza (R) Cut: Aidan O’Connell , Jacob Clark (R) O’Connell had a much better performance in last week’s game than what he showed against the Arizona Cardinals. But if the coaching staff wants to keep an extra cornerback, or another player at a different position, then rolling with two quarterbacks will help make the math work out. That’s especially true since O’Connell is heading into a contract year and, ideally, won’t see the field behind Cousins and Mendoza this season. The best case situation for Las Vegas is that AOC has a strong showing Thursday night to draw some trade interest ahead of cutdown day. Running Back (4) Previously: Starter: Ashton Jeanty Backups: Mike Washington Jr. (R), Connor Heyward (FB), Dylan Laube Cut: Roman Hemby (R) , Dare Ogunbowale , Patrick Gurd (R, FB) Updated : Starter: Ashton Jeanty Backups: Mike Washington Jr. (R), Connor Heyward (FB), Dylan Laube Cut: Roman Hemby (R) , Dare Ogunbowale , Patrick Gurd (R, FB) A couple of housekeeping items here: I’m lumping the fullbacks in with the running backs, and I’m writing this before we know the full extent of Jeanty’s injury. The Raiders seemingly avoided disaster with Jeanty suffering “just ” a sprained ankle , but how much time he’ll miss is unknown and could alter how many running backs the coaching staff wants to begin the season with. Hypothetically, say the 2025 first-round pick has to miss the first four games of the year. Then it might make sense to keep a veteran back like Ogunbowale around just in case. Plus, the team also has a question mark at kicker, and Ogunbowale has a career field goal percentage of 100% ; one-for-one from 29 yards. (That’s a joke…kind of…) Meanwhile, it seems like Laube established himself as the third running back with a strong performance in Houston last week, and Hemby seems like a good candidate for the practice squad. Wide Receiver (5) Previously: Starters: Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor, Jack Bech Backups: Malik Benson (R), E.J. Williams (R), Shedrick Jackson Cut: Dont’e Thornton Jr., Chase Roberts (R), Dareke Young, Phillip Dorsett II, Deven Thompkins, Noah Brown, Brandon Johnson Updated : Starters: Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor, Jack Bech Backups: Malik Benson (R), Dareke Young Cut: Shedrick Jackson, E.J. Williams (R), Dont’e Thornton Jr., Chase Roberts (R), Phillip Dorsett II, Deven Thompkins, Brandon Johnson Already Cut: Noah Brown To be honest, I’m still not really sure who is going to make the team at wide receiver. Klint Kubiak called out the entire position group last Friday , stating that he’s “still looking” for someone to step up and be accountable. That’s why I’m shifting to keeping just five wideouts, and the sixth spot could be left open for an outside hire. It wouldn’t surprise me to see the Raiders take a hard look at the waiver wire and add a wideout after cutdown day. Tight End (3) Previously: Starter: Brock Bowers Backups: Michael Mayer, Ian Thomas Cut: Carter Runyon, Albert Okwuegbunam , Chris Myarick Updated : Starter: Brock Bowers Backups: Michael Mayer, Ian Thomas Cut: Carter Runyon, Albert Okwuegbunam , Chris Myarick On the other end of the spectrum, it feels like tight end is pretty cut and dry. Bowers and Mayer were in street clothes last week—the former hasn’t played at all in the preseason, for that matter—while Thomas can round out the group and serve as a blocking tight end in 13 or 23 personnel. Also, fullback Connor Heyward has some position flexibility if the team gets in a pinch. Offensive Line (9) Previously: Starters: Kolton Miller, Spencer Burford, Tyler Linderbaum, Jackson Powers-Johnson, DJ Glaze Backups: Charles Grant, Caleb Rogers, Atonio Mafi, Trey Zuhn III (R) Cut: Dalton Wagner, Will Putnam, Jordan Meredith, Kamar Missouri (R), Justin Pickett (R), Isaiah Jatta (R), Niklas Henning (R) , Braeden Daniels Updated: Starters: Kolton Miller, Spencer Burford, Tyler Linderbaum, Jackson Powers-Johnson, DJ Glaze Backups: Charles Grant, Caleb Rogers, Atonio Mafi, Trey Zuhn III (R) Cut: Dalton Wagner, Will Putnam, Jordan Meredith, Kamar Missouri (R), Justin Pickett (R), Isaiah Jatta (R), Niklas Henning (R) , Braeden Daniels It feels like there’s only one open roster spot in the trenches for Las Vegas, and it’s a battle between Meredith, Mafi and Putnam. Of the three, Meredith has had the worst preseason to be on the chopping block. Meanwhile, Mafi has had issues in pass protection but has been impressive in the running game, and Putnam’s been the opposite. Edge (5) Previously: Starters: Maxx Crosby, Malcolm Koonce Backups: Kwity Paye, Keryon Crawford (R), Cian Slone (R) Cut: Jahfari Harvey, Patrick Johnson On IR: Brennan Jackson Updated: Starters: Maxx Crosby, Kwity Paye Backups: Malcolm Koonce , Keryon Crawford (R), Cian Slone (R) Cut: Jahfari Harvey, Patrick Johnson It’s hard to leave Johnson off the roster with how well he’s played during the preseason. But the rebuilding Raiders aren’t in the business of rostering a 28-year-old who has looked good against backups or linemen on the roster bubble and would be the defense’s fourth edge defender, at best, this season. Maybe he can stick around as one of the vets on the practice squad, or John Spytek can use the veteran defensive end as trade bait. Defensive Tackle (6) Previously: Starters: Tonka Hemingway, Adam Butler Backups: T homas Booker IV , Jonah Laulu, JJ Pegues , Folorunso Fatukasi Cut: Brandon Cleveland (R), Gary Smith II (R), Treven Ma’ae Already Cut: Benito Jones Updated: Starters: Tonka Hemingway, Adam Butler Backups: T homas Booker IV , Jonah Laulu, JJ Pegues , Folorunso Fatukasi Cut: Brandon Cleveland (R), Gary Smith II (R), Treven Ma’ae Defensive tackle is another position that can fall into the “anyone’s guess” category. Fatukasi has only been in camp for about two weeks, signing last Friday, but he was the team’s best run defender in Houston to earn a roster spot. The two rookies—Cleveland and Smith—feel like they’re destined for the practice squad, but it also wouldn’t be surprising to see a surprise here. It’s another spot where an outside hire could be on the table. Linebacker (5) Previously: Starters: Nakobe Dean, Quay Walker Backups: Cody Lindenberg, Tommy Eichenberg, Segun Olubi Cut: Xavian Sorey Jr. (R), Buddy Johnson, Cameron McGrone Updated: Starters: Nakobe Dean, Quay Walker Backups: Cody Lindenberg, Tommy Eichenberg, Segun Olubi Cut: Xavian Sorey Jr. (R), Buddy Johnson, Cameron McGrone I haven’t wavered at linebacker throughout the preseason, primarily because no one has given me a reason to. It seems like everyone in the position group is fulfilling the expectations that were set in front of them to begin camp. The biggest question is whether the coaching staff wants to keep a sixth linebacker for special teams, which is how Johnson could earn a spot. Cornerback (7) Previously: Starters: Eric Stokes, Darien Porter , Taron Johnson Backups: Hezekiah Masses (R), Jermod McCoy (R) , Greedy Vance Cut: Decamerion Richardson, Chigozie Anusiem, Caleb Offord (R),…

title: Folorunso Fatukasi provides hope for Las Vegas Raiders’ run defense in preseason game against Houston Texans
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders’ first two preseason games highlighted a potential problem for the 2026 regular season: the defense struggles to stop the run. The Arizona Cardinals totaled 156 rushing yards and 4.3 yards per carry as a team, while Houston Texans expected second-string running back Woody Marks marched right down the field with four […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - JANUARY 11: Defensive tackle Folorunso Fatukasi #91 of the Houston Texans celebrates after a play during the first half of an AFC Wild Card game against the Los Angeles Chargers, at NRG Stadium on January 11, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders’ first two preseason games highlighted a potential problem for the 2026 regular season: the defense struggles to stop the run. The Arizona Cardinals totaled 156 rushing yards and 4.3 yards per carry as a team, while Houston Texans expected second-string running back Woody Marks marched right down the field with four carries for 37 yards (9.3 ypc) and a touchdown on the opening drive last week. A big reason for that is the Raiders have a significant talent issue at defensive tackle. For example, the team has had 10 defensive tackles record a snap against the run in the preseason and only one has earned a run defense grade from Pro Football Focus above 70: Folorunso “Foley” Fatukasi, who was signed on Aug. 15 and recorded an 81.6 mark just five days later against the Texans. The 31-year-old may not be a part of the long-term plan in Las Vegas, but he provided a glimmer of hope that the team can at least get by for a year with his performance in Houston. Also, The Athletic’s Sam Warren reported on Aug. 23, the Sunday after the Texans game, that Fatukasi was getting reps with the first-team defense. So, let’s flip on the tape and break it down. First thing that stood out about Foley Fatukasi was his get-off; beats the center for a quick win to get a TFL here #Raiders (Sorry if you get motion sickness easily; the Texans were struggling w/ the EZ view last week lol) pic.twitter.com/b1XxOrbjiO — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) August 24, 2026 First, apologies for the shaky camera, especially if you get motion sickness easily. I guess it’s preseason for the Texans’ intern who’s responsible for the end zone camera, too. Or maybe he/she had a few before the game. Anyway, the first aspect of Fatukasi’s game that stood out last Thursday was his get-off. Here, he’s lined up as a shade nose tackle or a 1-technique and gets a great jump on the snap to beat the center, get penetration immediately and use a swim move to defeat the block. So, when the Texans try to run mid zone and attack the weakside b-gap, Fatukasi manages to cut the field in half by forcing the running back to cut backside as the back is getting the ball. That’s where defensive end Patrick Johnson (No. 93), who beats a backside cut-off block from a wide receiver, is waiting for an opportunity to make a tackle for loss. On top of that, the defensive tackle manages to escape from the center just enough to get a hand on the back and help Johnson make the play. Another good get-off for immediate penetration here, though I would like to see Fatukasi play with better pad level and sink his hips to avoid overrunning the play in the backfield. Front-side defenders getting whooped doesn't help either pic.twitter.com/IPsinq8tAV — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) August 24, 2026 This time, Fatukasi is on the backside of an outside zone run but is still lined up as a shade nose and gets another great jump on the snap. With the center working away from him and using a post arm to help the left guard, this isn’t a full-on combo block. However, the defender treats it like one by attacking the center and using his get-off to help split the two linemen, effectively beating the guard’s block and getting penetration into the backfield. Had any of the frontside defenders managed to get off a block or set the edge, Fatukasi would be in a decent position to make a tackle for loss. In other words, he’s cutting the field in half by taking away the cutback lane. That being said, this clip does highlight a concern with the nine-year pro when the competition level rises next month. You might have noticed this on the previous play too; he plays with high pad level and struggles to sink his hips. In this instance, that leads to him overrunning the running back and is part of the reason why he doesn’t make the tackle here. The other part (and the bigger issue, to be honest) is the frontside defenders mentioned above. If Fatukasi drops his butt and works flat down the 40-yard-line after beating the guard on this play, he might be able to save the day and bail out his teammates by making the tackle for a short gain. Again, the first down isn’t his fault, but there is a missed opportunity on what was otherwise a good rep. Foley Fatukasi has "grown man strength" Stays in his gap vs. the combo block and tosses the LT with a hump move to make the tackle #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/ttiOGGgeMZ — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) August 24, 2026 Here, we’ll see some grown-man strength from the well-tenured veteran! Houston comes out in 12 personnel, so Las Vegas matches with base personnel and an odd front for a 3-4 look. With the offense in an unbalanced line by having both tight ends on the same side of the formation, Fatukasi bumps over from his typical nose tackle position and lines up as a 3-technique defensive tackle. However, with the two inside linebackers stepping downhill and being fairly aggressive against the run, Fatukasi plays more like a 4i-technique defensive end by attacking the left tackle’s inside shoulder off the snap. Meanwhile, the Texans run duo, where the left guard and tackle are responsible for combo blocking the 3-technique before working up to the MIKE linebacker (Cody Lindenberg, No. 55). But Fatukasi does a great job of attacking and beating the tackle at the point of attack, and then using a knee drop or corkscrew technique with his inside leg to absorb contact from the guard. All of that allows him to avoid getting washed out of the playside B-gap and maintain control of the block. Now, the defensive tackle does end up getting square and chest-to-chest with the offensive linemen. He could afford to keep his hands tighter to take advantage of his long, over 34-inch arms and stay on an edge to have a better presence in his gap. However, that’s where the impressive strength comes into play to make up for it. Fatukasi perfectly executes a hump move to “close the gap with the man” and force the running back to cut backside. Additionally, he’s able to escape the block and make a tackle for about a one-yard gain. Defensive coordinators can’t ask for more than that from a defensive tackle taking on a combo block. Nice gap-and-a-half technique from Foley Fatukasi Beats the C at the POA, and crosses C's face to take away both A-gaps #Raiders pic.twitter.com/o1lIUr1L1Z — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) August 24, 2026 This is another example of the recent signing’s impressive strength as he effectively executes a gap-and-a-half technique . Fatukasi is back at the shade nose tackle spot where his primary responsibility is the weakside A-gap. Meanwhile, the Texans run halfback dive into the opposite A-gap, which puts the center on a downblock against the one-technique. Post-snap, Fatukasi wins at the point of attack to gain control of the center’s block. He stays in the weakside A-gap initially since that’s his primary responsibility while simultaneously peeking into the backfield to see where the running back is going. Since the defensive tackle has control of the block, he’s able to cross the center’s face and show color in the opposite A-gap, where the play is designed to hit. As a result, the back has to bounce outside and into the edge defender (Johnson, again) for a short gain. While Fatukasi doesn’t make the tackle here, he’s the difference between this being a roughly three-yard run and an explosive gain up the middle because there was a lot of open field down the right hashmarks with the linebacker getting sealed outside by the right guard. Of course, it was only one preseason game where he primarily played against the Texans’ backups. However, given the lack of talent the Raiders have at defensive tackle and that…

summary: One more preseason game for players trying to make the roster to make one last impression. The coaches probably know who they are going to release and add to the practice squad already. Maybe one last game will sway them in their tough decisions? Much of the discussion now is about JJ McCarthy and his […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: J.J. McCarthy #9 of the Minnesota Vikings looks to pass the ball against the Baltimore Ravens during the first quarter of the preseason game at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images One more preseason game for players trying to make the roster to make one last impression. The coaches probably know who they are going to release and add to the practice squad already. Maybe one last game will sway them in their tough decisions? Much of the discussion now is about JJ McCarthy and his potential depth chart position. There are even some reports out there now speculating that JJ may not even make the team. I think the original idiotic idea came from Florio and then it got aggregated by all the rest of the “writers” out there. If the team flat out releases him they have to take another 3.775M dead money cap hit on his already existing 5.96M cap hit. They would get that back in additional 2027 cap space though. If they are able to trade him then they would save an additional 2.781M in cap space this year and 3.775M in 2027. I am not sure there is another team that is going to give anything significant for JJ right now mainly because it is so close to the start of the season. He would be going to a new team having to learn a new system on the fly. I would be very surprised if the team moved him now but stranger things have happened. I think there is too much over analysis on every mistake he makes. It has to be tough for him to see all this social media stuff out there about himself. He can try to avoid it but it likely is impossible. I do not know what is going to happen due to his contract situation but the team does not have to do anything but continue to develop him and guide him on his journey. The NFL is unpredictable and we never know what will happen. KOC joined this podcast last year that explains his thought process a little when it comes to evaluating QBs during training camp. Kevin O’Connell tells Vikings QBs he doesn't care if they throw interceptions in training camp “There are so many things in society, not even just football nowadays, where we want to decide in a moment this guy can or can’t, this guy’s a success or failure. And it’s just not in… pic.twitter.com/YaZIFmtyYv — Josh Chambers (@JoshChambers) August 26, 2026 “There’s not enough time in the day for me to explain all the reasons why you’re wrong. We’re going to go into the quarterback room, we’re going to watch it, and we’re going to get better tomorrow,” he said. This last sentence is the key for those folks who look at practice reps and think they know who is “winning” the competition. The message that KOC gives to his QBs is to be aggressive in practices and he does not care about interceptions. He wants to use these situations as opportunities for growth IMHO. Minnesota Vikings News and Links Kevin O’Connell on J.J. McCarthy, Injury Updates, Final Preseason Game, Standout Players in Training Camp & More https://www.vikings.com/video/kevin-o-connell-on-j-j-mccarthy-injury-updates-final-preseason-game-standout-players-in-training-camp-more JJ McCarthy Predicted to Depart Vikings After Latest Development https://heavy.com/sports/nfl/minnesota-vikings/jj-mccarthy-cut-trade-carson-wentz-backup-qb/ One month ago, JJ McCarthy was embroiled in a battle for the Minnesota Vikings‘ starting quarterback job. One week from now, he could be unemployed and hunting a new team. So went a take from Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk after McCarthy and Carson Wentz split QB2 reps at practice on Tuesday, August 25. “With Max Brosmer also on the roster, McCarthy could be in danger of not being on the roster by Sunday, when the rosters reduce to 53,” Florio wrote. “The Vikings undoubtedly would try to trade him, since the balance of his 2026 pay ($1.075 million) and all of his 2027 compensation ($3.775 million) are fully guaranteed. The Vikings may have to pay a significant chunk of the money in order to facilitate a deal.” But with a thin trade market for quarterbacks because of relative health at the position around the league, there is a chance Minnesota might not find any takers for McCarthy if the franchise attempts to move him. The Indianapolis Colts haven’t been able to find a suitor for Anthony Richardson, a former No. 4 overall pick, since allowing him to seek a trade partner beginning at the NFL Combine in late February. Meanwhile, 2025 third-round selection Dillon Gabriel is a cut candidate for the Cleveland Browns heading into just his second year. “Ultimately, the Vikings may have to simply waive McCarthy,” Florio continued. “However it plays out, it’s not looking good for McCarthy in Minnesota. It will be interesting to see whether and to what extent McCarthy plays in the preseason finale against the [Denver] Broncos.” … Meanwhile, Wentz has outplayed McCarthy this preseason. He also arguably put together a better five-game stretch as the Vikings’ starter in 2025 between Weeks 3-7 while McCarthy was sidelined with a high-ankle sprain than McCarthy did across his 10 starts over the course of the campaign. … “We’ll see how these next couple weeks play out, and we’re gonna do what’s best for our team,” O’Connell said. J.J. McCarthy Gets Clear Assessment Amid Vikings Uncertainty https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/j-j-mccarthy-gets-clear-074917891.html Amid an uncertain future in Minnesota, former NFL QB Matt Leinart gave a blunt assessment of McCarthy’s outlook. “You get in there [and] you don’t have maybe the guys around you [and] you don’t play extremely well; you only get one or two opportunities in this league, and then you’re done,” Leinart said during an Aug. 26 appearance on “The Dan Patrick Show.” “They bring in a guy like Kyler Murray. I’m assuming Carson Wentz might be the backup, right? J.J. McCarthy might not be on the team. Big picture, I think it’s an opportunity for him to take a step back and understand, ‘Hey, this is where I need to get better, learn and grow.'” Moreover, Leinart stressed how much of a jump it is for a QB to go from college to the NFL. “I just think in this day and age, a lot of these guys are playing so much football,” Leinart added. “They’re so productive from high school to college and the system and all that. But I’m telling you, man, the NFL is a different game. It is just different. “You can’t practice the speed. You can’t practice the mental part of it. And these kids get thrown in there, especially a kid like J.J. McCarthy, who I covered at Michigan. I think he’s a really good player. I think he’s got a shot.” Leinart also isn’t placing the blame on the QB, noting that franchises can put players in positions where they can’t succeed. title: 2026 NFC North Season Forecast: Chicago Bears
summary: The start of the NFL regular season is just around the corner and it’s time for season predictions. I’ll start with the Minnesota Vikings’ division rivals and end with the Vikings season forecast in early September. As I have the last couple years, I’ll go through the key areas that can lead to changes from […]
full_text: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) speaks to head coach Ben Johnson during Family Fest at Soldier Field on Aug. 3, 2025, in Chicago. (Eileen T. Meslar/Chicago Tribune/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) The start of the NFL regular season is just around the corner and it’s time for season predictions. I’ll start with the Minnesota Vikings’ division rivals and end with the Vikings season forecast in early September. As I have the last couple years, I’ll go through the key areas that can lead to changes from the previous season. Namely coaching and roster changes, injury and luck factors, and strength of schedule. Up first among the Vikings’ division rivals: the Chicago Bears. Chicago Bears 2025 Season and Offseason Changes The Bears won the NFC North division last season in unconvincing fashion. They finished the season 11-6 after an 0-2 start with a last place schedule and having gone 2-4 in division games- splitting the series with each division rival except being swept by the Lions. They finished the season with a top ten offense and bottom ten defense in both points, yards, and DVOA . Their net point differential was +26, which was third lowest among playoff teams and tied for 15th overall. If those stats lead you to believe that the Bears won a lot of close games to finish 11-6, you are correct- they did. Seven of their eleven wins were one-score games and thirteen total (wins and losses) including the playoffs. But in terms of the just the regular season, the Bears post-game expected win total , based on what happened during each game and considering luck factors, was just 8.8 wins- just over two fewer than their actual win total. An example of a team winning a game they weren’t expected to win based on what happened during the game is the Vikings victory over the Bills a few years ago with Jefferson’s iconic catch on 4th and 18 or whatever it was and Josh Allen fumbling the snap on the goal line. Neither is something likely to happen more often than not so while it was a game the Vikings won, it was also a game they would not be expected to win given the events of the game and the likelihood of them reoccurring that way (i.e. how many times out of 100 would Josh Allen fumble the snap at their one-yard line late in the game and the Vikings recover?). The reason for the Bears success last season, and why they outperformed expectations, was largely due to turnovers. The Bears defense, while ranking 23rd in points allowed and 29th in yards allowed, also ranked 1st in takeaways. They had 33 takeaways last season- the same number the Vikings had in 2024. They also had the fewest giveaways offensively of any team last year, committing just 11 turnovers all season. And so while the Bears allowed more yards per play (6.0) than they gained (5.7), turnovers helped tilt results in their direction. But while the Bears may not have won the division in convincing fashion, new head coach Ben Johnson and his staff deserve a ton of credit for turning things around for the Bears, who hadn’t had a winning season since 2018. Like Dan Campbell in Detroit, Ben Johnson has turned around a losing culture in Chicago and along with Caleb Williams is giving the Bears hope that the team is in good hands and the best is yet to come. Offseason Changes The Bears have some welcome continuity this year among the coaching staff, as head coach and de facto offensive coordinator Ben Johnson returns (although Press Taylor replaces Declan Doyle with the OC title) and Dennis Allen returns as defensive coordinator. That should help each side gain more scheme mastery although defensively there have been a number of roster changes. Defensively, the Bears moved on from safeties Jaquan Brisker and Kevin Byard and cornerback Nanshon Wright. Those three played just about every snap defensively for the Bears and accounted for 15 of their 33 takeaways. They also moved on from linebacker Tremaine Edmunds, who played about 90% of snaps last season. The good news for the Bears is that they brought in some good replacements for Brisker and Byard in Coby Bryant and first-round pick Dillon Thieneman. The bad news is that Bryant will miss most or all of the season with a knee injury, which means new addition Xavier Woods, a one-time Viking now 31, will be starting alongside rookie Thieneman at safety. The Bears are elevating 2023 second-round pick Tyrique Stevenson to replace Wright at cornerback opposite Jaylon Johnson (2nd-team All-Pro in 2023). 2022 second-round pick Kyle Gordon, who missed most of last season, returns as slot corner although he has a calf-injury that may delay his return. At linebacker, the Bears are replacing Edmunds with Devin Bush, who put together a couple good seasons with the Browns after failing to live up to his #10 overall draft pick status with the Steelers and a one-year stint with the Seahawks. The Bears opted for continuity along the defensive line, however. The problem with that is the Bears defensive line ranked 26th last season according to PFF, with only edge rusher Montez Sweat grading above 70 (72.4). Both defensive tackles Grady Jarrett and Gervon Dexter Jr. and edge rusher Dayo Odeyingbo graded in the mid-50s. The Bears ranked 29th last season in net yards allowed per rush (5.0) and ranked 23rd in pressure rate (28.1%). So, while there will be some new starters for the Bears this season defensively, they may not represent improvement overall. Having Jaylon Johnson healthy all season, and Kyle Gordon eventually too, may help, but it’s difficult to see much roster improvement overall for the Bears defensively. Offensively, the Bears moved on from D.J. Moore and will effectively replace him with Luther Burden III, who by most accounts could have a breakout season. Moore was something of a disappointment for the Bears last season, as was Rome Odunze, who the Bears are hoping will live up to his #9 overall pick status at some point. The Bears also added former Lion Kalif Raymond as a slot receiver. Along the offensive line, the Bears dealt with the surprise retirement of starting center Drew Dalman by acquiring former Viking Garrett Bradbury, which represents a downgrade. The Bears are hoping left tackle Ozzy Trapilo is able to return sooner rather than later (he tore his patellar tendon in the playoffs) but may miss the first month or so as he ramps up after his recovery. He was recently taken off the PUP list but may start the season on IR which would mean he misses the first four games of the season. Braxton Jones is the backup and has been less reliable. The Bears are solid with Darnell Wright at right tackle, and future Hall of Famer Joe Thuney at left guard (although he turns 34 later this year), and Jonah Jackson has been fine at right guard. Bradbury has his limitations, as Vikings fans know, but otherwise the Bears offensive line should be pretty solid once Trapilo returns. The Bears also return tight end Colston Loveland, who is proving to be one of the best tight ends in the league, and D’Andre Swift, who had his best season last year. But how well the Bears offense does this season will depend largely on whether quarterback Caleb Williams is able to take another step forward. Williams has shown the off-schedule ability for which he was drafted #1 overall in 2024 and culminated last season in his improbable hail mary to force overtime against the Rams in the playoffs. But it’s his ability to do the more routine on-schedule tasks that has been lacking. He was the least accurate starting quarterback in the league last season by adjusted completion percentage (69.4%) which was lower than even J.J. McCarthy. PFF charted nearly 1 in 4 of Williams’ passes (24.3%) last season as inaccurate and uncatchable, which ranked 40th of 43 quarterbacks charted. Inconsistent mechanics are a part of the problem. And he also continues to hold the ball and revert to lower percentage off-schedule stuff- although with some spectacular mixed in. The issue…

title: 10 Patriots to watch in preseason finale vs. Browns
summary: The New England Patriots wrap up their preseason Thursday night in Cleveland as they take on the Browns. After sitting out of the first two preseason games, Drake Maye and the Patriots top regulars are again currently not expected to suit up with health a priority entering the season. “I do not think we have […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Nick DeGennaro #23 of the New England Patriots celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the second half of the preseason game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots wrap up their preseason Thursday night in Cleveland as they take on the Browns. After sitting out of the first two preseason games, Drake Maye and the Patriots top regulars are again currently not expected to suit up with health a priority entering the season. “I do not think we have a very deep team, so I think we have to make sure that we are preparing our football team and that we are doing everything that we can to keep our best players available,“ head coach Mike Vrabel said following Saturday’s preseason contest. As for who we will be watching closely with cutdown day on the horizon, here are 10 players on our radar. Running back: Hassan Haskins The injuries continued to pile up in the Patriots’ running back room this week, as Lan Larison and Jam Miller were in and out of practice before TreVeyon Henderson suffered a foot/ankle injury Monday. While Larison returned Tuesday in a red non-contact jersey and Miller remained very limited, the duo’s availability for Thursday night is unknown. That could lead to a heavy workload for Hassan Haskins, who may already be the in-house favorite for the RB3 job. Wide receiver: UDFAs The Patriots likely don’t need to see much more from second-year wide receivers Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III. While the team may use Thursday night as an opportunity to simply get them more reps, the duo has long appeared locked onto the roster — a standing that was seemingly solidified by the Kayshon Boutte trade this week. New England will now need to decide which wide receivers stick around on the practice squad after losing John Jiles, who was released, and Jeremiah Webb, who landed on injured reserve, from last year’s unit. Nick DeGennaro appears to be the leading candidate after a strong summer that included catching the game-winning touchdown last week. Cameron Dorner has also shown an ability to create separation and generate explosive plays, while Kyle Dixon’s size gives him an intriguing tool to bring to the practice squad. Tight end: Tanner Arkin A strong start to the summer has slowed down for undrafted tight end Tanner Arkin. In his fairness, Arkin has taken on fullback duties in game action, but he has continued to struggle as a lead blocker. It would be good to see more of Arkin blocking in-line Thursday night — a strength of his game at Illinois — as the Patriots look to fill the void left by free-agent addition Julian Hill. Offensive line: Caleb Lomu It’s been an inconsistent summer for first-round pick Caleb Lomu. The rookie has continued to cross-train at both tackle spots but has struggled in preseason action, particularly when it comes to handling line games and overextending himself into blocks. Coming to New England from Utah’s RPO-heavy scheme is a significant adjustment for the 28th overall pick, which is why many believed he would be best suited to begin his rookie season on the bench. Lomu will look to end his preseason on a high note in Cleveland, but that may be where things are trending. We’ll also highlight fellow rookie tackle Dametrious Crownover, who has impressed with his ability to generate push in the run game. The sixth rounder remains a bit raw in pass pro, but his size and physical tools may not be worth exposing to waivers. Edge rusher: Gabe Jacas and Q Hutchins In a similar fashion to first-round pick Caleb Lomu, inconsistencies have also followed second-round pick Gabe Jacas. While things started to pick up midway through the summer, the game is still moving quickly for Jacas after missing the entire spring and start of training camp. The coaching staff remains high on the rookie due to his raw power and physicality, but he still has a ways to go. “When you come in at this time — didn’t have the spring — we do a lot on defense, right, and so you get a young player like that, we’re just getting them lined up,” outside linebackers coach Mike Smith said. “Getting them lined up, know the defense, do your job, be in the right position. When he starts mastering that now you got to start working [on everything else].” Fellow rookie rusher Q Hutchins, meanwhile, has stacked days late in camp after ending preseason game No. 2 with a strip sack. Hutchins brings a speed element to New England’s edge room that nobody else possesses and will look to continue his push for a 53-man roster spot with a strong preseason finale. Linebacker: Namdi Obiazor Mike Vrabel’s comments about depth issues resonate at linebacker, where neither veteran K.J. Britt nor Chad Muma, nor any of the younger options, has truly ascended the depth chart. Undrafted free agent Khalil Jacobs was impressive before suffering an injury last week, which opens the door for sixth-round pick Namdi Obiazor to see extensive time in Cleveland. Obiazor has been a core special teams player this offseason, which could also open the door to a roster spot. Cornerback: Kindle Vildor and Karon Prunty Charles Woods’ usage this summer and absence from preseason games have appeared to position him as the fourth cornerback on the depth chart. Behind him, veteran Kindle Vildor and rookie Karon Prunty have established themselves as the next-best options and will look to build off strong preseason performances against the Eagles. But is there a spot on the roster for both in a cornerback room that already features Christian Gonzalez, Marcus Jones, Carlton Davis and Woods? Punter: Matt Haack The Patriots signed Haack this week following an injury to starting punter Bryce Baringer. It’s unclear whether Baringer’s injury will force him to miss the start of the regular season or if Haack will be called upon in Week 1. If so, Thursday night will give the 32-year-old lefty his first opportunity to punt in live action for the Patriots as he continues to acclimate to the team.
