full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - JANUARY 22: New General Manager Mike Borgonzi of the Tennessee Titans reacts during an introductory press conference at Ascension Saint Thomas Sports Park on January 22, 2025 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the biggest and most underrated position battles at Tennessee Titans training camp has happened at swing tackle. It was a position of concern before practice began and remains a worry-area heading into 53-man roster cuts this weekend. It seems that sophomore undrafted free agent Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson is winning the job. The Titans signed veteran tackle Austin Deculus in free agency . Fans immediately pointed out that he was terrible for the Los Angeles Chargers last season. Unsurprisingly, Deculus has been really bad in camp and throughout the preseason, and may not make Mike Borgonzi’s 53-man roster. Cutting Deculus would leave Crenshaw-Dickson as the lone swing tackle behind starters Dan Moore Jr. and JC Latham. Crenshaw-Dickson has performed admirably throughout the preseason, heading into this weekend’s finale. Meanwhile, Deculus has been demoted after failing to meet expectations. Crenshaw-Dickson did not play a single meaningful snap for the Titans as a rookie. Trusting the former Florida Gators standout to be the team’s No. 3 tackle requires a massive leap of faith. The Titans may not have a better alternative. Oli Udoh was a stellar swing tackle for the Titans last season. He signed with the Arizona Cardinals in free agency and the Titans have seemingly gotten worse at that crucial position . It’s imperative that both Moore and Latham stay healthy this season. Any other outcome could totally sink the offense, if we’re being honest. Borgonzi could attempt to search through 53-man roster cuts for an upgrade. You don’t find quality tackles on the waiver wire, but the Titans’ situation is so dire that an upgrade may be out there. There may also be opportunities for trades (late-round pick swap) this weekend as roster cuts begin transpiring. Borgonzi should be attentive to all opportunities. Crenshaw-Dickson might be the Titans’ swing tackle in 2026.

title: Washington Commanders roster: Three potential trade candidates
summary: Commanders general manager Adam Peters won’t sleep much throughout this weekend. There’s an initial 53-man roster to form and a practice squad to construct, plus a waiver wire to scour for pieces that can help Washington as the 2026 regular season kicks off.   We previously mentioned the prospect of trading for an experienced reserve center, […]
full_text: Commanders general manager Adam Peters won’t sleep much throughout this weekend. There’s an initial 53-man roster to form and a practice squad to construct, plus a waiver wire to scour for pieces that can help Washington as the 2026 regular season kicks off. We previously mentioned the prospect of trading for an experienced reserve center , maybe someone losing a position battle who has more of a chance to contribute in Washington. Peters could secure a coveted player before he hits the open market with some Day 3 NFL draft capital. The Commanders need to pick up players, but they could also deal from positions of strength. While player-for-player deals are relatively rare in the NFL, Peters could acquire some assets or fortify weaknesses in trade. Washington has some tough choices ahead at receiver and linebacker especially, possibly with players who will get picked up on the waiver wire after getting cut. Understand that you’ve got to give up something to get something, which is why this list is short and the players on it must be attractive additions to another team. Here are a few options Peters could flip for an asset. WR Dyami Brown Dyami Brown has had a strong camp, especially of late, yet sits squarely on the roster bubble in a deep receiver group. The Stefon Diggs signing changed this position group, bumping those seemingly competing for prominent roles deeper on the depth chart. Return ability is a factor here as well, which is why Jaylin Lane and (to a lesser extent) Luke McCaffrey seem safe. That puts Brown and Treylon Burks in a bout for the No. 6 receiver spot – keeping seven doesn’t seem likely – and could make one of them a trade target. Brown could fetch a bit more considering his speed and consistent availability, and Burks is a big-play option who provides injury protection and a big-body in the pattern. Washington could trade Brown and be okay. LB Jordan Magee Jordan Magee seems set to make the 53-man roster as a solid reserve behind Sonny Styles, Frankie Luvu and Leo Chenal. The Commanders also have Kain Medrano and Ale Kaho, athletic linebackers and special teams contributors who have played well this preseason yet sit on the roster bubble. While Magee has dealt with shoulder problems during camp, he might be more attractive as a solid backup. Washington could survive with Medrano and Kaho if they moved Magee, but the return would have to be fair. EDGE Dorance Armstrong This seems more like a trade deadline deal prospect than something before the season, with Dorance Armstrong coming off a torn ACL while facing a one-game suspension to start the season. The Commanders have received solid early returns from rookie Joshua Josephs – he’s definitely still developing – and Javontae Jean-Baptiste. Amstrong is an excellent depth piece with tons of experience and injury protection at a premium position, but he’s in a contract year and might be deemed a valuable trade asset closer to the deadline after he has proven productive coming off of injury. Still, sometimes you must give something valuable to get something. Who else would you trade prior to final cuts for a center or to accumulate future draft capital? Let us know in the comments below.

title: ‘He’s ready’: Jayden Daniels, Commanders confident in 2026 season prep
summary: Jayden Daniels will take three game snaps during the Commanders preseason. That’s a statement of absolute fact despite the fact we’ve got a full four quarters coming up on Friday night.   Snowball’s chance in H-E-double-hockey-sticks Washington’s franchise quarterback plays the exhibition finale against the Ravens.   He got tons of work in Wednesday’s joint […]
full_text: Jayden Daniels will take three game snaps during the Commanders preseason. That’s a statement of absolute fact despite the fact we’ve got a full four quarters coming up on Friday night. Snowball’s chance in H-E-double-hockey-sticks Washington’s franchise quarterback plays the exhibition finale against the Ravens . He got tons of work in Wednesday’s joint practice against the Ravens . Same can be said for the joint practice versus Miami a few weeks back, and several recent practices shaded towards starters. Daniels has been awesome by most all on-site accounts, with his accuracy and vocal leadership lauded at every turn. But that one preseason three-and-out in Detroit stands as his only live game action since Dec. 7, 2025, when an elbow injury ended his season early. That’s clearly enough for the Commanders. Exposing him to unnecessary injury risk wasn’t worth any more work. The team’s logic is sound, considering Daniels is borderline essential to Commanders victory. The play-in-the-preseason hardliners will erupt should anything go wrong in that Week 1 affair in Philadelphia, but a few more exhibition snaps don’t have a profound impact on what happens when the games actually count. Daniels lobbied for the importance of joint-practice reps especially after Wednesday’s Commanders-Ravens practice, and his rationale makes sense. “I took a lot of reps today,” Daniels told on-site reporters in his press conference . “That’s good, to go up here and see different looks. In the games, you don’t really see exotic looks. We got some good work on third downs, on first and second downs, working against a coordinator like this and a team like this, it gave us good work. … We’re getting ready to play ball. We’ll be ready when that time comes.” The preparation has been solid, from offseason work with Commanders receivers through Wednesday, the last reps he’ll take in the preseason. “I threw a good camp,” Daniels said. “I think I can still get better and work on things, but I took each and every day and didn’t take (anything) for granted. I love football and I had it taken away from me for some time last year and dealt with some different things. I have an appreciation for being able to be healthy and on the field practicing and getting better as a player.” The Commanders stuck to their plan for Daniels, even when that first-team series versus Detroit got cut ever so short . They loaded practice reps onto his plate over the last week especially, trying to get him as much work as possible in a semi-controlled environment. Quinn still dealt with the customary questions about Daniels’ preseason workload, especially with coordinator David Blough installing a new offense, but the justification for limiting it never changed. That was the case on Wednesday, when he summed up Daniels’ summertime work. “He has taken a lot of practice reps already,“ Quinn said in a pre-practice presser . ”Anytime we can challenge him, he’s always up for it. To have different matchups, different defenses, different looks. It’s valuable. It’s valuable in that sense the most. But this guy, he’s ready to play football.” While the preseason’s over for Daniels and most impact starters, the work isn’t over. Washington has more than a fortnight, a quasi-bye and then a standard game week before that Eagles clash. Daniels will use every second to prep for a crucial season in Washington. “We have to keep building, keep growing,” Daniels said. “You’re not winning a Super Bowl right now. You’re not playing for a Super Bowl right now. You’re playing for the division. The first game matters on September 13 and you try to get better every day and build reps over time. Hopefully you’re playing your best football at the end of the season.”

summary: The Daily Slop – 27 August 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. full_text: The Daily Slop – 27 August 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles The Athletic (paywall) Commanders’ Jayden Daniels, offense struggle against Ravens: ‘Not the best day’ What was likely the last live play of Jayden Daniels’ preseason showed exactly why there’s explosive potential in every Washington Commanders snap. Yes, two Baltimore Ravens bore down on Washington’s third-year quarterback. So off his back foot, Daniels let the ball fly. In a corner of the end zone 30-some yards downfield, rookie Antonio Williams caught it in stride. To be clear, it was Daniels who made the play possible. And when he did, the Commanders poured off their sideline at the Ravens’ complex, where the two teams concluded a joint practice session Wednesday in advance of Friday night’s final preseason game in Baltimore. There was a celebration of what Daniels can do at any point, which is to cover up inconsistency and sloppy execution by others with his extraordinary talent. Still, the closing play couldn’t erase an erratic and largely unproductive day for the Commanders’ offense. Washington is already dealing with a long-term injury to star left tackle Laremy Tunsil and a calf issue that has kept starting center Nick Allegretti out for most of camp. On Wednesday, Sam Cosmi, the starting right guard, didn’t participate because of an illness. That left Daniels with a group that featured a lot of sixth-round rookie Matt Gulbin and a little of Julian Good-Jones at center, and a right guard rotation with Good-Jones and undrafted rookie Tanoa Togiai. So outside of a few completions to receiver Terry McLaurin, a couple of scrambles by Daniels and the long toss to Williams, Washington struggled to move the ball. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE NFL.com Jayden Daniels ‘to learn from’ joint practice after Commanders’ offense struggles vs. Ravens Entering training camp, the biggest question marks in Washington centered on how the Commanders might deepen their receiving corps beyond star Terry McLaurin, and whether their remade defense could improve upon its last-place finish in 2025. After injuries to left tackle Laremy Tunsil and center Nick Allegretti, the greatest concern now exists in the trenches. There isn’t yet a timetable for Allegretti’s return yet, and Tunsil will miss most, if not all of the regular season after suffering a torn triceps earlier this month. It’s becoming increasingly likely Washington’s starting five could include a player (or two) who isn’t currently on the roster. That’s a problem for general manager Adam Peters to solve. Daniels, meanwhile, can only work on improving his own performance and building a rapport with the teammates who are currently taking the field with him. “Own this. Watch the tape. Take the coaching,” Daniels said when asked how the Commanders might learn from their tough day. “Be coachable to be able to move forward from this. The good thing about it is it’s August whatever, I don’t know what day it is, but it’s August whatever. Our first game is September 13th. That’s the one that really matters.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) What we learned at Commanders training camp about the defense, O-line and Jayden Daniels The tightest roster race is at receiver There was a time not too long ago when Washington sorely needed help at receiver. That changed (at least on paper) with the addition of Stefon Diggs . The four-time Pro Bowler agreed to a one-year deal with the Commanders earlier this month, giving them a needed “No. 2” behind Terry McLaurin. It also created some tough decisions for Peters and Quinn. Rookie Antonio Williams is a lock to make the roster, which leaves eight players — Treylon Burks, Luke McCaffrey, Dyami Brown, Jaylin Lane, Van Jefferson, Jaden Bradley, Nick Nash and Jacoby Jones — vying for the last three or four receiver spots. There’s a plan for the linebackers [T]he coaching staff is clearly preparing to weaponize Styles — who hasn’t blitzed in his limited appearances in games — once the regular season begins. “You’d say he could play man-to-man because of the speed,” Quinn added. “But I’d also say the zone parts of his game are gonna be exceptional because he has quickness as well as speed. Sometimes you might see a person who’s fast, but they have to build up to it. Whereas he’s got initial quickness to get to a certain location, and that’s a big deal.” On Wednesday, backup linebacker Kain Medrano also made an impact — picking off one pass and breaking up another. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Last Man Standig (paywall) ‘That’s how you win five games’: Commanders get a reality check from Ravens Missing starters and makeshift lineups mattered. So did the blocking, mistakes and slow start that had Jeremy Reaves invoking last season’s 5-12 record, and Jayden Daniels offering context. The Washington Commanders offense committed countless infractions in Wednesday’s joint practice: porous blocking, particularly in the middle of the line. Wayward snaps. False starts. Drops. Passes deflected at the line of scrimmage. Baltimore’s defense won the day. Washington’s suspect showing helped produce the outcome. [C]ontext matters. In this case, it matters plenty. We must note the missing bodies on both sides of the ball — especially in the trenches. Starting right guard Sam Cosmi (illness) became a late addition to the already lengthy injury report that includes center Nick Allegretti and front-seven defenders Daron Payne, Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson. Some of these players and others may return next week. The real panic comes if any are involved in Sunday’s cutdown-day transactions — meaning an injured reserve designation — though head coach Dan Quinn said before practice he doesn’t anticipate such events. And yet, for a team looking to significantly improve on a dismal 5-12 season, the effort lagged in a practice that will be the last time many players take the field before the roster goes from 90 to 53. “Everybody’s tired at this point of the year. Everybody’s body is hurting this training camp,” Reaves said. “You’re not supposed to feel good. But, you know, that’s how we started this. That’s how you win five games. And we got to be better. We got to be WAY better.” For more from Ben Standig, click here Sports Illustrated The Good and Not So Good From Commanders vs. Ravens Joint Practice Washington may not have owned most of the practice, but they certainly owned the ending. Baltimore moved into the red zone during the final two-minute period before Sainristil went up and intercepted Jackson, ending what looked like a scoring drive. The offense then got its opportunity and faced fourth down against an all-out Ravens blitz. Daniels stood in with pressure coming and found Williams downfield for a touchdown. It was a strong response from a team that had spent plenty of the day fighting through adversity. Washington’s pass rush didn’t have nearly the same type of success against Jackson that it did during the joint practice against Miami. Missing Oweh and Chaisson obviously matters, and Jackson presents a challenge unlike almost anybody else at the position, but the starting defense struggled to consistently affect him. The backups found more success once Tyler Huntley entered, but Washington would certainly like to see more pressure from the group surrounding its top edge rushers when those guys aren’t available. Daniels said afterward that it “wasn’t the best day we could have had,” and that’s probably the easiest way to describe Wednesday. Baltimore exposed some things Washington still needs to clean up, particularly along the offensive line, which is exactly why Quinn wanted this type of practice before the regular season. full_text: Darius Rush has not done much up to this point in his NFL career. A fifth-round selection of the Indianapolis Colts, Rush profiled with elite athletic measurables coming into the 2023 NFL Draft but so far has limited production at the professional level. However, as a converted wide receiver, Rush was incredibly raw as a defensive back in college and only played in 43 games at South Carolina, starting 21 over the course of four seasons with the Gamecocks. After being selected by the Colts, he was waived and cycled through the Chiefs (twice), Steelers, and Browns. Rush’s first NFL snaps didn’t come until November of his rookie season. He performed fairly well while logging 39 defensive snaps over two games. Unfortunately, he was relegated to strictly special teams work by Pittsburgh in 2024, before being released at final roster cuts in August 2025. He was signed to the Commanders’ practice squad and spent the majority of the season there, until he was elevated to the active roster in Week 15 versus the New York Giants. While Rush failed to record any stats, he did play on special teams. The team quietly signed him to a reserve/future contract in January 2026. While none of this may excite you, consider the following in comparison to Fabian Moreau and Antonio Hamilton Sr., who are 32 and 33 years old, respectively, and are popularly being included on current projections for the Washington Commanders’ initial 53-man roster. Rush is 26 years old and a self-described “ special teams demon. ” Commanders special teams coordinator Larry Izzo loves speed on his special teams units, and Rush’s 4.36 40-yard dash is a perfect match. Rush cut his teeth at South Carolina as a contributor on teams and was the primary gunner, recording 74 tackles over four seasons. This summer, Rush has focused his efforts there and caught the attention of analysts and reporters, first in training camp and then in both preseason games. Drove his blocker into the kick returner, resulting in a tackle. Has been running with the 1st coverage units. Numbers game at CB, but has ST value for sure. — John Keim (@john_keim) August 23, 2026 Rush had four tackles in the 17-13 loss at Detroit as well a some nice moments in coverage . He also shined in offseason-program activities, with a pick-six off of Athan Kaliakmanis to close out minicamp. The cornerback is still developing in coverage but profiles as a good fit in a zone scheme while having some skills in man coverage, bringing the versatility coordinator Daronte Jones covets. Great read and close by Darius Rush who intercepted QB Athan Kaliakmanis for a pick six in the flat. — David Harrison (@DHarrison82) June 18, 2026 Two red zone opportunities for rookie Ja'Kobi Lane. Two incompletions. pic.twitter.com/avY8MY5zLc — Sam Cohn (@samdcohn) August 26, 2026 In his Tuesday presser , head coach Dan Quinn talked about the importance of special teams for the Commanders, calling them “critical” to roster decisions. The retirement of Nick Bellore this summer, and elevation of Jeremy Reaves and Tyler Owens to more prominent defensive roles, means there is an opening for a special teams ace on the roster. Rush has been stating his case for the role, but will need a strong final preseason game to secure a spot. He will be one to watch in Friday’s game versus the Baltimore Ravens. If Rush can put together another good performance, he should be a player fans consider when making their final roster projections before Sunday’s 6 p.m. ET deadline.

title: Washington Commanders Mason/Brennan Preseason Hype! Power Rankings: Week 3
summary: Heading into the final preseason game, there has been a massive shakeup of the Mason/Brennan Preseason Hype! Award power rankings, compared to where they stood just one week ago. Last week’s leader, Drew Stevens now seems firmly entrenched as the Commanders’ kicker for the season.  The Week 1 breakout star plummeted down the board after […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - AUGUST 22: Kaytron Allen #31 of the Washington Commanders runs with the ball during the first quarter of a preseason game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on August 22, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images Heading into the final preseason game, there has been a massive shakeup of the Mason/Brennan Preseason Hype! Award power rankings, compared to where they stood just one week ago . Last week’s leader, Drew Stevens now seems firmly entrenched as the Commanders’ kicker for the season. The Week 1 breakout star plummeted down the board after a Dud performance in Week 2. A new player has taken the lead, giving rise to a position battle that no one expected. The battle for the WR6 position has intensified, with a new name making a meteoric rise up the board into the top 5. One of the Mason/Brennan hopefuls has become the top ranked player at his position in the preseason. And my favorite dark horse contestant has been released. While other Mason/Brennan weekly rankings appeal to popular opinion, the Bris Vegas Preseason Hype! Power Rankings © harness the power of proprietary advanced hype metrics to give you the most scientifically accurate account of where the contestants stand in the battle for Hogs Haven’s most coveted preseason award. But before we get to this week’s power rankings, I would like to acknowledge the most hype-worthy play of Week 2 by a Mason/Brennan contest alumnus: Tyler Owens has been everywhere this offeason. Great in space. pic.twitter.com/wpvrNCJ5OU — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) August 22, 2026 The Commanders took a flyer on Owens with a UDFA contract after the 2024 draft. The enigmatic prospect out of Texas Tech, with freakish measurables and little college experience stood out in his first training camp and earned himself a position on the final 53. In his first two seasons he became a core special teamer. In 2026 he has been making the case for a bigger role on defense with splash plays, like this obliteration of a Lions’ running back. Owens provides an example of the power of preseason hype to propel roster hopefuls to NFL success. Now, let’s see how the battle for the Mason/Brennan Preseason Hype! Award is shaping up following the second preseason game. Graduated K Drew Stevens Stevens won the kicking competition last week, and became the only kicker on the roster. There is no indication that the Commanders plan to bring in competition for him before the season opener. Since his hype has converted into reality, he is no longer a viable Mason/Brennan contestant. Preseason Hype! – Week 3 Power Rankings 1. QB Athan Kaliakmanis, +3 AK-16 has had a meteoric rise up the board over the past two weeks, ascending from 17 th place in the offseason rankings to claim first place heading into the final preseason game. Entering camp, the Commanders’ 7 th round pick was realistically battling Sam Hartman for the third-string QB role. That competition was effectively settled when Kaliakmanis’ attacked the Lions’ defense with surgical precision on Saturday, completing 11/14 (78.6%) for 162 yards at an ADOT of 9.4 yds for a 114.9 passer rating. He looked clearly superior to Hartman, who had a slightly higher completion rate (81.8%) on shorter targets (ADOT 5.4 yds). With Hartman in the rearview mirror and Marcus Mariota nursing an MCL sprain, Kaliakmanis could become Jayden Daniels’ primary backup on opening day. 2. WR Jaden “Moss” Bradley, +1 Bradley has been the Cinderella story of the Commanders’ preseason. He was a virtual unknown in the 2026 draft class, despite having a 931 yd, 4 TD breakout season at UNLV. The Commanders’ scouting team must have noticed his impressive receiving ability , and snapped him up as a UDFA. Bradley has taken full advantage of the opportunity, with standout performances in training camp and the first preseason game. He kicked it up a notch by hauling in the catch of the week against the Lions. Jaden Bradley getting arm-barred and still making the one-handed catch! pic.twitter.com/iUCFJd66v3 — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) August 22, 2026 That right there is what it looks like when a UDFA claims a roster spot. And, if that were not enough, he also came in for one special teams snap in punt coverage and recorded a tackle. The kid is going to be a star. 3. RB Kaytron Allen, +2 Allen looked better on Saturday than his 3.0 yards/attempt rushing average would seem to indicate. To put that figure into perspective, you have to appreciate that he averaged -0.9 yards before contact on his 10 rushing attempts. In other words, he was getting hit in the backfield and doing a great job of gaining positive yardage, despite getting little help from his blockers. In his second preseason outing, Allen flashed the ability to create something out of nothing, finding narrow running lanes and breaking tackles to gain the tough yards between the tackles. If the starting offensive line can give him more to work with, he can be the thunder to pair with Bill’s lightning. 4. DT Ricky Barber, +2 Barber built on an impressive outing in Miami with another tough performance against the Lions, to the tune of 1 QB hit, 2 tackles, 3 assists and 2 defensive stops. Is Barber the most underrated player on the Commanders’ defense? Why no. Through 2 preseason games, Barber is PFF’s highest rated defensive lineman ( Defense Grade: 85.2 ; min 50 snaps). Barber has a legitimate shot of making the 53-man roster to replace 2024 second-round pick, Johnny Newton, who is sidelined with a pec injury. Barber has similar burst to shoot gaps and gain leverage. What gives him a potential advantage over Newton is his ability to take on blocks and hold his gap in the running game. When Newton gets back, he might have a fight on his hands. 5. WR Nick Nash, +11 Nothing generates hype in Washington like a big WR with a slow 40 time making a highlight reel catch in a preseason game. Last week I wrote that Nash would need to kick it up a notch to beat out Jacoby Jones for a place on the practice squad. He listened: Nick Nash making plays ‼️ 📺 #WASvsDET @wusa9 pic.twitter.com/Vz5jtyKZis — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) August 22, 2026 Nash led all Commanders’ receivers against the Lions with 62 receiving yards, including that 55 yarder and another 7 yd reception. He was also by far the most productive pass catcher on the team, averaging a superhuman 7.75 Y/RR on just 8 passing plays. Nash is this week’s biggest riser, parlaying his big play ability to jump from last place into the top five. 6. WR Jacoby Jones, +6 The Commanders’ incumbent big practice squad receiver was not content to let some upstart steal his job. Jones had a big day himself, catching 3/3 targets for 37 yds on just 8 passing plays. On most Sunday afternoons, Jones’ 4.63 Y/RR would comfortably lead the team, if not the league. With a practice squad spot on the line, this battle could catch fire in the final preseason game against the Ravens. 7. CB Fred Davis II, +7 Why aren’t we talking more about Fred Davis? Maybe because he’s a cornerback. When he plays well, there is nothing to talk about on his side of the field. Davis has quietly put together a quality body of work in coverage through two preseason games. He hasn’t made any plays on the ball, yet. But he also hasn’t allowed opposing receivers to make plays in his coverage. Through two preseason games, Davis has allowed just 3 targets and 1 reception for 11 yards in 31 coverage snaps, and a 45.1 passer rating when targeted. In the regular season, allowing 0.35 yards/coverage snap against starting QBs and WRs would place Davis in the elite ranks of lockdown CBs. Against second- and third-string players in the preseason it is at least a positive sign of potential. Davis hasn’t generated the hype he deserves yet. But that’s not entirely his fault. I’m moving him up 7 places in the rankings, based on his hype potential, on spec that fans and the media will finally embrace…

title: Adam Peters must be aggressive fixing Commanders center situation
summary: Commanders general manager Adam Peters had a plan for the center position entering the 2026 campaign. It obviously wasn’t good enough.   We’ve seen that play out painfully over the course of this summer, with presumptive starter Nick Allegretti out most of training camp with a calf strain.   Allegretti suffered the injury during Washington’s […]
full_text: Commanders general manager Adam Peters had a plan for the center position entering the 2026 campaign. It obviously wasn’t good enough. We’ve seen that play out painfully over the course of this summer, with presumptive starter Nick Allegretti out most of training camp with a calf strain. Allegretti suffered the injury during Washington’s first training camp practice, way back on July 29 . He returned on Aug. 18, following nearly three weeks on the shelf. Allegretti aggravated the issue a day later and hasn’t returned since. That left reserves Julian Good-Jones and Matt Gulbin to fill a void, and results haven’t been great. Head coach Dan Quinn stuck with Good-Jones as the primary center (with Allegretti out) for weeks, and it didn’t work out well. Then he put Gulbin front and, well, center heading into the preseason’s final week. While this center setup has been messy for a while, it came to a head during Wednesday’s joint practice with the Ravens. On-site reporters generally agreed that the offensive line play was poor, especially at the center spot. It prompted The Athletic reporter Nicki Jhabvala to tweet this: The Commanders need a center. Badly. Still. That is all. — Nicki Jhabvala (@NickiJhabvala) August 26, 2026 And this (with some additional context about the state of Wednesday’s offensive line): To keep in mind about the offense today: As mentioned earlier, Cosmi was out. Jayden Daniels played with a front five that featured a lot of Matt Gulbin at center, some of Julian Good-Jones at center, and mostly Good-Jones and Tanoa Togiai at right guard. https://t.co/CYPhaGaGoj — Nicki Jhabvala (@NickiJhabvala) August 26, 2026 A play documented by the Washington Post ’s Tashan Reed, showed how bad things can get when the center spot’s not right: The #Commanders ' O couldn't get much going during that 11-on-11 red zone drill. The run blocking was subpar and the passing offense also couldn't get into a groove. The lowlight: Matt Gulbin had an errant snap, Jayden Daniels recovered it and threw it right to Kyle Hamilton. — Tashan Reed (@tashanreed) August 26, 2026 We’ve reached an untenable situation at center, which simply must get fixed before the regular season starts. The Allegretti injury exposed a major flaw in Peters’ positional construction. He earmarked Allegretti to take over at center despite him primarily playing guard in the NFL, without protection should injury or ineffectiveness take hold. Good-Jones doesn’t have tons of experience at center entering 2026. Gulbin’s just a sixth-round pick trying to find his way. Where else was Quinn supposed to turn, except to the front office asking for help? There are only so many levers he can pull at this point. It’s low-hanging fruit to relitigate the entire offseason, about why Tyler Biasdaz was released without the need for cap relief or why an outside veteran wasn’t signed once Tyler Linderbaum went to Las Vegas . It’s borderline lunacy to reimagine NFL draft picks in the first round or the third round going to a center over Sonny Styles and Antonio Williams. The Commanders are where they are at the center spot. They need depth at the very least. What is Peters going to do about it? There’s no doubt Peters and his pro scouting department understand the lay of the land when it comes to centers still on the street, including former Lions starter Graham Glasgow . They’ve also got a good idea of who might get cut and what that person’s market value might be. They’ve got salary-cap space to spare, plus a sixth- and seventh-round draft picks should Washington need to grease the wheels to secure the center they want most in trade. It’s hard to imagine landing a true, every-down starter at this point. The Commanders will surely hope their confidence in Allegretti is well placed and that he can play enough catch-up once healthy to be ready and capable on Sept. 13 against Philadelphia. Look, it’s entirely possible Allegretti returns and plays well at center and doesn’t get injured again and all this center consternation is but a blip. There’s reason for doubt, as this training camp showed. That’s why Peters must be aggressive in the marketplace and find an experienced backup and someone with the savvy required to step in and play meaningful snaps. As we’ve seen to this point, the reserves aren’t quite ready. Even dominant showings in Friday’s preseason finale won’t change that. That leaves the offensive line in flux over the next few days, even beyond the initial 53-man roster formation. The offensive line’s in a tough spot and has been since Laremy Tunsil tore his triceps a few weeks back. That moved Brandon Coleman to left tackle and ended his position battle with Chris Paul at left guard. That’s not an overall plus for the starting lineup or the position group’s depth, which must be reconstructed on the fly. This week’s D.J. Humphries signing was a start. It’s not the end. The Commanders need clear help at center and should continue looking for upgrades on the back end of the depth chart as we move forward.

title: 2027 NFL mock draft: Reid's preseason first-round predictions
summary: With the college and NFL seasons about to start, Jordan Reid projected the top 32 picks in next year's draft -- including a blockbuster trade.
full_text:
The 2026 college football season starts this weekend with Week 0, and evaluations for the 2027 NFL draft are already underway. Since releasing my way-too-early mock draft in late April, I've been in the film room dissecting tape while also talking to scouts and evaluators around the league to get an idea on how top prospects are trending. So, let's update those first-round projections with another mock draft.

 This is how I see Round 1 playing out right now . Keep in mind that plenty of changes will shake out between now and next April in Washington, D.C. Players will rise and fall on the board, and some might not even remain in the class. And since we don't know the draft order yet, I used current projections from ESPN's Football Power Index for the 1-32.

 With quarterbacks being such a focal point in this class, I've also projected a trade that would uproot the top of this draft at that position. Let's get this started with that blockbuster deal and then get to predictions for all 32 first-round picks.

 Note: Underclassmen are marked with an asterisk. 

 

 

 Projected trade: Browns move up to No. 1 
 Here, the Browns decide to take fate into their own hands, trading both of their first-round picks (Nos. 4 and 32), a 2027 fourth-round pick and their 2028 second-round pick to the Dolphins for the No. 1 selection. Will Cleveland use it to get its franchise quarterback -- and if so, which one?

 
 

 1. Cleveland Browns  (via projected trade with MIA ) 
 Dante Moore , QB, Oregon* 

 I had the Dolphins trade out because they recently invested in Malik Willis . While a lot depends on Willis' performance this season, Miami does already have a promising young quarterback. Unless  Shedeur Sanders  makes a massive leap in Year 2 ( which seems unlikely ), the Browns do not.  Deshaun Watson 's contract ends after this season, as well, making this a perfect time for Cleveland to take another swing at that elusive franchise QB to join the young talent it has accumulated in the past couple drafts.

 Moore has squeaky-clean mechanics, and his accuracy shined in his first year as a starter. This would be a good situation for him, with young players he can grow alongside. If he brings his stellar college play to the NFL, the Browns could turn things around quickly.

 
 

 2. Arizona Cardinals 
 Arch Manning , QB, Texas* 

 Even though Carson Beck , Arizona's third-round pick in April, has looked good this preseason, his presence wouldn't prevent the Cardinals from looking at a QB here -- especially with veteran Jacoby Brissett 's contract expiring after the season. Manning recovered from a slow start to 2025, with his development taking a big leap in mid-October. If he can build on that momentum and improve his accuracy on underneath throws, he has the physical tools to be picked at this spot and join 2026 first-round running back Jeremiyah Love to form Arizona's backfield of the future.

 
 

 3. New York Jets 
 CJ Carr , QB, Notre Dame* 

 The Jets' drafts in the past five years have seen them bring in bookend offensive tackles ( Olu Fashanu and Armand Membou ), a true WR1 ( Garrett Wilson ), a franchise RB ( Breece Hall ) and two talented tight ends ( Mason Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq ). Seems like an ideal base for a young quarterback to join. Carr's sample size is small (12 career starts), but he thrived last season in his first year as a starter. He's a capable passer who can distribute the ball and does a great job of syncing his feet, eyes and throwing motion. Notre Dame is a prime national title contender in 2026, and if Carr excels on that quest, it's easy to see him rise to this spot of the draft.

 

 
 

 4. Miami Dolphins  (via projected trade with CLE ) 
 Jeremiah Smith , WR, Ohio State* 

 The Dolphins fell three spots via our mock trade and would still be able to get my top-ranked player at a severe position of need. Smith grew up down the road from Hard Rock Stadium and would immediately become Miami's go-to receiver. At 6-foot-3, 225 pounds, he is a physically imposing wideout who glides past defenders and is capable of winning with speed or power. He's the best of Ohio State's recent run of first-round receivers. Not only would he be a massive upgrade from  Malik Washington and Jalen Tolbert , but he would also allow Miami to correctly evaluate QB Malik Willis.

 
 

 5. Las Vegas Raiders 
 Cam Coleman , WR, Texas* 

 The Raiders got their QB1 in April when they picked  Fernando Mendoza ; now they get their true WR1. Coleman is a sleek-built pass catcher who can make acrobatic receptions look routine with his outstanding catch radius. He transferred from Auburn to Texas , and this upcoming season could see his production explode as Arch Manning's featured option. Coleman can run every route on the route tree, so having him join 2024 first-rounder Brock Bowers and 2025 first-rounder Ashton Jeanty  would give Las Vegas a formidable core around Mendoza.

 
 

 6. Tennessee Titans 
 Dylan Stewart , Edge, South Carolina* 

 Even though they picked  Keldric Faulk in Round 1 in April, the Titans could use more edge-rush help, especially with Jermaine Johnson II  entering the final year of his contract. Few edge-rush prospects have ever possessed Stewart's blend of upfield acceleration, bend and closing speed. The production has yet to match the potential, as Stewart had only 4.5 sacks last season, but the 6-foot-5, 250-pounder has rare tools and already has teams giddy about what he could develop into at the NFL level.

 
 

 7. Carolina Panthers 
 Leonard Moore , CB, Notre Dame* 

 With  Mike Jackson set to be a free agent who could cash in elsewhere if he repeats his 2025 performance, the Panthers might have a vacancy at cornerback opposite Jaycee Horn . Adding Moore would give Carolina a dynamic coverage duo, as Moore is one of the best corners I've scouted in some time. He has been exceptional at Notre Dame and had five interceptions last season. His length (6-foot-2, 197 pounds) and fluidity give him potential to be a shutdown cover guy.

 
 

 8. New Orleans Saints 
 Colin Simmons , Edge, Texas* 

 The Saints need edge help in both the short term and long term, as  Chase Young and Carl Granderson  will be free agents in 2028. Simmons would be a major boost to New Orleans' defensive front as the most productive edge rusher in this class. He led the SEC with 12 sacks last season, and the 6-foot-3, 245-pounder is a terror with an unpredictable assortment of pass-rush moves. His combination of power and upfield quickness has him in the argument with Dylan Stewart as the top edge in this draft.

 

 
 

 9. New York Giants 
 Will Echoles , DT, Ole Miss* 

 The Giants traded away star defensive tackle  Dexter Lawrence II  this offseason, creating a gaping hole in their defensive interior. Echoles is the best of a deep defensive tackle crop, as his power and pass-rush push give him a well-rounded skill set. The 6-foot-3, 315-pound Echoles is a stout run defender who is difficult to move off the spot, allowing him to maintain gap control and generate negative plays. He just turned 20 years old earlier this month, giving him tremendous room for growth.

 
 

 10. Washington Commanders 
 Charlie Becker , WR, Indiana* 

 Even though  Stefon Diggs just signed with Washington , he'll be 33 years old and it's unclear if he'll be the Commanders' WR2 past this season. There's still a need for help opposite Terry McLaurin , and the 6-foot-4, 207-pound Becker was the player I enjoyed studying the most this offseason. title: 2026 NFL season: Ranking all 32 teams' watchability, excitement
summary: Which NFL teams are must-watches every Sunday? Ben Solak stacked all 32 by excitement, fun and intrigue, starting with Chicago.
full_text:
The NFL regular season returns in under two weeks, and boy am I excited. NFL RedZone will be up on one screen. My fantasy teams and group chats will overtake my phone. But what about the second screen? Which game gets my undivided attention on the laptop?

 To solve this problem, I've developed a watchability ranking for all 32 NFL teams. It's my second year doing so, and the first year went flawlessly . (I put the Commanders in the top spot; they went 5-12, and all of their most fun players got hurt.)

 Of course, a 5-12 team can still be watchable. Watchable football isn't necessarily winning football. Winning football teams sit on leads. They punt on fourth-and-mediums to play the field-position game. Winning football teams execute. Watchable football teams might do all of those things ... but they also go for that fourth down in the first quarter. They might fail to execute, and in doing so, invite hilarious out-of-script plays that end in either majesty or disaster.

 There are four key things I look for in highly watchable teams. They are as follows:

 
 Big plays . I don't just want points -- I want 'em fast. Teams that can score from anywhere on the field are eminently more watchable than teams that matriculate the football. The whole point of the RedZone channel is to broadcast those predictable scores to everyone at home. If a team is to demand a full screen, that means its touchdowns can come when RedZone isn't watching ... and means its defense can surrender those plays, too. 
 Competitive games . Some teams inherently play closer games than others. They lack the offensive star power to blow out inferior opponents but also have the gritty competitiveness to hang with superior ones. This is what we might call "the Chiefs Rule." Yes, the Chiefs have become boring to watch on offense (because they fail to create explosive plays). However, they have played so many close games over the past few seasons as a function of their careful style, and those games are always fun nail-biters. 
 Star players . It's rare to tune in to a bad team for one good player, but it's possible. You cared about Myles Garrett 's sack race last season, no matter the Browns' record down the stretch. The Cardinals might be a total mess this season, but if Jeremiyah Love looks like an Offensive Rookie of the Year when he totes the rock, we will be seated. That is not a team you'd watch over the Rams or the Lions, but over the other bad teams? For sure. 
 Nothing offensive . Teams with bad offenses or bad defenses can be watchable -- heck, a below-average defense that creates more shootouts can dramatically improve a team's watchability (hello, Chicago Bears ). But teams with dreadful offenses or horrible defenses are unendurable. I quite literally avert my gaze at the sight of them. Bad football is bad football even if it results in explosive gains or competitive games. I'll watch it if I have to in a primetime island game -- but otherwise, I'll pass. 
 
 With the legwork out of the way, here are my 2026 NFL watchability rankings.

 

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 

 1. Chicago Bears 
 There's no way you need me to explain this to you.

 If you watched every Bears game last season, you saw an NFL-leading six comeback wins by quarterback Caleb Williams and Chicago's  ludicrously explosive offense. Such games included a 58-yard  Colston Loveland catch-and-run touchdown in a 47-42 barn burner against the Bengals, a 56-yard kickoff return with less than 50 seconds left to set up a last-second field goal winner against the Vikings and the fourth-and-goal fadeaway touchdown to Jahdae Walker to set up the 50-yard  DJ Moore  lightning bolt against the Packers. You also saw this throw and this throw and this throw . You were well rewarded for your attention.

 

 This season's Bears might not produce as many wild swings, but they still figure to be the most explosive offense in football. Last season's takeaway-happy defense looks poised to give up plenty of yards and points, as well, which should lead to big scoreboards and more opportunities for fun offense. This one is not a hard sell.

 
 

 

 2. Los Angeles Rams 
 Everyone loves watching a "one last job" movie, and everyone will love watching the Rams in 2026. Every season could be the final one for 38-year-old quarterback  Matthew Stafford . Given just how sensational the sunset of his career has been -- an MVP trophy, the no-look throws, the never-say-die fourth-quarter comebacks -- how could you possibly endure missing what might be one of his last 17 games?

 

 And even if you could endure it ... Myles Garrett? On the Rams? Next to Aaron Donald ?! No, Donald hasn't signed yet . And Garrett has now missed 12 training camp practices because of  knee swelling . But this is not a ranking for cold water to be thrown on hype. The Rams in their final realized form -- Stafford, Garrett, Donald, receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams , cornerback Trent McDuffie and coach Sean McVay -- might be one of the most watchable teams in history. They fail to take the top spot only because Donald is not yet on the roster. We wait with bated breath.

 
 
 3. Detroit Lions 
 It's the Jahmyr Gibbs show!

 It's a little tricky to say "tune in for the Lions' offense!" when that has been true for every season since 2022. But you should still tune in. Even in a down season, Detroit was a top-10 unit in offensive DVOA, yards per play, points per drive and EPA per play in 2025 -- all the big metrics. Now that Gibbs (current betting favorite for Offensive Player of the Year) no longer splits time with David Montgomery , there are more chances for electrifying runs from anywhere on the field.

 

 The Lions' appearance on the watchability podium is thanks to their defense, which surrendered a ton of explosive passes in 2025 (13.9% of opponent dropbacks, 25th among league defenses) and is only thinner and slower in the secondary this season with cornerback Terrion Arnold off the team and safeties  Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph still injured. It's going to be big-play central on both sides of the ball during Lions games.

 
 

 4. Los Angeles Chargers 
 If you aren't champing at the bit to see Justin Herbert in the Mike McDaniel offense, then you and I don't like the same football. Few quarterbacks produce more spectacular throws than Herbert, though his career has been plagued by poor offensive design, shaky O-line play and ill-timed drops. Few offensive designers have elevated quarterback play more than McDaniel, who created an explosive downfield passing attack in Miami with Tua Tagovailoa 's below-average arm strength. Now, with a golden-armed shotmaker under center, he isn't even trying to hide his excitement.

 

 

 The Chargers could easily have the coolest offense, with Herbert, McDaniel, speedy running back Keaton Mitchell , second-year running back Omarion Hampton and a healthy No. 1 receiver in Ladd McConkey . Even if the defense takes a step back without Jesse Minter (now the head coach of the Ravens) calling the shots, the Chargers should be better equipped to score fast, score big and win shootouts.

 
 

 5. New England Patriots 
 Everyone knows the Patriots' strength of schedule in 2025 hugely impacted their record, but it also impacted their watchability. It wasn't particularly fun to tune in to Patriots games. They emerged as true AFC contenders across a stretch in which they beat the Saints, Titans, Browns, Falcons, Buccaneers, Jets, Bengals and Giants. Save for the doubleheader against the Bills and a fun fourth-quarter win against the Ravens, quarterback Drake Maye 's breakout year wasn't particularly interesting to watch.

 

 The schedule is tougher in 2026, which makes New England more watchable. The Patriots' first-place schedule sets them…

title: Matt and Mike LaFleur hold joint Cardinals-Packers practice in front of family
summary: The LaFleur family turned up to the joint practice between the Cardinals and Packers on Wednesday.
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- On Monday, Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur said the best way to settle any fights at a joint practice between his team and his brother Mike's Arizona Cardinals would be for the two of them to throw down at midfield .

 Though there were a few scuffles during Wednesday's two-plus-hour practice, that wasn't necessary.

 

 However, their father, Denny, remembered what happened one time when the brothers LaFleur went at it as kids.

 "This guy, me, came out on top," Denny said before practice. "It's not going to happen, but if they did, I still might come out on top. It's a long story, but I will tell you this: We were in close quarters and I had to take care of them."

 Denny wore a combination of Packers and Cardinals colors. He had on a red shirt to represent the Cardinals, and he wore a Packers visor. 

 There was a little trash-talking, especially from Matt.

 "He was more of a pest," Matt said when asked if he and Mike fought as kids. "There's a 7½-year age difference, so picture me at 18: He's 10½, 11, so there was not a lot of fighting going on."

 Matt's wife, Bre, and their two sons were at practice. Mike's wife, Lauren, and their daughter and son were on their way to Green Bay, and they planned to stay at Matt's house.

 And the LaFleur brothers' parents, Denny and Kristi, also were on hand. They live in Green Bay.

title: Josh Allen's got jokes -- some too mischievous to tell
summary: We asked the people who have been on the other side of an Allen joke or prank. Here are their stories.
full_text:
Josh Allen is known for many things. Developing into one of the NFL's star quarterbacks, including earning the 2024 MVP award. Leading the Buffalo Bills to the postseason for the past seven consecutive seasons. Becoming a husband and a father by age 30.

 Another thing Allen is known for? Being a jokester.

 Many of the stories and wisecracks are considered unshareable. The content isn't fit for all audiences.

 When asking Bills teammates, coaches and friends what their favorite funny Allen moment is, long pauses linger as they recall, they smile, and their minds decipher which ones can be spoken out loud.

 

 While no player has more weight on his shoulders than the Bills franchise quarterback leading a team that hasn't been to the Super Bowl since 1993, Allen puts a priority on arriving to work with a smile every day. The 30-year-old's love of jokes, banter and pranks play a role in building a culture that has permeated through Buffalo's ranks.

 However, the nine-year veteran tends to keep his playful side behind the scenes. But to those within the Bills organization, that jovial part of Allen is an important component to what makes him an effective leader.

 "He's MVP, Josh Allen, best quarterback in the world. You don't expect him to just be a down-to-earth guy's guy that loves jokes and pranks and [has an] incredible sense of humor," Bills coach Joe Brady said in an interview with ESPN. "He's literally just one of the guys. If you didn't know who he was and you met him in public, you'd be like, 'This guy's awesome. I'm sure he's just a normal guy with a normal family,' and nothing about him or his personality would say superstar or any type of pride."

 We asked the people who have been on the other side of an Allen joke or prank. Here are their stories ahead of the Bills' final 2026 preseason game hosting the Pittsburgh Steelers (7 p.m. ET, NFL Network).

 

 

 Want an Allen rookie card? Just ask Knox 

 In Allen's second season in the league in 2019, he wasn't above pulling a bit of a prank on a player who was only slightly less seasoned.

 Tight end Dawson Knox , who was a 2019 third-round pick by the Bills, arrived in the locker room one day to a disgruntling revelation. About 100 of Allen's rookie trading cards were hidden in every crevice of Knox's locker. Everything from his wallet to the bottom of his cleats had an Allen trading card sticking out and staring him in the face.

 "It was funny. I was just so confused," Knox said. "And he's just looking around the corner and waiting for me to realize what's going on, just laughing his butt off."

 The location of one of the QB's 2018 rookie cards inside his cleats, however, was found a bit too late.

 "One of them I didn't even realize till I was out at practice, and I had to take my shoe off, take it out," Knox recalled.

 The card that was taped to the back plate of Knox's shoulder pads remains to this day. Someone called out the card to Knox in recent years, inquiring what the value of the card is now.

 The tight end has about four left in his locker.

 "I'm gonna have to have him sign one for me personally," Knox said.

 

 From flying footballs to packing peanuts: 'Got you!' 

 Making an impression on rookies is a specialty of Allen's.

 In 2024, during running back Ray Davis ' rookie season, the Bills quarterback pulled one of his "classic" moves. Allen made it seem like a ball was coming toward Davis and Allen during a practice, yelling, "Ooooo" to get out of the way. So, Davis moved.

 "I jump out the way and [Allen] goes, 'Got you!'" Davis said. There was no ball headed their way.

 Getting to see Allen's goofy personality catches some rookies off guard.

 "I got here and I thought he was going to be stern," Davis said. "And then, I was like, 'Yo, he's just a big 'ole kid.' So, that's a good thing."

 A personal favorite of offensive lineman Alec Anderson is when cornerback Kaiir Elam , the Bills' 2022 first-round pick, received a surprise in his car one day.

 Packing peanuts. Everywhere.

 During one Bills practice, Allen had the custodial staff put what Anderson estimated as "100,000 packing peanuts," in Elam's truck. When Elam opened the truck, they all came pouring out.

 

 

 'Wait, are you serious right now?' 

 While countless plays have documented Allen's abilities over his pro career, every now and then, there's time for a joking moment during a game.

 "If we're on the sideline, there's times where he'll be able to keep it light," Knox said. "'Mr. Brightside' [a song played during Bills home games for the past couple years] comes on, he's dancing around with us, and it kind of depends on the game, too."

 Sometimes, it's the little things in practice.

 Second-year cornerback Maxwell Hairston noticed in organized team activities (OTAs) that if Allen completes a pass with Hairston defending, Allen makes a gun out of his hand and acts like he is pulling a trigger to indicate a spot-on play.

 So, now if Hairston gets a stop in practice, he does the move right back.

 For opponents, Allen's playful moves can be subtle.

 Pass rusher Bradley Chubb , who was drafted the same year as Allen in 2018 and signed a three-year deal with Buffalo in March, said that when he would play against Allen, the QB would wink or do something else small toward defenders. 

 So how will Allen react with Chubb not lining up against him as an opponent?'

 "Him joking? Every day. Nonstop," Chubb said. "It's one of those things, like, sometimes you're like, 'Wait, are you serious right now?' And then he just start busting out laughing. So, yeah, it's dope to see somebody with that much talent, that much weight on his shoulders, just kind of be lighthearted and taking every day day-by-day."

  

 

 Knowing when to joke and when to be serious 

 Brady has prioritized trying to think what is best for players when designing the team's schedule and planning practices. He noted that he encourages player feedback and tries to explain the "why" behind his choices in team meetings.

 But no one, he says, has a better pulse and understanding of a locker room than Allen. And a significant part of that is his ability to adapt his personality.

 "Sometimes people think he's a jokester," Brady said. "He jokes when he feels like guys are uptight. He jokes to keep a guy loose. But when he knows, 'Hey, we're too loose,' he's the guy that can be serious. And it's so unique."

 When Brady, as Buffalo's quarterbacks coach, first met Allen in 2022, the veteran made quite the impression on his coach. A few minutes into the meeting, Brady recalls Allen "got me on an unprofessional joke." 

 Looking back, Brady appreciates what Allen was trying to do.

 "He knew that, 'Hey bro, just because I'm Josh Allen, loosen up,' and it was good for me," Brady said. "And so, I sometimes can tell his demeanor and based off his demeanor, how he actually perceives the locker room."

 Now in their fifth season together, Brady knows not to respond right away if Allen asks him a question out of the blue -- that has become a common indicator that the quarterback is trying to lull people into a joke.

 

 Flight delay? 

 Brady changed a Bills practice schedule during OTAs this past spring.

 Just ahead of Memorial Day weekend, practice was pushed back.

 Brady, however, knew that Allen had weekend travel plans that the quarterback had been looking forward to. 

 Of course, OTAs are voluntary, so Allen deciding to leave early to stick to his original travel plans was a possibility. But the quarterback stayed and didn't comment on the timing.

 Allen left soon after practice, so Brady shot him a text.

 "''Hey, everything good, just making sure you got on the flight and everything,'" Brady said, recalling his text.

 

 Allen's response as Brady remembers:

 "'No, obviously, we didn't make it, so I think we'll probably just go up to Toronto for the weekend or something like that.'''

title: Panthers' waiver wire watch: 3 biggest areas of need
summary: With the cut-down deadline Sunday, Carolina could look to make claims for potential upgrades at the bottom of the roster.
full_text:
As Sunday's NFL cut-down deadline (6 p.m. ET) looms, the Carolina Panthers will get one last look at the bottom of their roster against the Houston Texans on Friday at Bank of America Stadium ( 7 p.m. ET ). And while the front office and coaching staff are preparing for an exodus of players this weekend as NFL teams trim down to 53 players, Carolina should also be scouting film to find potential gems on the waiver wire next week.

 Nearly every team in the league will cut NFL roster-worthy talent. The players who haven't earned vested veteran status (four or more accrued seasons) will be subject to waivers. From there, teams can make their claims for other squads' departing talent.

 

 That's an opportunity for Panthers general manager Dan Morgan and his front office to search preseason film to find fits and improve the depth chart. Over the past two offseasons under Morgan, Carolina has claimed eight total players -- six in 2024 and two in 2025 -- off the waiver wire following the cut-down deadline.

 The Panthers are in the middle of the waiver wire pecking order (No. 19), but they still should be able to make claims for potential upgrades at the bottom of the roster. The three biggest positions of need -- inside linebacker, guard and defensive line -- have been glaring throughout training camp and the preseason. Let's break down the three along with potential roster-improving scenarios:

 
 Inside linebacker 
 Projected starters: Devin Lloyd , Trevin Wallace / Claudin Cherelus 
 Preseason depth: Bam Martin-Scott , Jackson Kuwatch , Maema Njongmeta , Mapalo Mwansa 

 The Panthers have staged a competition opposite Lloyd throughout the summer. Unfortunately for Carolina, neither Wallace (a 2024 third-round pick) nor Cherelus (a longtime backup and special teams standout) has separated himself in the battle. Coach Dave Canales acknowledged as much Monday, stating the pair is "head-to-head ... and it's like neck-and-neck" heading into the final week of the preseason.

 Wallace, according to NFL Next Gen Stats, has played 62 snaps in the first three preseason games. He has allowed three catches for 14 yards on three targets while producing seven tackles and a QB pressure. Conversely, Cherelus has collected nine tackles in 65 preseason snaps, while allowing opponents to catch all six of his coverage targets for 52 yards.

 Behind the competing pair, Martin-Scott and Kuwatch have flashed potential as long-term developmental players. Neither appears to be in the discussion for a starting role, but if Wallace or Cherelus fails to take advantage of the challenge those two are facing, the Panthers might need to look elsewhere to complement Lloyd.

 While the waiver wire is known more for depth opportunities, the Panthers could look to upgrade over their current crop of competitors. Inside linebacker is not considered a premium position by most teams, and the Panthers might need to pounce if a scheme fit hits the wire.

 If not, they could look to the trade market to pair a better player with Lloyd.

 

 
 Guard 
 Projected starters: Damien Lewis (LG) and Robert Hunt (RG) 
 Preseason depth: Brady Christensen , Jake Curhan , Chandler Zavala , Isaia Glass ,  Ja'Tyre Carter 

 Lewis and Hunt make up one of the league's better guard tandems, but the current roster behind them leaves quite a bit to be desired. And because both starters have had notable injury histories, getting some quality insurance is paramount for a 17-game season.

 Zavala, a 2023 fourth-round pick, has struggled in pass protection, giving up three QB pressures -- including two sacks -- in 43 preseason pass-blocking snaps, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Christensen, who is coming off Achilles surgery, has also given up three QB pressures in 39 pass sets. Curhan, a versatile lineman, has a history with the staff and the team, but there's reason to believe he can be upgraded on the roster, given he waited until earlier this month to be re-signed out of free agency.

 Linemen, particularly guards, tend to flood the waiver wire after the cut deadline. Perhaps the Panthers can find a better fit from elsewhere. And after the way the line was dominated by the Texans' defense Wednesday in joint practice, the urgency to add new talent to the group feels palpable.

 
 Defensive line 
 Projected starters: Derrick Brown (DE), Cam Jackson (NT), Bobby Brown III (DE) 
 Preseason depth: Lee Hunter , Jared Harrison-Hunte , Aaron Hall , Elijah Garcia , Kyon Barrs , Tywone Malone Jr .,  Parker Petersen 

 

 Similar to the Panthers' outlook on their guard depth chart, Carolina could afford to enhance the group along the defensive line. With Turk Wharton (neck) on the physically unable to perform list, the proven talent within the trenches is minimal.

 Derrick Brown is a Pro Bowl-worthy player, but there are still questions about Bobby Brown's effectiveness. Jackson and Hunter are recent draft picks who have flashed big-time potential this summer, but they won't be able to prove their worth until the regular season begins. The same could be said for Harrison-Hunte and Hall, who have three and five QB pressures in the preseason, respectively, according to NFL Next Gen Stats.

 So, Morgan might need to push for upgrades on the wire or through a trade. He has routinely discussed his desire to continuously improve both sides of the line throughout his tenure, and the wire could be his opportunity to plug some depth holes in both areas.

title: 2026 Carolina Panthers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our updates from Panthers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Panthers writer Mike Kaye will have the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Panthers camp. Will QB Bryce Young and the Panthers take another step forward after making the playoffs in 2025? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Panthers' top camp performer and biggest lingering question.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 Wednesday, Aug. 26 
 Dave Canales couldn't spin his offense's performance Wednesday following joint practice between the Carolina Panthers and Houston Texans in Charlotte.

 They were dominated.

 The coach knew it. His players knew it. And the Texans did enough celebrating after several defensive stops to make sure everyone else knew it as well.

 

 "They were better than us today," Canales said.

 Five-time Pro Bowl defensive end Danielle Hunter lived in the backfield throughout the joint workout. He got to quarterback Bryce Young on at least five occasions for would-be sacks. Fellow pass rusher  Will Anderson Jr . got to Young a couple of times, too, and forced regular pressure.

 Young was hurried on the bulk of his dropbacks, which led to throws on the run to mixed results. Texans defensive back Calen Bullock picked Young off twice, once off an ill-advised throw and once off a ricochet ball that bounced off wide receiver Jalen Coker 's hands. Young also sailed a couple of balls off the mark to open receivers as he tried to make off-platform throws.

 Left tackle Rasheed Walker and rookie right tackle Monroe Freeling seemed to be overmatched throughout the majority of practice.

 "Danielle Hunter, Will Anderson ... those guys are fantastic players," Canales said. "That's exactly what we need to see. Monroe needs it. Rasheed needs it. When we dropped back today, we couldn't really do much, other than Bryce extending and getting a couple of plays going. The rush was phenomenal, and that's exactly the information we need to be able to regroup. The run game was fine."

 Wednesday's results aside, Canales said he's excited about what the offense has been able to do in camp. He's looking forward to what the unit can do with its scheme and various wrinkles. He's also excited about Young's connection with Coker and Tetairoa McMillan in the passing game.

 "Today didn't show that," Canales said. "Today there were some flashes of some nice throws and catches, but that was a good group today. Again, I try not to take it all in a microcosm, but if we want to be good, we have to be able to play against teams like this."

 Canales said after practice that the starters won't play against the Texans in the preseason finale on Friday ( 7 p.m. ET ) at Bank of America Stadium. The Panthers coach said the starters got roughly 75% of the reps in the joint practice, which he felt was enough work to move into the regular-season preparation process.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Wide receiver Ja'seem Reed , who made a nice catch off a Kenny Pickett deep ball in team drills, worked on the Jugs machine more than 35 minutes after practice. 
 Pickett threw a pair of impressive touchdown passes to wide receivers John Metchie III and Jimmy Horn Jr . during 11-on-11 work. Both throws split two defenders, and Texans defensive back George Odum ended both plays with loud hits on the receivers. Metchie's score was a perfectly placed ball in the corner of the end zone, while Horn's grab was the final play of practice and came on a leaping play. 
 Depth offensive lineman Ryan Hayes sustained an undisclosed injury in the middle of practice. 
 Following the workout, Young and Anderson -- a pair of 2024 top-three picks and former Alabama teammates -- sat on the field and caught up for several minutes by themselves before Metchie -- another Alabama alum -- visited with them. 
 Linebacker Devin Lloyd (knee) and wide receiver Xavier Legette (foot) didn't participate in the practice. Neither did cornerback Will Lee III , who had been dealing with a groin injury but practiced on Monday. 
 

 
 Monday, Aug. 24 

 The Panthers won't see wide receiver Xavier Legette again in the preseason. He also won't take part in joint practice against the Houston Texans on Wednesday as he will wear a walking boot on his right foot through Thursday, according to coach Dave Canales .

 Rookie quarterback Haynes King (hamstring) will also be sidelined through the week as well, Canales said. King, like running back Chuba Hubbard (hamstring), is targeting a post-cut-deadline return to the field.

 Tight end Darren Waller , who made his practice debut on Monday, will probably be held out of Friday's preseason finale. The recent addition will be peppered into team drills -- similar to his work to begin the week -- against the visiting AFC South squad.

 The Panthers will cut their roster from 91 players -- including an international exemption -- to 53 players by 6 p.m. on Sunday. Check out our Panthers' 53-man roster projection from Monday morning.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Safety Lathan Ransom (undisclosed) and nose tackle Cam Jackson (concussion protocol) practiced in red non-contact jerseys. 
 Cornerbacks Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans , wide receiver Ja'seem Reed , outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips all returned to practice after missing last week's matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars due to minor injuries. 
 Linebacker Devin Lloyd (knee) was held out of practice after dealing with soreness following joint practice with the Jaguars on Wednesday. Per Canales, the team doesn't view the injury as something major, but he did undergo treatment. 
 Tight end Feleipe Franks made an excellent over-the-shoulder catch for a big gain off a throw from depth QB Kyle Trask in 11-on-11 drills. 
 Veteran offensive lineman Brady Christensen took some tackle reps on Monday after spending most of the summer at guard. 
 Rookie safety Zakee Wheatley picked off starting QB Bryce Young in 7-on-7 work. 
 Cornerback Corey Thornton ended practice on a diving pick off a throw from backup QB Kenny Pickett . 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 19 
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- As Jaguars tight ends Brenton Strange and Nate Boerkircher made life difficult for the Panthers' defense Wednesday in joint practice, quarterback Bryce Young and wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan had some fun of their own on the opposite field.
 Young and McMillan were nearly automatic in foreign territory outside of EverBank Stadium. The quarterback heaved the ball down the field for his top target and McMillan routinely made him look good.

 The fireworks started with Young tossing a beautiful strike to McMillan as he beat cornerback Jabbar Muhammad to the end zone in 11-on-11 drills. A little while later, Young hit McMillan on a crossing route in front of defenders at the tip of the goal line for a contested touchdown grab.

 Finally, Young lifted a ball toward the end zone, about 25 yards, for McMillan, who jumped up to snag the ball over two defensive backs for a third touchdown.

 

 More observations: 

 
 The following players were sidelined during the joint practice: RB  Chuba Hubbard  (hamstring), NT Cam Jackson (concussion protocol), WR Ja'seem Reed (calf), CB Akayleb Evans (undisclosed), QB Haynes King (hamstring), CB  Will Lee III  (groin) and TE Darren Waller (onboarding). 
 Outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips and wide receiver Xavier Legette were pulled early from drills as a precaution due to minor injuries, according to coach Dave Canales. Phillips told the staff he was fine after hurting his wrist, while the team's medical staff cleared Legette after he got rolled up on in team drills. 
 Tight ends…
